Recall that the \emph{Kullback-Leibler divergence} of two probability measures $P_1, P_2$ on some measurable space $(\Omega,\mathcal{A})$ is given by $\mathrm{KL}(P_1,P_2) := \int_{\Omega}\log (\frac{\mathrm{d}P_1}{\mathrm{d}P_2} )\;\mathrm{d}P_1$ 
if $P_1$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $P_2$, and $+\infty$ otherwise. 

To apply Theorem 20 of \cite{fischer2020sobolev} on the measurable space $\Omega = (\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}\times\mathbb{R})^{n}$, we construct a family of probability measures $P_0, P_1, \dots, P_M$ over $(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}\times\mathbb{R})$ that share the same marginal distribution over $(Z,O)$ but different conditional distributions $P_{Y\mid Z, O}$. Our strategy follows the construction in \citet{chen2011rate} and can be explained as follows. We fix a marginal probability measure $P_{ZO}$ over $\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O}$. We then propose a family of conditional probability measures $P_{i; Y\mid Z,O}$ indexed by $f_i \in \mathfrak{F}$ for $0\leq i\leq M$. Since $f_i$'s are functions on $\mathcal{X}\times \mathcal{O}$, we fix a marginal probability measure $P_X$ on $\mathcal{X}$ under the constraint that $X$ is independent of $O$. Then, we define a smooth copula to parametrize the dependence between $P_{X}$ and $P_{Z}$, which fully specifies $P_{X\mid Z,O}$. This induces a fixed conditional expectation operator $T : L^2(P_{XO})\to L^2(P_{ZO})$. We then specify $P_{i; Y\mid Z,O}$ for $0\leq i\leq M$ via the following equation:
\begin{align*}
    Y\mid Z = \mathbf z, O = \mathbf o \sim \mathcal{N}((Tf_{i})(\mathbf z, \mathbf o), \sigma^2),
\end{align*}
for a fixed $\sigma>0$, and for any $(\mathbf z,\mathbf o)\in \mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O}$. $P_i$ denotes the probability measure on $\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O}\times \mathbb{R}$ by coupling $P_{i;Y\mid Z,O}$ and $P_{ZO}$. In the above construction, we require $P_{X\mid Z,O}$ to satisfy \Cref{assn: technical}, and all $f_i$'s to satisfy \Cref{ass:f_ast}, namely $f_i\in \mathfrak{S}$. 

Concretely, we fix $P_{ZO}$ to be the Lebesgue measure over $\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O}$. Without loss of generality, we take $\mathcal{X} = [-0.5, 0.5]^{d_x}$ rather than $[0,1]^{d_x}$.  By working with a symmetric domain, we exploit the fact that even functions have real-valued Fourier transforms, which simplify our subsequent calculations. We fix $P_{X}$ via the density function
\begin{talign} p_X(\mathbf x)\propto \prod_{i=1}^{d_x} g_i(x_i), \quad g_i(x_i) := \exp\left(-\frac{2}{1 - 4x_i^2}\right) \mathbbm{1}_{x_i \in [-0.5, 0.5]},
\end{talign}
where each $g_i$ is a smooth, compactly supported \emph{bump function}. We fix an arbitrary smooth copula~\citep{nelsen2006introduction}, such that $P_{X\mid Z,O}$ satisfies \Cref{assn: technical} and $T$ satisfies \Cref{ass:T_contractivity} with parameter $\eta_1>0$. 

The main technical challenge of the minimax lower bound is the construction of the function class $\mathfrak{F}$ whose each element $f_i$ induces a conditional distribution $P_{X\mid Z, O}$.
Our goal is to design $\mathfrak{F}$ so that it satisfies three desirable properties: 1) we want $\mathfrak{F}\in B_{2,\infty}^{s_x,s_o}(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})$ as per \Cref{ass:f_ast}. 
2) we want the size of $\mathfrak{F}$ to be large to enable the application of \citet[Theorem 20]{fischer2020sobolev}. 
3) we want all elements of $\mathfrak{F}$ to exhibit high partial Fourier frequency such that after applying $T$, the resulting functions become difficult to distinguish. 
This increases the intrinsic difficulty of the problem and yields a tighter lower bound. 
The construction of such a function class satisfying the first two properties is standard and can be achieved using anisotropic B-splines~\citep{ibragimov1984asymptotic, suzuki2021deep,schmidt2020nonparametric}. 
However, the third property poses a challenge: the Fourier transform of B-splines has full support. 
Consequently, conventional B-splines cannot enforce the desired partial high-frequency restriction. To address this limitation, we convolve the B-splines with a high frequency bandpass filter in the $X$-direction. 
Since convolution acts as a smoothing operator, the function class constructed with such modified B-splines remains in the Besov space. 

To start with, we introduce the definition of anisotropic B-splines~\citep{leisner_nonlinear_wavelet_approximation_2003}. 


\begin{defi}[Anisotropic B-spline \citep{leisner_nonlinear_wavelet_approximation_2003}] The cardinal B-spline of order $\mathfrak{m}\in \mathbb{N}$ is defined as the repeated $\mathfrak{m}$ times convolution $\iota_{\mathfrak{m}} = \iota_{0}\ast \dots \ast \iota_0$ where $\iota_0$ is the indicator function $\mathbbm{1}_{[0,1]}$. Let $d$ denote the ambient dimension, and let $\boldsymbol{s} = (s_1,\dots, s_d)$ denote a smoothness vector. Define the notation $\underline{s} = \min(s_1,\dots,s_{d})$ and $s_i^\prime := \frac{\underline{s}}{s_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq d$.  The (anisotropic) B-spline  of order $\mathfrak{m}$ with resolution $\mathfrak{K} \in \mathbb{N}_+$ and location vector $ {\boldsymbol\ell} \in  \prod_{i=1}^{d}\{-\mathfrak{m},-\mathfrak{m}+1,\dots, 2^{\left\lfloor \mathfrak{K} s_i^\prime \right\rfloor} \}$ is defined as $M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}}(\mathbf x) = \prod_{i=1}^{d} \iota_{\mathfrak{m}} (2^{\lfloor \mathfrak{K} s_i^\prime \rfloor}x_i - \ell_i)$.
\end{defi}
\noindent

Let $\mathfrak{m} > s_x \vee s_o$ be a non-negative even integer. 
The resolution $\mathfrak{K} = \mathfrak{K}(n)$ is defined later in Eq.~\eqref{eq:choice_k_lb}, such that $\mathfrak{K} \to \infty$ as $n\to\infty$. 
The B-spline basis in the $O$-direction follows the standard construction. Define the set of location vectors $\mathcal{L}_O$ and the associated B-splines
\begin{talign} \mathcal{L}_O := \left\{ 2 \mathfrak{m} \mathbb{N}\cap \left\{0, \dots, 2^{\left\lfloor \mathfrak{K}\frac{\underline{s}}{s_o}\right\rfloor}\right\}\right\}^{d_o} , \quad M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}(\mathbf o) = \prod_{j=1}^{d_o}\iota_{\mathfrak{m}}\left(2^{\left\lfloor \frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}\right\rfloor} o_j - \ell_{o,j}\right).
\end{talign}
Note that here we enforce all location vectors to be a multiple of $2\mathfrak{m}$ such that the $\{M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\}_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o\in\mathcal{L}_O}$ have disjoint supports, which will simplify the calculations later on. 
In contrast, the basis functions in the $X$-direction are constructed by convolving a standard B-spline $M_{0,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}$ on $X$ with the inverse Fourier transform of the indicator function $\mathbbm{1}_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_x}$, for ${\boldsymbol\ell}_x \in \mathcal{L}_X$:  
\begin{talign} \mathcal{L}_X &:= \left\{0,1,\dots, \left\lfloor \frac{0.8\pi}{\zeta}2^{\mathfrak{K}\frac{\underline{s}}{s_x}}\right\rfloor\right\}^{d_x} , \quad \Omega_{\mathfrak{K}{\boldsymbol\ell}_x}(\mathbf x) := \left(M_{0, -\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\ast \mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_x}]\right)\left(2^{\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_x}}\mathbf x\right) . 
\end{talign}
where $\mathbbm{1}_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_x}$ is the indicator function over the following hyper-rectangle: 
\begin{align} I_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_x} := \bigtimes_{j=1}^{d_x}\left[1.1\pi + \zeta \ell_{x,j}2^{-\mathfrak{K}\frac{\underline{s}}{s_x}}, 1.1\pi + (\zeta \ell_{x,j} + 1)2^{-\mathfrak{K}\frac{\underline{s}}{s_x}}\right]. 
\end{align}
$\zeta>0$ is a width hyperparameter that determines the spacing of different hyper-rectangles; its value will be specified later.
For sufficiently large $n\geq 1$, since $\ell_{x,j} \leq \frac{0.8\pi}{\zeta}2^{\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_x}}$, we know that $ 1.1\pi + (\zeta \ell_{x,j} + 1)2^{-\mathfrak{K}\frac{\underline{s}}{s_x}} \leq 1.9\pi + 2^{-\mathfrak{K}\frac{\underline{s}}{s_x}} \leq 1.95\pi$. Thus we have $I_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_x}\subseteq [1.1\pi, 1.95\pi]^{d_x}$. 

The main consequence of this construction is revealed via the convolution theorem~\citep[Theorem 9.2]{rudin1987real}, which gives
\begin{align} \mathcal{F}[\Omega_{\mathfrak{K}{\boldsymbol\ell}_x}](\boldsymbol{\omega}_x) = \mathcal{F}[M_{\mathfrak{K},-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}](\boldsymbol{\omega}_x) \cdot \mathbbm{1}_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_x}(2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_x}}\boldsymbol{\omega}_x).
\end{align}
As a result, we have that $\mathrm{supp}(\mathcal{F}[\Omega_{\mathfrak{K}{\boldsymbol\ell}_x}])= 2^{\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_x}} \cdot I_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_x} \subseteq [\pi 2^{\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_x}}, 2\pi 2^{\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_x}}]^{d_x}$. Since $\mathfrak{K} \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, the construction guarantees that $\Omega_{\mathfrak{K}{\boldsymbol\ell}_x}$ only has high-frequency spectrum, thereby fulfilling the third desirable property for $\mathfrak{F}$. 


\begin{figure}
\vspace{-10pt}
    \centering
    \includegraphics[width=0.65\linewidth]{include/Figures/frequency_masking_two_zeta.pdf}
    \vspace{-5pt}
    \caption{
    This figure illustrates the partial Fourier transform of $f_{\mathbf v}$ in Eq.~\eqref{eq:mathfrak_F}, where we take $d_x = 1$, $\mathfrak{K} = 2$, $\mathfrak{m} = 4$, $s_x = \underline{s} \leq s_o$.  
    The dashed blue line represents the Fourier transform of the B-spline $M_{\mathfrak{K},-2}$. 
    The red line shows the result of applying frequency masks to this B-spline: $\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_x}\beta_{\mathbf v({\boldsymbol\ell}_x,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o)} \mathcal{F}[M_{\mathfrak{K},-2}](\omega_x) \cdot \mathbbm{1}_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_x}(2^{-\mathfrak{K}}\omega_x)$. The Fourier transform of $f_{\mathbf v}(\cdot, \mathbf o)$ is equal to this result up to scaling factors dependent only on $\mathbf o$. 
    } \vspace{-15pt}
\end{figure}



Define the basis $\Omega_{\mathfrak{K}({\boldsymbol\ell}_x,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}(\mathbf x,\mathbf o) := \Omega_{\mathfrak{K}{\boldsymbol\ell}_x}(\mathbf x) \cdot M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}(\mathbf o)$ and the set of all location vectors $\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_X\times\mathcal{L}_O$. 
We have $|\mathcal{L}| \asymp \zeta^{-d_x}2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}(\frac{d_x}{s_x} + \frac{d_o}{s_o})}$. 
We construct a function class $\mathfrak{F}$ as follows:
\begin{talign} \mathfrak{F}:= \left\{f_{\mathbf v}: f_{\mathbf v}(\mathbf x,\mathbf o) =  2^{-\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}\left(1 - \frac{d_x}{2s_x}\right)} \sum_{({\boldsymbol\ell}_x,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o)\in \mathcal{L}} \beta_{\mathbf v({\boldsymbol\ell}_x,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}\Omega_{\mathfrak{K}({\boldsymbol\ell}_x,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}(\mathbf x,\mathbf o)\,\middle\vert\,  \mathbf v\in \{0,1\}^{|\mathcal{L}|}\right\},
\end{talign}
where $\beta_{\mathbf v({\boldsymbol\ell}_x,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}\in\{0,1\}$ is the value assigned by $\mathbf v\in \{0,1\}^{|\mathcal{L}|}$ to the location vector $({\boldsymbol\ell}_x,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o)\in\mathcal{L}$. 
Specifically, for each $f_{\mathbf v}\in\mathfrak{F}$ and for a fixed $\mathbf o\in\mathcal{O}$, we can see that $f_{\mathbf v}(\cdot, \mathbf o)$ is constructed by applying a sum of \emph{frequency masks} indexed by ${\boldsymbol\ell}_x\in\mathcal{L}_X$ to the original B-spline $M_{\mathfrak{K},-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}$,
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{F}[f_{\mathbf v}(\cdot, \mathbf o)](\boldsymbol{\omega}_x) = \mathcal{F}\left[M_{\mathfrak{K},-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\right](\boldsymbol{\omega}_x) \cdot \Big(  \sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o\in \mathcal{L}_O} \underbrace{ \sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_x \in \mathcal{L}_X} \beta_{\mathbf v({\boldsymbol\ell}_x,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o)} \mathbbm{1}_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_x}\left(2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_x}}\boldsymbol{\omega}_x\right)}_{\text{frequency masks}} M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}(\mathbf o) \Big).
\end{align*}
\Cref{fig:masks_visualisation} is provided to illustrate this effect of frequency masking. 

We prove in Eq. \eqref{eq:f_bv_besov_norm_estimate} in the Supplementary that $\mathfrak{F}\subseteq \mathbb{U}(B^{s_x,s_o}_{2,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})) \cap L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}) \cap L^1(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}) \cap C^0(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}) \subseteq \mathfrak{S}$, satisfying \Cref{ass:f_ast}. 
For each $f_{\mathbf v} \in \mathfrak{F}$, we construct the conditional distribution $P_{\mathbf v}(\cdot\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o) := \mathcal{N}((Tf_{\mathbf v})(\mathbf z,\mathbf o), \sigma^2)$ as the normal distribution on $\mathbb{R}$ with mean $(Tf_{\mathbf v})(\mathbf z,\mathbf o)$ and variance $\sigma^2$, such that $P_{\mathbf v}$ satisfies \Cref{ass:subgaussian}. Together with the marginal distribution $P_{ZO}$ over $\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}$, we have constructed a family of distributions $\{
P_{\mathbf v}, \mathbf v \in \{0,1\}^{|\mathcal{L}|}\}$ over $\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}\times\mathbb{R}$ with each $P_{\mathbf v}$ associated to a $f_{\mathbf v} \in \mathfrak{F}$. 
Next, by the Gilbert-Varshamov Bound~\citep[Lemma 2.9]{Tsybakov}, we prove in Eq.~\eqref{eq:f_l2_separate} and Eq.~\eqref{eq:kl_upper_bound_small} in the Supplementary that there exists a subset $V_\mathfrak{K} \subseteq \{0,1\}^{|\mathcal{L}|}$ with 
$|V_\mathfrak{K}|\geq 2^{\frac{\mathcal{L}}{8}}$ such that for any $f_{\mathbf v}, f_{\mathbf v^\prime} \in \mathfrak{F}_{\mathrm{pruned}} = \{f_{\mathbf v}\mid \mathbf v\in V_\mathfrak{K}\}$, there is 
\begin{align*}
    \|f_{\mathbf v} - f_{\mathbf v'}\|^2_{L^2(P_{XO})} \geq 2^{-2\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}} \zeta^{-d_x}, \quad \mathrm{KL} \left(P_{\boldsymbol{v}}^{\otimes n}, P_{\boldsymbol{0}}^{\otimes n}\right) \leq n 2^{-2\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}(\frac{d_x}{s_x}\eta_1 + 1)} . 
\end{align*}
Therefore, we have established that the function class $\mathfrak{F}_{\mathrm{pruned}}$ satisfies all the three properties as desired, namely $\mathfrak{F}_{\mathrm{pruned}}\subset \mathfrak{G}$, functions $f_{\mathbf v} \in \mathfrak{F}_{\mathrm{pruned}}$ are well-separated in $L^2(P_{XO})$ yet statistically indistinguishable. 
Finally, we take $\zeta = (\log n)^2$, we apply \citet[Theorem 20]{fischer2020sobolev} and the general reduction scheme in \citet[Section 2.2]{Tsybakov} to obtain the desired minimax lower bound.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce NPIV-O to NPIR-O with known $T$, build a packing of Besov functions from B-splines convolved with high-frequency band-pass masks in $x$, and apply Fischer–Steinwart Thm 20 / Tsybakov reduction.

nodes.statement: The cardinal B-spline of order $\mathfrak{m}\in \mathbb{N}$ is defined as the repeated $\mathfrak{m}$ times convolution $\iota_{\mathfrak{m}} = \iota_{0}\ast \dots \ast \iota_0$ where $\iota_0$ is the indicator function $\mathbbm{1}_{[0,1]}$. Let $d$ denote the ambient dimension, and let $\boldsymbol{s} = (s_1,\dots, s_d)$ denote a smoothness vector. Define the notation $\underline{s} = \min(s_1,\dots,s_{d})$ and $s_i^\prime := \frac{\underline{s}}{s_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq d$. The (anisotropic) B-spline of order $\mathfrak{m}$ with resolution $\mathfrak{K} \in \mathbb{N}_+$ and location vector $ {\boldsymbol\ell} \in \prod_{i=1}^{d}\{-\mathfrak{m},-\mathfrak{m}+1,\dots, 2^{\left\lfloor \mathfrak{K} s_i^\prime \right\rfloor} \}$ is defined as $M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}}(\mathbf x) = \prod_{i=1}^{d} \iota_{\mathfrak{m}} (2^{\lfloor \mathfrak{K} s_i^\prime \rfloor}x_i - \ell_i)$.

nodes.name: Approximation error analysis for KIV without covariates
nodes.statement:
In NPIV, the conditional expectation operator is $T: L^2(P_{X}) \to L^2(P_{Z})$, $f \mapsto \mathbb{E}[f(X)\mid Z]$.
Hence $f_{\lambda}$ defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:f_lambda_main} reduces to the following
\begin{talign*}
    f_{\lambda} := arg\,min_{f\in \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}}\lambda\|f\|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}} + \|T([f]-f_{\ast})\|^2_{L^2(P_{Z})}.
\end{talign*}
We first employ the fact that $f_{\lambda}$ is the minimizer, hence for some $f_{\mathrm{aux}} \in \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}$,
\begin{align*}
    \|T([f_{\lambda}] - f_{\ast})\|^2_{L^2(P_{Z})} \leq \lambda \|f_{\mathrm{aux}}\|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}} + \|T([f_{\mathrm{aux}}] - f_{\ast})\|^2_{L^2(P_{Z})} .
\end{align*}
Here, $f_{\mathrm{aux}}$ is defined as
$f_{\mathrm{aux}} := f_{\ast, \mathrm{low}} + K_{\gamma_x}\ast f_{\ast, \mathrm{high}}$ , where $K_{\gamma_x}$ is defined, following \citet{hang2021optimal,eberts2013optimal}, as
\begin{talign} K_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x) := \sum_{j=1}^r\binom{r}{j}(-1)^{1-j} \frac{1}{(j\gamma_x)^{d}} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}}  \exp\left( -2 \sum_{i=1}^{d} \frac{x_i^2}{(j\gamma_x)^2} \right) ,
\end{talign}
and $f_{\ast, \mathrm{low}}, f_{\ast ,\mathrm{high}}$ are defined such that $f_{\ast, \mathrm{low}}$ (resp. $f_{\ast, \mathrm{high}}$) corresponds to the low-frequency (resp. high-frequency) component of $f_{\ast} = f_{\ast, \mathrm{low}} + f_{\ast ,\mathrm{high}}$:
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{F}[f_{\ast, \mathrm{low}}](\boldsymbol{\omega}_x) &= \mathcal{F}[f_{\ast}](\boldsymbol{\omega}_x)\cdot \mathbbm{1}[\boldsymbol{\omega}_x: \|\boldsymbol{\omega}_x\|_{2}\leq \gamma_x^{-1}]\\
    \mathcal{F}[f_{\ast, \mathrm{high}}](\boldsymbol{\omega}_x) &= \mathcal{F}[f_{\ast}](\boldsymbol{\omega}_x)\cdot \mathbbm{1}[\boldsymbol{\omega}_x: \|\boldsymbol{\omega}_x\|_{2}\geq \gamma_x^{-1}]. 
\end{align*}
To see why $f_{\mathrm{aux}}\in\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}$, note that 
$\|f_{\ast,\mathrm{low}}\|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}} \lesssim \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x}}|\mathcal{F}[f_{\ast}](\boldsymbol{\omega}_x)|^2\;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{\omega}_x = \|f_{\ast}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})} < \infty$ and $K_{\gamma_x}\ast f_{\ast, \mathrm{high}} \in \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}$ proved by \citet{eberts2013optimal}.
Then we have
\begin{align}
    \|T([f_{\lambda}] - f_{\ast})\|^2_{L^2(P_{Z})} &\leq \lambda \|f_{\mathrm{aux}}\|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}} + \|T(f_{\ast,\mathrm{high}} - K_{\gamma_x}\ast f_{\ast, \mathrm{high}})\|^2
    _{L^2(P
    _{Z})} \nonumber \\
    &\stackrel{(\ast)}{\leq} \lambda \|f_{\mathrm{aux}}\|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}} + \gamma_x^{2d_x\eta}\|f_{\ast,\mathrm{high}} - K_{\gamma_x}\ast f_{\ast, \mathrm{high}}\|^2
    _{L^2(P_{X})} \\
    &\stackrel{(\ast\ast)}\lesssim \lambda \gamma_x^{-d_x} + \gamma_x^{2d_x\eta + 2s_x} \nonumber .
\end{align}
where $(\ast)$ follows by \Cref{ass:T_contractivity}, and $(\ast\ast)$ follows by the same derivations in \citet[Theorem 2.2, Theorem 2.3]{eberts2013optimal}. 
Eq.~\eqref{eq:key_step} is the key step which would require significant modifications in the setting of NPIV-O due to the existence of observed covariates. Finally, we have
\begin{align*}
    &\quad \|[f_{\lambda}] - f_{\ast}\|^2_{L^2(P_{X})}\nonumber\\
    &\leq \|[f_{\lambda}] - [f_{\mathrm{aux}}]\|^2_{L^2(P_{X})} + \|[f_{\mathrm{aux}}] - f_{\ast}\|^2_{L^2(P_{X})}\nonumber\\
    &\stackrel{(a)}{\leq} \gamma_{x}^{-2d_x\eta} \|T[f_{\lambda}] - T [f_{\mathrm{aux}}]\|^2_{L^2(P_{Z})} + \|[f_{\mathrm{aux}}] - f_{\ast}\|^2_{L^2(P_{X})}\nonumber\\
    &\leq \gamma_{x}^{-2d_x\eta}\left(\|T([f_{\lambda}] - f_{\ast})\|^2_{L^2(P_{Z})} + \|T([f_{\mathrm{aux}}] - f_{\ast})\|^2_{L^2(P_{Z})}\right) + \|[f_{\mathrm{aux}}] - f_{\ast}\|^2_{L^2(P_{X})}\nonumber\\
    &\stackrel{(b)}{\leq} \gamma_{x}^{-2d_x\eta}\left(\|T([f_{\lambda}] - f_{\ast})\|^2_{L^2(P_{Z})} + \gamma_x^{2d_x\eta}\|[f_{\mathrm{aux}}] - f_{\ast}\|^2_{L^2(P_{X})}\right) + \|[f_{\mathrm{aux}}] - f_{\ast}\|^2_{L^2(P_{X})}\nonumber\\
    &\lesssim \gamma_x^{-2d_x\eta} \left(\lambda \gamma_x^{-d_x} + \gamma_x^{2d_x\eta + 2s_x} \right) + \steve{2} \|[f_{\mathrm{aux}}] - f_{\ast}\|^2_{L^2(P_{X})} \nonumber \stackrel{(c)}{\lesssim} n^{-\frac{2s_x}{d_x + 2s_x + 2\eta d_x}} .
\end{align*}
In the above derivations, $(a)$ follows by an application of \Cref{ass:T_frequency_ill_posedness} and \Cref{lem:l2toprojected_illp} since $\|f_\lambda\|^2 \leq \lambda^{-1}\|Tf_\ast\|_{L^2(P_Z)}^2 \lesssim n$ by the optimality of $f_\lambda$ and $\|f_{\text{aux}}\|\leq n$ by the same derivations as in Eq.~\eqref{eq:f_aux_norm} in the Supplement. The second term of Eq.~\eqref{eq:term_lemma_D_18} in the Supplement is subsumed by the following choice of $\gamma_x$. 
Furthermore, $(b)$ follows from \Cref{ass:T_contractivity}, and $(c)$ follows from using Eq.~\eqref{eq:f_f_aux_diff} in the Supplement and choosing $
\lambda = n^{-1}$, $\gamma_x = n^{-\frac{1}{d_x + 2s_x + 2\eta d_x}}$.
The upper bound on the approximation error above is \emph{optimal} in the sense that \steve{it matches the minimax lower bound of NPIV with Besov targets (see e.g \citep{Chen_2018} and our Theorem 4.2 with $d_o=0$)}.

nodes.name: Lengthscale balance conditions explain the gap
nodes.statement:
We conclude this section by offering a more practical perspective on why the gap emerges. 
Hyperparameters including the kernel lengthscales are selected via cross-validation in practice. 
For the KIV-O estimator $\hat{f}_{\lambda}$ computed from Stage II samples $\mathcal{D}_2=\{(\mathbf{z}_i, \mathbf{o}_i, y_i)\}_{i=1}^n$, the kernel lengthscales $\gamma_x, \gamma_o$ are selected by minimizing the following cross-validation criterion. 
\begin{talign} \mathrm{CV}(\gamma_x,\gamma_o,\lambda) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_i - \langle \hat{f}_{-i, \gamma_x,\gamma_o,\lambda}, \hat{F}_{\xi}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i)\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}})^2,
\end{talign}
where $\hat{f}_{-i, \gamma_x,\gamma_o,\lambda}$ denotes the version of $\hat{f}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o,\lambda}$ computed from $n-1$ samples from $\mathcal{D}_2$ excluding its $i$-th sample. 
This cross-validation criterion $\mathrm{CV}(\gamma_x,\gamma_o,\lambda)$ is a consistent estimator for the \emph{projected} risk $\|T([\hat{f}_\lambda] - f_*)\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})}$ and has been used in many 2SLS approaches~\citep{hartford2017deep, xu2021deep, mastouri2021proximal, xu2025kernelsingleproxycontrol}. 

Similarly, the choice of lengthscales $\gamma_x,\gamma_o, \lambda$ in our upper bound analysis is also obtained by minimizing the projected risk $\|T([\hat{f}_\lambda] - f_*)\|_{L^2(P_{X O})}$ which results 
$\gamma_x^{s_x+d_x\eta} = \gamma_o^{s_o}$. 
This can be contrasted with the choice of kernel lengthscales in anisotropic kernel ridge regression which imposes a different balance condition $\gamma_x^{s_x} = \gamma_o^{s_o}$~\citep{hang2021optimal}. The extra $d_x\eta$ in the exponent of $\gamma_x$ arises due to the partial smoothing effect of $T$, which maps a function that is $(s_x, s_o)$-smooth on $\mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{O}$ to a function that is $(s_x + d_x\eta, s_o)$-smooth on $\mathcal{Z} \times \mathcal{O}$. 
On the other hand, our minimax lower bound requires constructing B-splines in Eq.~\eqref{eq:Bspline_main} in the Supplement with resolution $\mathfrak{K}$ and $J_x := 2^{\lfloor\frac{\mathfrak{K} s}{s_x}\rfloor}$ and $J_o := 2^{\lfloor\frac{\mathfrak{K} s}{s_o}\rfloor}$. $J_x, J_o$ play a role analogous to $\gamma_x, \gamma_o$ (see \Cref{rem:connection_smoip}), but they satisfy the balance condition $J_x^{s_x} \asymp J_o^{s_o}$. 
This discrepancy between the kernel lengthscales balance condition and B-spline lengthscales balance condition gives rise to the gap between our upper and lower bound.
Simply enforcing $\gamma_x^{s_x} = \gamma_o^{s_o}$ in our upper bound analysis would result in a slower rate.
nodes.section: 5.2 Analysis of the approximation error in KIV-O
nodes.statement_short: Tuning lengthscales to the projected risk (as cross-validation does) gives balance $\gamma_x^{s_x+d_x\eta}=\gamma_o^{s_o}$, unlike the B-spline balance in the lower bound; this mismatch is the gap.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.1
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma\in (0,1)$ be arbitrary. Let $\epsilon > 0$ be arbitrary. We define \begin{align*} f_{\gamma, \epsilon}(\mathbf x,\mathbf o) &:= \mathcal{F}^{-1}\left[\mathbbm{1}[\|\boldsymbol{\omega}\|_2 \in [\gamma^{-1}, \gamma^{-1}+\epsilon]]\right](\mathbf x). \end{align*} We have $f_{\gamma,\epsilon}\in \mathrm{LF}\left((\gamma^{-1} + \epsilon)^{-1}\right)\cap \mathrm{HF}(\gamma)\cap L^{\infty}(P_{XO})$. Since $P_{XO}$ admits a density function on $\mathcal{X}\times \mathcal{O}$, and $f_{\gamma,\epsilon}$ only vanishes on sets of null Lebesgue measure, we have $\|f_{\gamma,\epsilon}\|_{L^2(P_{XO})}\neq 0$. As imposed by \Cref{ass:T_contractivity} and \Cref{ass:T_frequency_ill_posedness}, we thus have \begin{align*} c_0^{-1} \left(\gamma^{-1} + \epsilon\right)^{-d_x\eta_0}\|f_{\gamma,\epsilon}\|_{L^2(P_{XO})} \leq \|Tf_{\gamma,\epsilon}\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} \leq c_1 \gamma^{d_x\eta_1}\|f_{\gamma,\epsilon}\|_{L^2(P_{XO})}. \end{align*} Since $\|f_{\gamma,\epsilon}\|_{L^2(P_{XO})}\neq 0$, we have $(\forall \gamma\in (0,1))\;(\forall \epsilon >0)\; c_0^{-1}\left(\gamma^{-1} + \epsilon\right)^{-d_x\eta_0} \leq c_1 \gamma^{d_x\eta_1}$. For a fixed $\gamma$, taking the limit $\epsilon \to 0$, we have by continuity \begin{align} (\forall \gamma\in (0,1))\; \frac{1}{c_0 c_1}\leq \gamma^{d_x(\eta_1-\eta_0)}. \end{align} Taking the limit $\gamma\to 1$ in Eq.~\eqref{eq:lem_eta_key}, we find $c_0c_1 \geq 1$. Then since Eq.~\eqref{eq:lem_eta_key} holds for all $\gamma\in (0,1)$, we find that $\eta_1\leq \eta_0$.

nodes.name: Distribution and distribution of a function
nodes.statement: Let $\Omega\subseteq \mathbb{R}^{d}$ be a domain. A distribution $u\in \mathcal{D}'(\Omega)$ is a continuous linear functional on the space of test functions $\mathcal{D}(\Omega)$, where $\mathcal{D}(\Omega)$ is the set $C^{\infty}_c(\Omega)$ endowed with the \emph{canonical limit of Fréchet topology}. For a locally integrable function $f\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$, for all $\phi\in \mathcal{D}(\Omega)$, we define the distribution $T_f$ by \begin{align*} T_f\phi := \int_{\Omega}f(\mathbf x)\phi(\mathbf x)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x . \end{align*}
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
nodes.label: defi:fn_dist

nodes.name: Support of a distribution
nodes.statement: A distribution $u\in \mathcal{D}'(\Omega)$ is supported in the closed set $K\subset \Omega$ if $u[\phi] = 0$ $\forall \phi\in C^{\infty}_c(\Omega\setminus K)$. The \emph{support} of $u$, $\mathrm{supp}\; u$ is the set \begin{align*} \mathrm{supp}\; u = \cap \{K: u\text{ is supported in }K\}. \end{align*}
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
nodes.label: defi:supp_dist

nodes.name: Tempered distribution and Schwartz space
nodes.statement: We define the \emph{Schwartz space} $\mathcal{S}$ via \begin{align*} \mathcal{S} = \left\{\phi\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{d})\mid \forall \bm{\alpha}, \forall N\in \mathbb{N},\;\sup_{\mathbf x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}}\left|(1+|\mathbf x|)^{N}D^{\bm{\alpha}}\phi(\mathbf x)\right| < \infty\right\}. \end{align*} We say that a sequence $\{\phi_j\}^{\infty}_{j=1}\subset \mathcal{S}$ tends to zero iff \begin{align*} \sup_{\mathbf x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}}|(1+|\mathbf x|)^{N}D^{\bm{\alpha}}\phi_j(\mathbf x)|\to 0 \end{align*} for all $N\in \mathbb{N}$ and all multi-indices $\bm{\alpha}$. This endows $\mathcal{S}$ with a topology. We define the space of \emph{tempered distributions} to be the continuous dual space of $\mathcal{S}$, denoted as $\mathcal{S}'$.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T

nodes.name: Periodic distribution
nodes.statement: We define the translation of a distribution $u\in \mathcal{D}'(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ via $\tau_{\mathbf z}u[\phi] = u[\tau_{-\mathbf z}\phi]$ for all $\phi\in \mathcal{D}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$, where we use $\tau_{\mathbf z}\phi(\mathbf x):= \phi(\mathbf x-\mathbf z)$. We say that a distribution $u\in \mathcal{D}'(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ is periodic if for each $\mathbf{g}\in \mathbb{Z}^{d}$ we have $\tau_{\mathbf{g}} u = u$. Clearly, if $f\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ is periodic, then $T_f$ is a periodic distribution.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T

nodes.name: Fourier transform of L^1 functions
nodes.statement: For $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^{d})$, we define the Fourier transform $\mathcal{F}[f] = \hat{f} : \mathbb{R}^{d}\to \mathbb{C}$ by \begin{align*} \mathcal{F}[f](\boldsymbol{\xi}) = \hat{f}(\boldsymbol{\xi}) := \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} f(\mathbf x)\exp(-i\langle \mathbf x, \boldsymbol{\xi}\rangle)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x. \end{align*}
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T

nodes.name: Fourier transform of tempered distributions
nodes.statement: For a distribution $u\in \mathcal{S}'$, we define the Fourier transform of $u$, written $\hat{u}\in \mathcal{S}'$, to be the distribution satisfying: \begin{align*} \hat{u}[\phi] = u[\hat{\phi}], \;\forall \phi\in\mathcal{S}, \end{align*} which is well defined since the Fourier transform maps $\mathcal{S}$ to $\mathcal{S}$ continuously.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
nodes.definiendum: Fourier transform of a tempered distribution

nodes.name: Exponential e_xi
nodes.statement: Hence, $\forall \mathbf x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}$, we define $e_{\boldsymbol{\xi}}(\mathbf x) = \exp(i2\pi \langle \mathbf x, \boldsymbol{\xi}\rangle)$.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T

nodes.name: Fourier transform of a trigonometric exponential is a Dirac delta
nodes.statement:
So $\forall \phi\in \mathcal{S}$, we have
\begin{align} T_{e_{\boldsymbol{\xi}}}[\hat{\phi}] = \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} \exp(i2 \pi \langle \mathbf x, \boldsymbol{\xi}\rangle)\hat{\phi}(\mathbf x)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x 
    = (2\pi)^{d}\phi(2\pi \boldsymbol{\xi}).
\end{align}
i.e. $\mathcal{F}[T_{e_{\boldsymbol{\xi}}}] = (2\pi)^{d}\delta_{2\pi \boldsymbol{\xi}}$, the Dirac delta distribution at $2\pi \boldsymbol{\xi}$.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
assumptions: $\forall \phi\in \mathcal{S}$
conclusions: $\mathcal{F}[T_{e_{\boldsymbol{\xi}}}] = (2\pi)^{d}\delta_{2\pi \boldsymbol{\xi}}$, the Dirac delta distribution at $2\pi \boldsymbol{\xi}$

nodes.name: Fourier transform of a trigonometric polynomial (eq:fourier_transform_trig_poly)
nodes.statement: T_{e_{\boldsymbol{\xi}}}[\hat{\phi}] = \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} \exp(i2 \pi \langle \mathbf x, \boldsymbol{\xi}\rangle)\hat{\phi}(\mathbf x)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x = (2\pi)^{d}\phi(2\pi \boldsymbol{\xi}).
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
nodes.label: eq:fourier_transform_trig_poly

nodes.name: Periodic distributions are tempered
nodes.statement: Let $u\in \mathcal{D}'(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ be a periodic distribution. Then $u$ is in fact a tempered distribution, i.e. $u\in \mathcal{S}'$.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
assumptions: Let $u\in \mathcal{D}'(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ be a periodic distribution.
conclusions: $u$ is in fact a tempered distribution, i.e. $u\in \mathcal{S}'$.
nodes.label: lem:periodic_distributions_tempered

nodes.name: Fourier series of periodic distributions
nodes.statement: Suppose $u\in \mathcal{D}'(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ is a periodic distribution. Then there exist constants $c_{\boldsymbol{\xi}}\in \mathbb{C}$ such that $u$ can be represented as a (generalized) Fourier series, \begin{align*} u = \sum_{\boldsymbol{\xi}\in \mathbb{Z}^d}c_{\boldsymbol{\xi}} \,T_{e_{\boldsymbol{\xi}}}, \end{align*} with $c_{\boldsymbol{\xi}}$ satisfying the bound $|c_{\boldsymbol{\xi}}|\leq K(1+|\boldsymbol{\xi}|)^N$ for some $K>0$ and $N\in \mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
assumptions: Suppose $u\in \mathcal{D}'(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ is a periodic distribution.
conclusions: there exist constants $c_{\boldsymbol{\xi}}\in \mathbb{C}$ such that $u$ can be represented as a (generalized) Fourier series, \begin{align*} u = \sum_{\boldsymbol{\xi}\in \mathbb{Z}^d}c_{\boldsymbol{\xi}} \,T_{e_{\boldsymbol{\xi}}}, \end{align*} with $c_{\boldsymbol{\xi}}$ satisfying the bound $|c_{\boldsymbol{\xi}}|\leq K(1+|\boldsymbol{\xi}|)^N$ for some $K>0$ and $N\in \mathbb{Z}$.

nodes.name: LF(gamma), HF(gamma) for distributions
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
nodes.statement_short: Generalises LF/HF to locally integrable $f$ whose slices are tempered distributions, with Fourier support inside/outside the radius-$\gamma^{-1}$ ball.

nodes.name: Distributional LF/HF sets (eq:distribution_lf_hf_set_defn)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \mathrm{LF}(\gamma) := \{ f\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}) \ | \ & \forall \mathbf o \in \mathcal{O}, \; T_{f(\cdot, \mathbf o)} \in \mathcal {S}'(\mathbb{R}^{d_x}), \\ & \;\mathrm{supp}\big(\mathcal{F}[f(\cdot, \mathbf o)]\big) \subseteq \left\{ \boldsymbol{\omega}_x \in \mathbb{R}^{d_x} : \|\boldsymbol{\omega}_x\|_2 \leq \gamma^{-1} \right\} \}.\\ \mathrm{HF}(\gamma) := \{ f\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}) \ | \ & \forall \mathbf o \in \mathcal{O}, \; T_{f(\cdot, \mathbf o)} \in \mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}^{d_x}), \\ & \;\mathrm{supp}\big(\mathcal{F}[f(\cdot, \mathbf o)]\big) \subseteq \left\{ \boldsymbol{\omega}_x \in \mathbb{R}^{d_x} : \|\boldsymbol{\omega}_x\|_2 \geq \gamma^{-1} \right\} \}. \end{aligned}
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
nodes.label: eq:distribution_lf_hf_set_defn

nodes.name: Fourier measure of partial ill-posedness of T (distributional)
nodes.statement: There exists a constant $c_0>0$ and a parameter $\eta_0\in [0,\infty)$ only depending on $T$, such that for all $\gamma \in (0,1)$ and all functions $f \in \mathrm{LF}(\gamma) \cap L^\infty(P_{XO})$, the following inequality is satisfied: \begin{align*} \|f\|_{L^2(P_{XO})} \leq c_0\gamma^{-d_x\eta_0} \|Tf\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} . \end{align*} In particular, $c_0$ does not depend on $\gamma$.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
nodes.label: ass:T_frequency_ill_posedness_schwartz

nodes.name: Fourier measure of partial contractivity of T (distributional)
nodes.statement: There exists a constant $c_1>0$ and a parameter $\eta_1\in [0,\infty)$ only depending on $T$, such that for all $\gamma \in (0,1)$ and all functions $f \in \mathrm{HF}(\gamma) \cap L^\infty(P_{XO})$, the following inequality is satisfied: \begin{align*} \|Tf\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} \leq c_1\gamma^{d_x\eta_1}\|f\|_{L^2(P_{XO})} . \end{align*} In particular, $c_1$ does not depend on $\gamma$.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
nodes.label: ass:T_contractivity_schwartz

nodes.name: Unit circle S^1 and Haar measure
nodes.statement: Let $(S^{1}, +)$ denote the unit circle (equipped with a group structure via addition), and let $\mathrm{d}x$ denote the Haar measure on $S^{1}$, which coincides with the pushforward of the Lebesgue measure under the quotient map $S^{1}\cong \frac{\mathbb{R}}{\mathbb{Z}}$.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T

nodes.name: Fourier series on S^1
nodes.statement: Let $f\in L^1(S^{1})$. We define the $n$th Fourier coefficient of $f$ by $\mathcal{F}[f][n] = \int_{S^1} f(x)e^{-i2\pi n x}\;\mathrm{d}x$. The Fourier series of $f\in L^1(S^1)$ is the trigonometric series $f(x) = \sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}\mathcal{F}[f][n]e^{i2\pi nx}$.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T

nodes.name: Convolution theorem on S^1
nodes.statement: Let $f,g \in L^1(S^{1})$. For almost all $t\in S^1$, the function $f(t - \tau)g(\tau)$ is $L^1(S^{1})$-integrable as a function of $\tau$, and if we define the convolution \begin{align*} h(t) = \int_{S^1} f(t-\tau)g(\tau)\;\mathrm{d}\tau \end{align*} then $h\in L^1(S^1)$ with $\|h\|_{L^1(S^{1})}\leq \|f\|_{L^1(S^{1})}\|g\|_{L^1(S^{1})}$. Moreover, $(\forall n\in \mathbb{Z})$, we have \begin{align*} \mathcal{F}[h][n] = \mathcal{F}[f][n]\mathcal{F}[g][n]. \end{align*}
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
assumptions: Let $f,g \in  L^1(S^{1})$.
conclusions: For almost all $t\in S^1$, the function $f(t - \tau)g(\tau)$ is $L^1(S^{1})$-integrable as a function of $\tau$, and if we define the convolution \begin{align*} h(t) = \int_{S^1} f(t-\tau)g(\tau)\;\mathrm{d}\tau \end{align*} then $h\in L^1(S^1)$ with $\|h\|_{L^1(S^{1})}\leq \|f\|_{L^1(S^{1})}\|g\|_{L^1(S^{1})}$. Moreover, $(\forall n\in \mathbb{Z})$, we have \begin{align*} \mathcal{F}[h][n] = \mathcal{F}[f][n]\mathcal{F}[g][n]. \end{align*}
nodes.label: prop:convolution_theorem

nodes.name: Circle-valued example satisfying partial contractivity and ill-posedness with eta = k
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
nodes.statement_short: On the torus with $X=Z+0.1(U_1+\dots+U_k)$, $T^*T$ is a convolution whose Fourier coefficients decay like $n^{-2k}$, giving contractivity on HF and ill-posedness on LF with $\eta=k$.

nodes.name: Vanishing low-frequency Fourier coefficients (eq:schwartz_assumption_calf_g)
nodes.statement: \mathcal{F}[g][n] = 0 \quad \text{for all } n \in \mathbb{Z} \text{ such that } |n| \leq (2\pi \gamma)^{-1}.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
nodes.label: eq:schwartz_assumption_calf_g

nodes.name: L2 norm factorisation (eq:schwartz_f_g_l2_norm_equiv)
nodes.statement: \|f\|_{L^2(P_{XO})}^2 &= \int_{\mathbb{R}^{2}}|f(x,o)|^2p(x,o)\;\mathrm{d}x\;\mathrm{d}o \nonumber \\ &= \int_{S^1\times S^1}|f(x,o)|^2p(x,o)\;\mathrm{d}x\;\mathrm{d}o = \|g\|_{L^2(P_{X})}^2\|h\|^2_{L^2(P_{O})}.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
nodes.label: eq:schwartz_f_g_l2_norm_equiv

nodes.name: Expansion of ||Tf||^2 (eq:schwartz_expansion_tf_l2_sq)
nodes.statement: \|Tf\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})}^2 &= \langle f, T^{\ast}Tf\rangle_{L^2(P_{XO})}\nonumber\\ &= \int_{S^1\times S^1}\overline{f(x,o)}(T^{\ast}Tf)(x,o)p(x,o)\;\mathrm{d}x\;\mathrm{d}o.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
nodes.label: eq:schwartz_expansion_tf_l2_sq

nodes.name: Intermediate expression for ||Tf||^2 (eq:schwartz_tf_intm)
nodes.statement: \|Tf\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})}^2 &= \int_{S^1\times S^1}\overline{g(x)}\overline{h(o)}(T^{\ast}Tf)(x,o)p(x,o)\;\mathrm{d}x\;\mathrm{d}o\nonumber\\ &= \left(\int_{S^1}\overline{g(x)}\left(\int_{S^1}g(x')L(x,x')p(x)\;\mathrm{d}x'\right)\;\mathrm{d}x\right)\|h\|^2_{L^2(P_{O})}.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
nodes.label: eq:schwartz_tf_intm

nodes.name: Fourier coefficients of the kernel frak L (eq:schwartz_fourier_nonabs_val)
nodes.statement: \mathcal{F}[\mathfrak{L}][n] &= \left|10\int_{0}^{0.1}e^{-2\pi i nz}\;\mathrm{d}z\right|^{2k} = \left|\frac{10}{2\pi i n}\left(1 - e^{-0.2\pi i n}\right)\right|^{2k} = \left(\frac{10}{\pi n}\right)^{2k}\sin^{2k}(0.1\pi n).
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
nodes.label: eq: schwartz_fourier_nonabs_val

nodes.name: Decay bound on Fourier coefficients of frak L (eq:schwartz_fcoeff_mf_L)
nodes.statement: \mathcal{F}[\mathfrak{L}][n]\leq \left(\frac{10}{\pi n}\right)^{2k}.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
nodes.label: eq:schwartz_fcoeff_mf_L

nodes.name: Ratio ||Tf||^2/||h||^2 via Parseval (eq:example_ratio)
nodes.statement:
rac{\|Tf\|^2_{L^2(P_{ZO})}}{\|h\|^2_{L^2(P_{O})}} &= \int_{S^1}\overline{g(x)}\left(\int_{S^1}g(x')\mathfrak{L}(x-x')\;\mathrm{d}x'ight)\;\mathrm{d}x
onumber\ &\stackrel{(a)}{=} \sum_{n = -\infty}^{\infty}\overline{\mathcal{F}[g][n]}\mathcal{F}\left[\int_{S^1}g(x')\mathfrak{L}(\cdot -x')\;\mathrm{d}x'ight][n]
onumber\ &\stackrel{(b)}{=} \sum_{n = -\infty}^{\infty}\overline{\mathcal{F}[g][n]}\mathcal{F}[g][n]\mathcal{F}[\mathfrak{L}][n] = \sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}|\mathcal{F}[g][n]|^2\cdot \mathcal{F}[\mathfrak{L}][n]\ &\stackrel{(c)}{=} \sum_{n\in \mathbb{Z}, |n|> (2\pi\gamma)^{-1}}|\mathcal{F}[g][n]|^2\cdot \mathcal{F}[\mathfrak{L}][n] \stackrel{(d)}{\leq} (20\gamma)^{2k}\sum_{n\in \mathbb{Z}, |n|> (2\pi\gamma)^{-1}}|\mathcal{F}[g][n]|^2

nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T
nodes.label: eq: example_ratio

nodes.name: Closed-form KIV-O estimator
nodes.statement_short: Closed form of KIV-O: Stage I kernel ridge weights $J=(K_{\tilde Z\tilde O}+\tilde n\xi I)^{-1}(K_{\tilde ZZ}\odot K_{\tilde OO})$, Stage II dual KRR with Gram $(J^TK_{\tilde X\tilde X}J)\odot K_{OO}$.

nodes.name: Closed-form Stage I estimator (eq:closed_form_stage_1_estimator)
nodes.statement: \hat{F}_{\xi}(\cdot, \cdot) = \hat{C}_{X\mid Z,O; \xi} \phi_{Z}(\cdot)\otimes \phi_{O,1}(\cdot),\quad \hat{C}_{X\mid Z,O; \xi} = \boldsymbol{\Phi}_{\tilde{X}}^{\ast}\left(K_{\tilde{Z}\tilde{O};1} + \tilde{n}\xi\mathrm{Id}\right)^{-1}\boldsymbol{\Phi}_{\tilde{Z}\tilde{O}; 1},
nodes.label: eq:closed_form_stage_1_estimator

nodes.name: Closed form of hat F_xi at Stage II points (eq:closed_form_hat_F_xi)
nodes.statement: \hat{F}_{\xi}(\mathbf z_j, \mathbf o_j) = \boldsymbol{\Phi}_{\tilde{X}}^{\ast}\underbrace{\left(K_{\tilde{Z}\tilde{O},1} + \tilde{n}\xi\mathrm{Id}\right)^{-1}\left(K_{\tilde{Z}Z}\odot K_{\tilde{O}O;1}\right)_{: j}}_{=: J_{:j}} = \sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{n}}J_{ij}\phi_{X}(\tilde{\mathbf x}_i),
nodes.label: eq:closed_form_hat_F_xi

nodes.name: NPIV-O as a statistical inverse problem (eq:xi_inverse)
nodes.statement: Y = (Tf_\ast)(Z, O) + \upsilon, \quad \mathbb{E}[\upsilon \mid Z, O] = 0,
nodes.label: eq:xi_inverse

nodes.name: RKHS H_FO
nodes.statement: We define a reproducing kernel Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_{FO}$ as \begin{align*} \mathcal{H}_{FO} = \left\{f: \mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O}\to \mathbb{R}\mid \exists w\in \mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}, \; f(\mathbf z,\mathbf o) \equiv \langle w, F_{\ast}(\mathbf z,\mathbf o) \otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o)\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}\right\}, \end{align*} equipped with the norm \begin{align*} \|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}} := \inf\left\{\|w\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}\mid f(\mathbf z,\mathbf o) \equiv \langle w, F_{\ast}(\mathbf z,\mathbf o)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o)\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}\right\}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{H}_{FO}$: functions $(z,o)\mapsto\langle w, F_*(z,o)\otimes\phi_{\gamma_o}(o)\rangle$ for $w\in\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}$, with the infimum norm.
nodes.label: defi:H_F

nodes.name: Map V from H_{gamma_x,gamma_o} to H_FO
V is a metric surjection
nodes.statement: From Theorem 4.21 of \cite{steinwart2008support}, $V$ is a metric surjection.
conclusions: $V$ is a metric surjection

nodes.name: V acts as T on H_{gamma_x,gamma_o}
assumptions: for any $f\in \mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}$
conclusions: (Vf)(\mathbf z,\mathbf o) = \langle f, F_{\ast}(\mathbf z,\mathbf o)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o)\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} = \mathbb{E}[f(X,O)\mid Z=\mathbf z, O = \mathbf o] = (T[f])(\mathbf z,\mathbf o).

nodes.name: V is a surjective partial isometry
conclusions: $V$ is also a surjective partial isometry, i.e. $V$ is surjective and satisfies

nodes.name: H_FO norm as infimum (eq:r_pseudoinv_norm)
nodes.statement: \|r\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}} = \inf\{\|h\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}: h\in \mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o},\;r = Vh\},
nodes.label: eq:r_pseudoinv_norm

nodes.name: Canonical feature map of H_FO
nodes.statement: Thus, the canonical feature map of $\mathcal{H}_{FO}$ is $(\mathbf z,\mathbf o)\mapsto V(F_{\ast}(\mathbf z,\mathbf o)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o))$, a fact which was also observed on \citet[Page 28]{meunier2024nonparametricinstrumentalregressionkernel}.
conclusions: the canonical feature map of $\mathcal{H}_{FO}$ is $(\mathbf z,\mathbf o)\mapsto V(F_{\ast}(\mathbf z,\mathbf o)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o))$

nodes.name: Images h_lambda, bar h_lambda, h_*
bar h_lambda solves a KRR problem in H_FO
conclusions: $\overline{h}_{\lambda}$ is the solution to a standard kernel ridge regression problem with the RKHS $\mathcal{H}_{FO}$

nodes.name: bar h_lambda as KRR solution (eq:bhl_bvfl)
nodes.statement: \Bar{h}_{\lambda} = arg\,min_{h\in \mathcal{H}_{FO}}\lambda \|h\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}}^2 + \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(h(\mathbf z_i, \mathbf o_i) - y_i)^2 .
nodes.label: eq:bhl_bvfl

nodes.name: h_lambda solves a population KRR problem in H_FO
conclusions: for $h_\lambda$ we have

nodes.name: h_lambda as population KRR solution (eq:hat_bhl_bvfl)
nodes.statement: h_{\lambda} = arg\,min_{h\in \mathcal{H}_{FO}} \lambda \|h\|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}} + \|h_{\ast} - h\|^2_{L^2(P_{ZO})}.
nodes.label: eq:hat_bhl_bvfl

nodes.name: Projected error equals KRR generalization error in H_FO
nodes.statement:
Finally, we have 
\begin{align} \left\|T\left(\left[\Bar{f}_{\lambda} \right] - [f_{\lambda}]\right)\right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} = \left\| \left[V \Bar{f}_{\lambda}\right] - [V f_{\lambda}] \right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} = \left\|\left[\Bar{h}_{\lambda} \right] - \left[h_{\lambda}\right]\right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})},
\end{align}
which means that the projected error $\|T([\Bar{f}_{\lambda}] -[f_{\lambda}]])\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})}$ has been translated to the generalization error $\left\|\left[\Bar{h}_{\lambda} \right] - [h_{\lambda}]\right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})}$ of a standard kernel ridge regression (KRR) with this new hypothesis space $\mathcal{H}_{FO}$, which allows us to apply techniques from the analysis of kernel ridge regression.
conclusions: the projected error $\|T([\Bar{f}_{\lambda}] -[f_{\lambda}]])\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})}$ has been translated to the generalization error $\left\|\left[\Bar{h}_{\lambda} \right] - [h_{\lambda}]\right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})}$ of a standard kernel ridge regression (KRR) with this new hypothesis space $\mathcal{H}_{FO}$

nodes.name: Error translation identity (eq:error_translate)
nodes.statement: \left\|T\left(\left[\Bar{f}_{\lambda} \right] - [f_{\lambda}]\right)\right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} = \left\| \left[V \Bar{f}_{\lambda}\right] - [V f_{\lambda}] \right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} = \left\|\left[\Bar{h}_{\lambda} \right] - \left[h_{\lambda}\right]\right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})},
nodes.label: eq:error_translate

nodes.name: H_FO has a bounded kernel and embeds compactly into L2
nodes.statement:
We have
\begin{align*}
    &\quad \sup_{\mathbf o,\mathbf o^\prime} \sup_{\mathbf z,\mathbf z^\prime} \left\langle V (F_{\ast}(\mathbf z,\mathbf o) \otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o)), V (F_{\ast}(\mathbf z^\prime,\mathbf o^\prime) \otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o^\prime) ) \right\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}} \\
    &= \sup_{\mathbf o,\mathbf o^\prime} \sup_{\mathbf z,\mathbf z^\prime} \left\langle F_{\ast}(\mathbf z,\mathbf o) \otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o), F_{\ast}(\mathbf z^\prime,\mathbf o^\prime) \otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o^\prime) \right\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} \\
    &= \sup_{\mathbf o,\mathbf o^\prime} k_{O, \gamma_o}(\mathbf o, \mathbf o^\prime) \sup_{\mathbf z,\mathbf z^\prime} \iint_{\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{X}} k_{X, \gamma_x}(\mathbf x, \mathbf x^\prime)p(\mathbf x \mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o) p(\mathbf x^\prime \mid \mathbf z^\prime,\mathbf o^\prime)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x'\\
    &\leq \sup_{\mathbf o,\mathbf o^\prime}k_{O, \gamma_o}(\mathbf o, \mathbf o^\prime) \sup_{\mathbf x,\mathbf x^\prime} k_{X, \gamma_x}(\mathbf x, \mathbf x^\prime) \sup_{\mathbf z,\mathbf z^\prime} \iint_{\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{X}} p(\mathbf x \mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o) p(\mathbf x^\prime \mid \mathbf z^\prime,\mathbf o^\prime)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x' \\
    &= \sup_{\mathbf o,\mathbf o^\prime} k_{O, \gamma_o}(\mathbf o, \mathbf o^\prime) \sup_{\mathbf x,\mathbf x^\prime}k_{X, \gamma_x}(\mathbf x, \mathbf x^\prime) . 
\end{align*}
Hence the RKHS $\mathcal{H}_{FO}$ has a bounded kernel, therefore by \citet[Lemma 2.3]{steinwart2012mercer}, $\mathcal{H}_{FO}$ is compactly embedded into $L^2(P_{ZO})$.
conclusions: the RKHS $\mathcal{H}_{FO}$ has a bounded kernel
$\mathcal{H}_{FO}$ is compactly embedded into $L^2(P_{ZO})$

nodes.name: Covariance operator C_FO
Spectral decomposition of C_FO
nodes.statement:
It is a self-adjoint compact operator by \citet[Lemma 2.2]{steinwart2012mercer}.
The spectral theorem for self-adjoint compact
operators~\cite[Theorems VI.16,
VI.17]{reed1980methods} yields, there exists countable $\mu_{FO,1}\geq \mu_{FO,2}\geq \dots \geq 0$,  $([e_{FO,i}])_{i\geq 1}$ an orthonormal system of $L^2(P_{ZO})$ and $\left(\sqrt{\mu_{FO,i}}e_{FO,i}\right)\subseteq \mathcal{H}_{FO}$ an orthonormal system in $\mathcal{H}_{FO}$, such that 
\begin{align} C_{FO} = \sum_{i\geq 1}\mu_{FO,i}\langle \cdot, \sqrt{\mu_{FO,i}}e_{FO,i}\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}} \sqrt{\mu_{FO,i}}e_{FO,i}.
\end{align}
conclusions: It is a self-adjoint compact operator
there exists countable $\mu_{FO,1}\geq \mu_{FO,2}\geq \dots \geq 0$

nodes.name: Eigendecomposition of C_FO (eq:C_F_covariance)
nodes.statement: C_{FO} = \sum_{i\geq 1}\mu_{FO,i}\langle \cdot, \sqrt{\mu_{FO,i}}e_{FO,i}\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}} \sqrt{\mu_{FO,i}}e_{FO,i}.
nodes.label: eq:C_F_covariance

nodes.name: Effective dimension of H_FO
nodes.statement: The effective dimension of $\mathcal{H}_{FO}$, denoted as $\mathcal{N}_{FO} : [0,\infty)\to [0,\infty)$ is defined as \begin{align*} \mathcal{N}_{FO}(\lambda) = \mathrm{tr}\left((C_{FO}+\lambda)^{-1}C_{FO}\right) = \sum_{i\geq 1}\frac{\mu_{FO,i}}{\mu_{FO,i} + \lambda} . \end{align*}

nodes.name: Effective dimension bound for H_FO
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq 10$ and $\lambda=n^{-1}$. Let $\gamma_x,\gamma_o\in (0,1]$ be the lengthscales for the RKHS $\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}$. Suppose that the distribution $P_{XO}$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{assn: technical}. Then we have, \begin{align*} \mathcal{N}_{FO}(\lambda) \leq C'(\log n)^{d_x+d_o+1} \left(\gamma_x^{d_x}\gamma_o^{d_o}\right)^{-1} \end{align*} for some constant $C'$ independent of $n, \gamma_x,\gamma_o$.
assumptions: Let $n\geq 10$ and $\lambda=n^{-1}$. Let $\gamma_x,\gamma_o\in (0,1]$ be the lengthscales for the RKHS $\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}$. Suppose that the distribution $P_{XO}$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{assn: technical}.
conclusions: \begin{align*} \mathcal{N}_{FO}(\lambda) \leq C'(\log n)^{d_x+d_o+1} \left(\gamma_x^{d_x}\gamma_o^{d_o}\right)^{-1} \end{align*} for some constant $C'$ independent of $n, \gamma_x,\gamma_o$.
nodes.statement_short: With $\lambda=1/n$, $\mathcal{N}_{FO}(\lambda)\lesssim(\log n)^{d_x+d_o+1}(\gamma_x^{d_x}\gamma_o^{d_o})^{-1}$.
nodes.label: prop:eff_dim

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition C.1
nodes.statement_short: Bound eigenvalues of $C_{FO}$ via entropy numbers with $p=1/\log n$, then apply Caponnetto–De Vito Proposition 3 to bound the effective dimension.

nodes.name: Singular, entropy and approximation numbers
nodes.statement: In this section, for real-valued Hilbert spaces $E,F$ and a bounded, linear, compact operator $S:E\to F$, $s_i(S)$ denotes the $i$th singular value of $S$, as defined in \citet[Eq. (A.25) Page 505]{steinwart2008support}; $e_i(S)$ denotes the $i$th entropy number of $S$, as defined in \citet[Definition A.5.26 Page 516]{steinwart2008support}; $a_i(S)$ denotes the $i$th approximation number of $S$, as defined in \citet[Eq. (A.29) Page 506]{steinwart2008support}.

nodes.name: Entropy numbers of the anisotropic Gaussian RKHS
nodes.statement: Suppose that $P_{XO}$ satisfies \Cref{assn: technical} in the main text. Then, $(\forall i\geq 1)$, $(\gamma_x,\gamma_o\in (0,1])$, there exists a constant $C>0$ such that for any $p>0$, \begin{align*} e_i(\mathrm{id} : \mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}\hookrightarrow L^{2}(P_{XO})) \leq (3C)^{\frac{1}{p}} \left(\frac{d_x+d_o+1}{ep}\right)^{\frac{d_x+d_o+1}{p}}\left(\gamma_x^{d_x}\gamma_o^{d_o}\right)^{-\frac{1}{p}}i^{-\frac{1}{p}}. \end{align*}
assumptions: Suppose that $P_{XO}$ satisfies \Cref{assn: technical} in the main text.
conclusions: $(\forall i\geq 1)$, $(\gamma_x,\gamma_o\in (0,1])$, there exists a constant $C>0$ such that for any $p>0$, \begin{align*} e_i(\mathrm{id} : \mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}\hookrightarrow L^{2}(P_{XO})) \leq (3C)^{\frac{1}{p}} \left(\frac{d_x+d_o+1}{ep}\right)^{\frac{d_x+d_o+1}{p}}\left(\gamma_x^{d_x}\gamma_o^{d_o}\right)^{-\frac{1}{p}}i^{-\frac{1}{p}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Entropy numbers of $\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}\hookrightarrow L^2(P_{XO})$ decay like $(\gamma_x^{d_x}\gamma_o^{d_o})^{-1/p}i^{-1/p}$ for every $p>0$.
nodes.label: cor:entropy_bounded_obscov

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.1
nodes.statement: The corollary follows immediately from \citet[Proposition 1]{hang2021optimal} by setting $\boldsymbol{\gamma}=[\underbrace{\gamma_x, \ldots, \gamma_x}_{d_x}, \underbrace{\gamma_o, \ldots, \gamma_o}_{d_o}]^\top \in (0,1]^{d_x+d_o}$, and noting that $L^{\infty}(\mathcal{X}\times \mathcal{O})$ continuously embeds into $L^2(P_{XO})$ with $\|L^{\infty}(\mathcal{X}\times \mathcal{O})\hookrightarrow L^2(P_{XO})\|\leq 1$ and \citet[Eq. (A.38)]{steinwart2008support}.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from Hang & Steinwart Proposition 1 with anisotropic bandwidth vector.

nodes.name: Entropy numbers of H_FO are dominated by those of H_{gamma_x,gamma_o}
nodes.statement: We have, $(\forall i\geq 1)$, \begin{align*} e_i(\mathrm{id}: \mathcal{H}_{FO} \hookrightarrow L^2(P_{ZO})) \leq e_i(\mathrm{id}:\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}\hookrightarrow L^2(P_{XO})). \end{align*}
conclusions: We have, $(\forall i\geq 1)$, \begin{align*} e_i(\mathrm{id}: \mathcal{H}_{FO} \hookrightarrow L^2(P_{ZO})) \leq e_i(\mathrm{id}:\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}\hookrightarrow L^2(P_{XO})). \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:reduced_rkhs_entropy

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.2
nodes.statement: Fix $i\geq 1$. For a Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$, $B_{\mathcal{H}}$ denotes the unit ball in $\mathcal{H}$, and $B(x, r, \|\cdot \|_{\mathcal{H}})$ denotes the ball in $\mathcal{H}$ centred at $x\in\mathcal{H}$ with radius $r$. Fix $\epsilon>0$ such that $\exists g_1, \dots, g_{2^{i-1}} \in B_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}$ such that \begin{align*} B_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^{2^{i-1}}B\left(g_i, \epsilon, \|\cdot \|_{L^2(P_{XO})}\right). \end{align*} Fix $f\in B_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}}$ and an arbitrary $\tilde{\epsilon}>0$. By \citet[Eq. (4.11)]{steinwart2008support}, there exists $g\in \mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}$ such that \begin{align*} f = \langle g, F_{\ast}(\cdot, \cdot)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\cdot)\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} = Vg, \end{align*} and $\|g\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}\leq 1 + \tilde{\epsilon}$. By the preceding statement, $(\exists i\in \{1,\dots, 2^{i-1}\})$ such that \begin{align*} \|g - (1+\tilde{\epsilon})g_i\|_{L^2(P_{XO})}\leq \epsilon(1 + \tilde{\epsilon}). \end{align*} For $i\in \{1,\dots, 2^{i-1}\}$, define $f_i = (1+\tilde{\epsilon})Vg_i = (1+\tilde{\epsilon})\langle g_i, F_{\ast}(\cdot, \cdot)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\cdot)\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}$. Then we have \begin{align*} \|f - f_i\|^2_{L^2(P_{ZO})} &= \int_{\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O}}\langle g - (1+\tilde{\epsilon})g_i, F_{\ast}(\mathbf z,\mathbf o)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o)\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}^2p(\mathbf z,\mathbf o)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf z\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\ &= \int_{\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O}}\mathbb{E}[(g-(1+\tilde{\epsilon})g_i)(X,O)\mid Z = \mathbf z,O = \mathbf o]^2p(\mathbf z,\mathbf o)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf z\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\ &\leq \|g - (1+\tilde{\epsilon}) g_i\|^2_{L^2(P_{XO})}, \end{align*} where the inequality is deduced by Jensen's inequality. We find thus that \begin{align*} \mathcal{H}_{B_{FO}}\subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^{2^{i-1}}B(f_i, \epsilon(1+\tilde{\epsilon}), \|\cdot\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})}). \end{align*} Hence $e_i(\mathrm{id}: \mathcal{H}_{FO}\hookrightarrow L^2(P_{ZO})) \leq \epsilon(1+\tilde{\epsilon})$. Since $\epsilon > e_i(\mathrm{id}:\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}\hookrightarrow L^2(P_{XO}))$ and $\tilde{\epsilon}>0$ are arbitrary, it follows that $e_i(\mathrm{id}:\mathcal{H}_{FO}\hookrightarrow L^2(P_{ZO}))\leq e_i(\mathrm{id}:\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}\hookrightarrow L^2(P_{XO}))$.
nodes.statement_short: Covering argument: an $\epsilon$-net of the unit ball of $\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}$ maps under $V$ to a net of $\mathcal{H}_{FO}$ by Jensen's inequality.

nodes.name: Eigenvalues of C_FO bounded by entropy numbers
nodes.statement: Suppose that $P_{XO}$ satisfies \Cref{assn: technical} in the main text. We have that \begin{align*} \mu_{FO,i}\leq 4e_i(\mathrm{id}:\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}\hookrightarrow L^2(P_{XO}))^2 \end{align*}
assumptions: Suppose that $P_{XO}$ satisfies \Cref{assn: technical} in the main text.
conclusions: \begin{align*} \mu_{FO,i}\leq 4e_i(\mathrm{id}:\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}\hookrightarrow L^2(P_{XO}))^2 \end{align*}
nodes.label: cor:CFO_evalue_entropy_bound

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary C.1
nodes.statement: Let $\iota_{FO}: \mathcal{H}_{FO}\to L^2(P_{ZO})$ denote the embedding $\mathcal{H}_{FO}\hookrightarrow L^2(P_{ZO})$. We have, $(\forall i\geq 1)$, the following chain of derivations \begin{align*} \mu_{FO,i} &= \lambda_i(\iota_{FO}^{\ast}\iota_{FO}) \stackrel{(a)}{=} s_i(\iota_{FO})^2 \stackrel{(b)}{=} a_i(\iota_{FO})^2\\ &\stackrel{(c)}{\leq} 4e_i(\iota_{FO})^2 \stackrel{(d)}{\leq} 4e_i(\mathrm{id}:\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}\hookrightarrow L^2(P_{XO}))^2. \end{align*} In the above derivations, $(a)$ follows from \citet[Eq. (A.25)]{steinwart2008support}, $(b)$ follows from the paragraph after \citet[Eq. (A.29)]{steinwart2008support}, $(c)$ follows from \citet[Eq. (A.44)]{steinwart2008support}, and $(d)$ follows from \Cref{lem:reduced_rkhs_entropy}.
nodes.statement_short: Chain eigenvalues = squared singular = approximation numbers $\le$ 4 x entropy numbers, then apply Lemma C.2.

nodes.name: Continuous embedding
nodes.statement: A Hilbert space $(X,\|\cdot\|)$ is said to continuously embed into Hilbert space $(Y,\|\cdot\|)$ if $X\subset Y$ and there exists a constant $C$ such that $\|x\|_{Y}\leq C\|x\|_{X} $ for all $x\in X$. We denote this as $X\hookrightarrow Y$. The embedding norm $\|X\hookrightarrow Y\|$ is defined as the smallest constant $C$ for which the above inequality holds.
nodes.label: defi:cont_embed

nodes.name: Interpolation space (K-method)
nodes.statement: Assume that $X_0$ and $X_1$ are Hilbert spaces and $X_1\subseteq X_0$. For $\theta\in (0,1)$ and $x\in X_0$, we define the \emph{$K$-functional} $K(t,x;X_0,X_1)$ as follows \begin{align} K(t,x;X_0,X_1):= \inf_{y\in X_1}\left\{\|x-y\|_{X_0} + t\|y\|_{X_1}\right\} . \end{align} For $\theta\in (0,1)$, we define \emph{interpolation space} \cite{Hytönen2016AnalysisBanachSpaces}[Definition C.3.1] \begin{align*} (X_0,X_1)_{\theta,2}:= \{x\in X_0 \mid \|x\|_{\theta,2}<\infty\},\quad \|x\|_{\theta,2} := \left(\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(t^{-\theta}K(t,x;X_0,X_1)\right)^{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}t}{t}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} . \end{align*}
nodes.label: def:interpolation_space

nodes.name: H_FO embeds compactly into L2(Z x O)
nodes.statement: Since $P_{ZO}$ is equivalent to the Lebesgue measure over $\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}$ as per \Cref{ass:equiv_leb}, $\mathcal{H}_{FO}$ can also be compactly embedded into $L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O})$.
assumptions: $P_{ZO}$ is equivalent to the Lebesgue measure over $\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}$ as per \Cref{ass:equiv_leb}
conclusions: $\mathcal{H}_{FO}$ can also be compactly embedded into $L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O})$

nodes.name: theta-power space of H_FO
Power space of H_FO equals interpolation space
nodes.statement: For $0<\theta<1$, the $\theta$-power space coincides with the interpolation space $[\mathcal{H}_{FO}]^{\theta}_{L^2(P_{ZO})} \cong [L_2(P_{ZO}),[\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{P_{ZO}}]_{\theta, 2}$~\cite[Theorem 4.6]{steinwart2012mercer}.
assumptions: For $0<\theta<1$
conclusions: the $\theta$-power space coincides with the interpolation space

nodes.name: Notation [H_FO]_{L2(P_ZO)}
nodes.statement: We write $[\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(P_{ZO})} := [\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(P_{ZO})}^{1}$.

nodes.name: Notation [H_FO]_{L2(Z x O)}
nodes.statement: Similarly, we write $[\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})} := [\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})}^{1}$.

nodes.name: Embedding of power spaces of H_FO into L-infinity
nodes.statement: Suppose Assumption~\ref{assn: technical} holds, and let $m_o,m_z,\rho$ be as defined in the statement of Assumption~\ref{assn: technical}. Suppose $\theta\in (0,1)$ satisfies $\frac{d_o}{2m_o\theta} < 1$ and $\frac{d_z}{2m_z\theta} < 1$. Then there exists a constant $C_{\theta}>0$ independent of $n$ such that \begin{align*} \left\|k_{FO}^{\theta}\right\|_{\infty} := \left\|[\mathcal{H}_{FO}]^{\theta}_{P_{ZO}}\hookrightarrow L^{\infty}(P_{ZO})\right\|\lesssim C_{\theta} \rho^{\theta}\gamma_o^{-\theta m_o}. \end{align*}
assumptions: Suppose Assumption~\ref{assn: technical} holds, and let $m_o,m_z,\rho$ be as defined in the statement of Assumption~\ref{assn: technical}. Suppose $\theta\in (0,1)$ satisfies $\frac{d_o}{2m_o\theta} < 1$ and $\frac{d_z}{2m_z\theta} < 1$.
conclusions: there exists a constant $C_{\theta}>0$ independent of $n$ such that \begin{align*} \left\|k_{FO}^{\theta}\right\|_{\infty} := \left\|[\mathcal{H}_{FO}]^{\theta}_{P_{ZO}}\hookrightarrow L^{\infty}(P_{ZO})\right\|\lesssim C_{\theta} \rho^{\theta}\gamma_o^{-\theta m_o}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: For $\theta$ with $d_o/(2m_o\theta)<1$, $d_z/(2m_z\theta)<1$: $\|[\mathcal{H}_{FO}]^\theta\hookrightarrow L^\infty\|\lesssim \rho^\theta\gamma_o^{-\theta m_o}$ (EMB condition).
nodes.label: prop:emb_main

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition C.2
nodes.statement: By \Cref{lem:hfo_conts_embedding}, we have $[\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})} \hookrightarrow MW^{m_z,m_o}(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})$ and \begin{align*} \| [\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})} \hookrightarrow MW^{m_z,m_o}(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})\| \lesssim \rho \gamma_o^{-m_o}. \end{align*} By \Cref{lem:anisotropic_sobolev_embedding}, since $\frac{d_o}{2s_o}<1$ and $\frac{d_z}{2s_z}<1$, we have $MW^{\theta m_z, \theta m_o}(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})\hookrightarrow L^{\infty}(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})$, with embedding norm a universal constant independent of $n$. By Lemma \ref{lem:embedintosobolevimplies}, we thus have $(L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O}), [\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})})_{\theta,2}\hookrightarrow L^{\infty}(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})$ and \begin{align*} \| (L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O}), [\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O})})_{\theta,2}\hookrightarrow L^{\infty}(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})\| \lesssim \rho^{\theta} \gamma_o^{-\theta m_o}, \end{align*} Next, since we know by Assumption~\ref{assn: technical} that $P_{ZO}$ is equivalent to Lebesgue measure on $\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O}$, \Cref{lem:interpolation_equiv_measure} shows that we have \begin{align} \left(L^2(P_{ZO}), [\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(P_{ZO})}\right)_{\theta,2}\hookrightarrow \left(L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O}), [\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})}\right)_{\theta,2} \hookrightarrow L^{\infty}(P_{ZO})\nonumber, \end{align} and we have \begin{align} \left\|\left(L^2(P_{ZO}), [\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(P_{ZO})}\right)_{\theta,2} \hookrightarrow L^{\infty}(P_{ZO})\right\| \lesssim \rho^{\theta}\gamma_o^{-\theta m_o} \end{align} Finally, by \cite{steinwart2012mercer}[Theorem 4.6], $(L^2(P_{ZO}), [\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(P_{ZO})})_{\theta,2} \cong [\mathcal{H}_{FO}]^{\theta}_{L^2(P_{ZO})}$ with the constant of equivalence depends only on $\theta$. Putting it back to Eq. \eqref{eq: chain_embedding} completes the proof of the proposition.
nodes.statement_short: Chain of embeddings: $\mathcal{H}_{FO}\to$ mixed Sobolev (Lemma C.3), Sobolev interpolation into $L^\infty$ (Lemmas C.5, C.6), change of measure (Lemma C.4).

nodes.name: Embedding norm chain (eq: chain_embedding)
nodes.statement: \left\|\left(L^2(P_{ZO}), [\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(P_{ZO})}\right)_{\theta,2} \hookrightarrow L^{\infty}(P_{ZO})\right\| \lesssim \rho^{\theta}\gamma_o^{-\theta m_o}
nodes.label: eq: chain_embedding

nodes.name: H_FO embeds into the mixed Sobolev space
nodes.statement: Suppose Assumption~\ref{assn: technical} holds, and let $m_z,m_o,\rho$ be as defined in the statement of Assumption~\ref{assn: technical}. We have $[\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})}\hookrightarrow MW^{m_z,m_o}_2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O})$ with \begin{align*} \left\|[\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})}\hookrightarrow MW^{m_z,m_o}_2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})\right\| \lesssim \rho \gamma_o^{-m_o} . \end{align*}
assumptions: Suppose Assumption~\ref{assn: technical} holds, and let $m_z,m_o,\rho$ be as defined in the statement of Assumption~\ref{assn: technical}.
conclusions: $[\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})}\hookrightarrow MW^{m_z,m_o}_2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O})$ with \begin{align*} \left\|[\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})}\hookrightarrow MW^{m_z,m_o}_2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})\right\| \lesssim \rho \gamma_o^{-m_o} . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:hfo_conts_embedding

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.3
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{id}: \mathcal{H}_{FO}\hookrightarrow L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})$ denote the canonical inclusion map. Since we have $(\ker \mathrm{id})^{\perp} \cong [\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})}$, we may represent an arbitrary element of $[\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})}$ as $[f]$, where $f\in (\ker \mathrm{id})^{\perp}$. Moreover, we have $\|[f]\|_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})} = \|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}}$. We fix $f$ for the remainder of the proof. Let $\boldsymbol\alpha \in \mathbb{N}^{d_z}$ with $|\boldsymbol\alpha| \leq m_z$ and $\boldsymbol\beta\in \mathbb{N}^{d_o}$ with $|\boldsymbol\beta| \leq m_o$, we have for any $f\in\mathcal{H}_{FO}$, \begin{small} \begin{align*} &\left\|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta}_{\mathbf o}f\right\|^2_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O};\mathbb{R})} = \int_{\mathcal{Z}}\int_{\mathcal{O}} \left(\partial_{\mathbf z}^{\boldsymbol\alpha}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta}_{\mathbf o}f(\mathbf z,\mathbf o)\right)^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf z\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\ \stackrel{(a)}{=}& \int_{\mathcal{Z}}\int_{\mathcal{O}}\left(\partial_{\mathbf z}^{\boldsymbol\alpha}\partial_{\mathbf o}^{\boldsymbol\beta}\int_{\mathcal{X}} w(\mathbf x,\mathbf o) p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\right)^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf z\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\ \stackrel{(b)}{=}& \int_{\mathcal{Z}}\int_{\mathcal{O}}\left(\sum_{\boldsymbol\beta_1+\boldsymbol\beta_2 = \boldsymbol\beta}\binom{\boldsymbol\beta}{\boldsymbol\beta_1}\int_{\mathcal{X}} \partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}_{\mathbf o} w(\mathbf x,\mathbf o) \partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_2}_{\mathbf o}p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\right)^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf z\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\ \stackrel{(c)}{\leq}& \int_{\mathcal{Z}}\int_{\mathcal{O}}\left(\sum_{\boldsymbol\beta_1+\boldsymbol\beta_2 = \boldsymbol\beta}\binom{\boldsymbol\beta}{\boldsymbol\beta_1}\left(\int_{\mathcal{X}} \left(\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}_{\mathbf o} w(\mathbf x,\mathbf o) \right)^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \left(\int_{\mathcal{X}} \left(\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_2}_{\mathbf o}p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\right)^2 \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf z\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\ \leq & \left(\sum_{\boldsymbol\beta_1+\boldsymbol\beta_2 = \beta}\binom{\boldsymbol\beta}{\boldsymbol\beta_1}\right)^2 \left(\max_{\boldsymbol\beta_2\leq \beta}\sup_{\mathbf x,\mathbf z,\mathbf o}\left|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_2}_{\mathbf o}p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\right|^2\right) \int_{\mathcal{Z}}\int_{\mathcal{O}} \max_{\boldsymbol\beta_1\leq \beta} \int_{\mathcal{X}}\left(\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}_{\mathbf o}w(\mathbf x,\mathbf o)\right)^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf z\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\ =& \left(\sum_{\boldsymbol\beta_1+\boldsymbol\beta_2 = \beta}\binom{\boldsymbol\beta}{\boldsymbol\beta_1}\right)^2 \left(\max_{\boldsymbol\beta_2\leq \beta}\sup_{\mathbf x,\mathbf z,\mathbf o}\left|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_2}_{\mathbf o}p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\right|^2\right) \max_{\boldsymbol\beta_1\leq \beta} \int_{\mathcal{O}}\int_{\mathcal{X}}\left(\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}_{\mathbf o}w(\mathbf x,\mathbf o)\right)^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\ \stackrel{(d)}{=}& c_{m_o, d_o}\left(\max_{\boldsymbol\beta_2\leq \beta}\sup_{\mathbf x,\mathbf z,\mathbf o}\left|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_2}_{\mathbf o}p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\right|^2\right) \gamma_o^{-2|\beta|} \|w\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}^2\\ \leq & c_{m_o,d_o} \left(\max_{\boldsymbol\alpha\leq m_z}\max_{\boldsymbol\beta\leq m_o}\sup_{\mathbf x,\mathbf z,\mathbf o}\left|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta}_{\mathbf o}p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\right|^2\right) \gamma_o^{-2m_o} \|w\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}^2 , \end{align*} \end{small} where $(a)$ follows from the fact that, for any $f\in\mathcal{H}_{FO}$, there exists $w\in\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}$ such that $f(\mathbf z,\mathbf o) = \langle w, F_{\ast}(\mathbf z,\mathbf o)\otimes\phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o)\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} = \int_{\mathcal{X}}w(\mathbf x,\mathbf o)p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x$ and $\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}} = \|w\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}$. $(b)$ follows from generalized Leibniz's rule and differentiation under the integral sign \cite{klenke2013probability}[Theorem 6.28], $(c)$ follows from a Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. $(d)$ follows from the following arguments. From \citet[Theorem 4.21]{steinwart2008support}, we know that for any $w\in \mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}$, there exists $g\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})$ such that \begin{align*} w(\mathbf x,\mathbf o) = \langle g, \Phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x)\Phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o)\rangle_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})},\quad \|w\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} = \|g\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})}, \end{align*} with $\Phi_{\gamma_x}: \mathcal{X}\to L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x}), \Phi_{\gamma_o}: \mathcal{O}\to L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})$ defined in \citet[Lemma 4.45]{steinwart2008support}. We have \begin{align*} &\int_{\mathcal{O}} \int_{\mathcal{X}}\left(\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}_{\mathbf o}w(\mathbf x,\mathbf o)\right)^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\ =& \int_{\mathcal{O}}\int_{\mathcal{X}}\left(\partial_{\mathbf o}^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}} g(\mathbf x',\mathbf o')\Phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x)(\mathbf x')\Phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o)(\mathbf o')\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x'\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o'\right)^{2}\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\ \stackrel{(i)}{=}& \int_{\mathcal{O}}\int_{\mathcal{X}}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}} g(\mathbf x',\mathbf o')\Phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x)(\mathbf x')\partial_{\mathbf o}^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}(\Phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o)(\mathbf o'))\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x'\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o'\right)^{2}\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\ \leq & \|g\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})}\int_{\mathcal{O}}\int_{\mathcal{X}}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}} \left(\Phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x)(\mathbf x')\partial_{\mathbf o}^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}(\Phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o)(\mathbf o'))\right)^{2}\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x'\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o'\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\ = & \|g\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})}\int_{\mathcal{O}}\int_{\mathcal{X}}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x}}(\Phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x)(\mathbf x'))^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x'\right) \left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_o}}\left(\partial_{\mathbf o}^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}(\Phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o)(\mathbf o'))\right)^{2}\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o'\right)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\ \stackrel{(ii)}{=} & \|g\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})}\int_{\mathcal{O}} \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_o}}\left(\partial_{\mathbf o}^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}(\Phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o)(\mathbf o'))\right)^{2}\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o'\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\ \stackrel{(iii)}{\leq} & \|g\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})}c_{\boldsymbol\beta_1, d_o}\gamma_o^{-2|\boldsymbol\beta_1|} \\ = & \|w\|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} c_{\boldsymbol\beta_1, d_o}\gamma_o^{-2|\boldsymbol\beta_1|}, \end{align*} where we're allowed to exchange differentiation and integration in $(i)$ using the differentiation lemma \cite{klenke2013probability}[Theorem 6.28], $(ii)$ follows from the fact that \begin{align*} \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x}}(\Phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x)(\mathbf x'))^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x' = \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x}} \left(\frac{2^{d_x/2}}{\pi^{d_x/4}\gamma_x^{d_x/2}}\exp\left(-2\frac{\|\mathbf x - \mathbf x'\|^2_{2}}{\gamma_x^2}\right)\right)^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x' = 1, \end{align*} and $(iii)$ follows from the proof of \cite{steinwart2008support}[Theorem 4.48]. Here $c_{\boldsymbol\beta_1,d_o}$ is a constant only depending on $\boldsymbol\beta_1,d_o$. Hence we've shown \begin{align*} &\|f\|^2_{MW^{m_z,m_o}_2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O};\mathbb{R})}\\ = & \sum_{\boldsymbol\alpha\leq m_z, \boldsymbol\beta\leq m_o}\left\|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta}_{\mathbf o}f\right\|^2_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O};\mathbb{R})}\\ \lesssim & \sum_{\boldsymbol\alpha \leq m_z, \boldsymbol\beta\leq m_o} \left(\max_{\boldsymbol\alpha\leq m_z}\max_{\boldsymbol\beta\leq m_o}\sup_{\mathbf x,\mathbf z,\mathbf o}\left|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta}_{\mathbf o}p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\right|^2\right) \gamma_o^{-2m_o} \|w\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}^2\\ = & \left(\sum_{\alpha \leq m_z, \boldsymbol\beta\leq m_o} 1\right) \left(\max_{\boldsymbol\alpha\leq m_z}\max_{\boldsymbol\beta\leq m_o}\sup_{\mathbf x,\mathbf z,\mathbf o}\left|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta}_{\mathbf o}p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\right|^2\right) \gamma_o^{-2m_o} \|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}}^2 \\ \lesssim &\rho^2 \gamma_o^{-2m_o} \|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}}^2 \\ = & \rho^2 \gamma_o^{-2m_o} \|[f]\|_{[\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})}}^2 . \end{align*} The second last inequality holds by Assumption \ref{assn: technical}. This concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate under the integral with the Leibniz rule, Cauchy–Schwarz, and bound derivatives of Gaussian feature maps by $\gamma_o^{-|\beta|}$.
