nodes.name: Embedding into Sobolev space implies L-infinity embedding of interpolation spaces
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{Z} = [0,1]^{d}$. Let $\mathcal{H}, W \subseteq L^2(\mathcal{Z})$ be two Hilbert spaces. Suppose that $\mathcal{H} \hookrightarrow W$ with embedding norm $\| \mathcal{H} \hookrightarrow W\| \leq c$. Suppose that $\theta\in(0,1)$ is chosen so that $\left(L^2(\mathcal{Z}), W \right)_{\theta,2} \hookrightarrow L^{\infty}(\mathcal{Z})$ holds. Then we have $\left(L^2(\mathcal{Z}), \mathcal{H}\right)_{\theta,2} \hookrightarrow L^{\infty}(\mathcal{Z})$ with embedding norm $\leq c^{\theta}c_0$, where $c_0$ only depends on $\theta,m$ and $d_z$.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal{Z} = [0,1]^{d}$. Let $\mathcal{H}, W \subseteq L^2(\mathcal{Z})$ be two Hilbert spaces. Suppose that $\mathcal{H} \hookrightarrow W$ with embedding norm $\| \mathcal{H} \hookrightarrow W\| \leq c$. Suppose that $\theta\in(0,1)$ is chosen so that $\left(L^2(\mathcal{Z}), W \right)_{\theta,2} \hookrightarrow L^{\infty}(\mathcal{Z})$ holds.
conclusions: $\left(L^2(\mathcal{Z}), \mathcal{H}\right)_{\theta,2} \hookrightarrow L^{\infty}(\mathcal{Z})$ with embedding norm $\leq c^{\theta}c_0$, where $c_0$ only depends on $\theta,m$ and $d_z$.
nodes.label: lem:embedintosobolevimplies

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.5
nodes.statement: We adapt the proof of \cite{kanagawa2018gaussianprocesseskernelmethods}[Lemma A.2, Corollary 4.13]. We have, for any $x \in (L^2(\mathcal{Z}), W)_{\theta,2}$, \begin{align*} \|x\|_{\left(L^2(\mathcal{Z}), W\right)_{\theta,2}}&= \left(\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(t^{-\theta}K\left(t,x;L^2(\mathcal{Z}),W\right)\right)^{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}t}{t}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\&= \left(\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(t^{-\theta}\inf_{y\in W}\left\{\|x-y\|_{L^2(\mathcal{Z})} + t\|y\|_{W}\right\}\right)^{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}t}{t}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\ &\leq \left(\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(t^{-\theta}\inf_{y\in \mathcal{H}}\left\{\|x-y\|_{L^2(\mathcal{Z})} + t\|y\|_{W}\right\}\right)^{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}t}{t}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\ &\leq \left(\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(t^{-\theta}\inf_{y\in \mathcal{H}}\left\{\|x-y\|_{L^2(\mathcal{Z})} + tc\|y\|_{\mathcal{H}}\right\}\right)^{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}t}{t}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\ &= c^\theta \left(\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(\left(tc \right)^{-\theta}\inf_{y\in \mathcal{H}}\left\{\|x-y\|_{L^2(\mathcal{Z})} + tc \|y\|_{\mathcal{H}}\right\}\right)^{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}t}{t}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\ &= c^{\theta}\left(\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(t^{-\theta}K\left(t,x;L^2(\mathcal{Z}),\mathcal{H}\right)\right)^{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}t}{t}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\ &= c^{\theta}\|x\|_{\left(L^2(\mathcal{Z}), \mathcal{H}\right)_{\theta,2}} . \end{align*} Notice that we correct an error in \cite{kanagawa2018gaussianprocesseskernelmethods} which obtained the exponent $-\theta$ instead of $\theta$ due to an error in the change of variables argument in $(a)$. Now we have proved that $(L^2(\mathcal{Z}), \mathcal{H})_{\theta,2} \hookrightarrow (L^2(\mathcal{Z}), W)_{\theta,2}$ and $\left\| (L^2(\mathcal{Z}), \mathcal{H})_{\theta,2} \hookrightarrow (L^2(\mathcal{Z}), W)_{\theta,2} \right\| \leq c^\theta$. On the other hand, by assumption, we have $(L^2(\mathcal{Z}), W)_{\theta,2} \hookrightarrow L^\infty(\mathcal{Z})$. Consequently, we have $(L^2(\mathcal{Z}), \mathcal{H})_{\theta,2} \hookrightarrow W(L^2(\mathcal{Z}), W)_{\theta,2} \hookrightarrow L^{\infty}(\mathcal{Z})$. The embedding norm is bounded by $c^{\theta}c_0$, where $c_0$ depends only on $\theta$, $m$, and $d_z$.
nodes.statement_short: Compare K-functionals using $\|y\|_W\le c\|y\|_{\mathcal H}$, then compose with the assumed $L^\infty$ embedding.

nodes.name: Mixed Sobolev space embeds into L-infinity
nodes.statement: If $\frac{d_o}{2s_o}< 1 $ and $\frac{d_z}{2s_z} < 1$, then the dominating mixed smoothness Sobolev space $MW^{s_o,s_z}_2([0,1]^{d_o+d_z})$ continuously embeds into $L^{\infty}([0,1]^{d_o+d_z})$.
assumptions: If $\frac{d_o}{2s_o}< 1 $ and $\frac{d_z}{2s_z} < 1$
conclusions: the dominating mixed smoothness Sobolev space $MW^{s_o,s_z}_2([0,1]^{d_o+d_z})$ continuously embeds into $L^{\infty}([0,1]^{d_o+d_z})$.
nodes.label: lem:anisotropic_sobolev_embedding

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma C.6
nodes.statement: See \cite[Equation 1.13]{schmeisser2007recent} for the result where the domain is $\mathbb{R}^{d_z+d_o}$. By \cite{devore1993besov}, there exists a continuous extension operator $\mathcal{E}: MW^{s_o,s_z}_2([0,1]^{d_o+d_z})\to MW^{s_o,s_z}_2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o + d_z})$ such that $\|\mathcal{E}[f]\|_{MW^{s_o,s_z}_2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o+d_z})} \leq C' \|f\|_{MW^{s_o,s_z}_2([0,1]^{d_o+d_z})}$ holds for some universal constant $C^\prime$. Hence, for $f\in MW^{s_o,s_z}_2([0,1]^{d_o+d_z})$, we thus have $\|f\|_{L^{\infty}([0,1]^{d_o+d_z})}\leq \|\mathcal{E}[f]\|_{L^\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{d_o+d_z}) \leq C \|\mathcal{E}[f]\|_{MW^{s_o,s_z}_2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o+d_z})} \leq C' \|f\|_{MW^{s_o,s_z}_2([0,1]^{d_o+d_z})}$, for some universal constants $C,C'>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Known result on $\mathbb{R}^d$ plus a bounded extension operator from the cube.

nodes.name: Interpolation of tensor Sobolev spaces
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{Z}=[0,1]^{d_z}$ and $\mathcal{O} = [0,1]^{d_o}$. The interpolation space $[L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}), W_2^{s_z}(\mathcal{Z}) \otimes W_2^{s_o}(\mathcal{O})]_{\theta,2} \cong W_2^{s_z \theta}(\mathcal{Z}) \otimes W_2^{s_o \theta}(\mathcal{O})$.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal{Z}=[0,1]^{d_z}$ and $\mathcal{O} = [0,1]^{d_o}$.
conclusions: The interpolation space $[L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}), W_2^{s_z}(\mathcal{Z}) \otimes W_2^{s_o}(\mathcal{O})]_{\theta,2} \cong W_2^{s_z \theta}(\mathcal{Z}) \otimes W_2^{s_o \theta}(\mathcal{O})$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition D.1
nodes.statement: From \Cref{prop:T_hat_f_bar_f}, with $P^{n+\tilde{n}}$-probability $\geq 1 - 28e^{-\tau}$, we have \begin{align*} &\left\|T\left(\left[\bar{f}_{\lambda}\right] - \left[\hat{f}_{\lambda}\right]\right)\right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})}\\ &\lesssim \tau \lambda^{-\frac{1}{2}} \underbrace{\left(\frac{\left\|\hat{F}_{\xi}-F_*\right\|_{\mathcal{G}}}{\sqrt{n}}+\left\|F_*-[\hat{F}_{\xi}] \right\|_{L^2\left(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}; \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}\right)} \right)}_{(\ddag)} \left(1 + \|\bar{f}_{\lambda}\|_{\mathcal{H}_{XO, \gamma_x, \gamma_0}}\right) . \end{align*} By \Cref{lem:f_bar_lambda_norm_bound}, we have with $P^n$-probability $\geq 1 - 2e^{-\tau}$ \begin{align*} \|\bar{f}_{\lambda}\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}\lesssim \tau n^{\frac{1}{2}\frac{1 + \frac{d_o}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1 + (2 + \frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x} + \eta_1)}}. \end{align*} Under the probabilistic event that \Cref{prop:T_hat_f_bar_f} holds, the bounds in \Cref{prop:cme_rate} also hold, so we have \begin{align*} \left\|\left[\hat{F}_\xi \right]-F_*\right\|_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}; \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x})} \leq J \tau \tilde{n}^{-\frac{1}{2}\frac{m^{\dag}}{m^{\dag} + d^{\dag}/2 + \zeta}} , \quad \left\| \hat{F}_\xi -F_*\right\|_{\mathcal{G}} \leq J \tau \tilde{n}^{-\frac{1}{2}\frac{m^{\dag} - 1}{m^{\dag} + d^{\dag}/2 + \zeta}} , \end{align*} hold for any $\zeta > 0$. $J$ is some constant independent of $\tilde{n}, n$. Thus under this probabilistic event, a sufficient condition so that $(\ddag)\lesssim \frac{1}{n}$ is given by \begin{align*} \tilde{n} \geq (J\tau n)^{2\frac{m^{\dag}+d^{\dag}/2+\zeta}{m^{\dag}}} \vee (J^2\tau^2n)^{\frac{m^{\dag} + d^{\dag}/2 + \zeta}{m^{\dag} - 1}}. \end{align*} This is satisfied since $\tilde{n}$ satisfies Eq. \eqref{eq:m_sufficient_large}. Hence, \begin{align} \left\|\left[\hat{F}_\xi \right]-F_*\right\|_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}; \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x})} \leq n^{-1} , \quad \left\| \hat{F}_\xi - F_*\right\|_{\mathcal{G}} \leq n^{-\frac{1}{2}} . \end{align} By the union bound, we have that with $P^{n+\tilde{n}}$-probability $\geq 1 - 30 e^{-\tau}$, the following bound holds \begin{align*} \left\|T\left(\left[\bar{f}_{\lambda}\right] - \left[\hat{f}_{\lambda}\right]\right)\right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} \lesssim \tau n^{-\frac{\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}. \end{align*} Hence the proof is concluded.
nodes.section: D Proof of Theorem~4.1 in the main text
nodes.statement_short: Combine Prop. D.3 with the RKHS-norm bound of Prop. D.6 and CME rates (Prop. D.4); choose $\tilde n$ large and take a union bound.

nodes.name: Sufficient condition on Stage I size
nodes.statement: \left\|\left[\hat{F}_\xi \right]-F_*\right\|_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}; \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x})} \leq n^{-1} , \quad \left\| \hat{F}_\xi - F_*\right\|_{\mathcal{G}} \leq n^{-\frac{1}{2}} .

nodes.name: Projected Stage II error bound
nodes.statement: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:T_contractivity}, \ref{ass:T_frequency_ill_posedness}, \ref{ass:T_injective}, \ref{ass:f_ast}, \ref{assn: technical} hold. Let $\lambda \asymp n^{-1}$ and \begin{align*} \gamma_x = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{d_x}}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}, \quad \gamma_o = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}. \end{align*} Then, with $P^n$-probability $\geq 1- 4e^{-\tau}$, for sufficiently large $n\geq 1$, we have \begin{align*} \left\|T\left(f_{\ast} - \left[\bar{f}_{\lambda}\right]\right)\right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} \leq 2C\tau (\log n)^{\frac{d_x+d_o+1}{2}} n^{-\frac{\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}} \end{align*} for some constant $C>0$ independent of $n$.
nodes.section: D Proof of Theorem~4.1 in the main text
assumptions: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:T_contractivity}, \ref{ass:T_frequency_ill_posedness}, \ref{ass:T_injective}, \ref{ass:f_ast}, \ref{assn: technical} hold. Let $\lambda \asymp n^{-1}$ and \begin{align*} \gamma_x = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{d_x}}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}, \quad \gamma_o = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}. \end{align*}
conclusions: with $P^n$-probability $\geq 1- 4e^{-\tau}$, for sufficiently large $n\geq 1$, we have \begin{align*} \left\|T\left(f_{\ast} - \left[\bar{f}_{\lambda}\right]\right)\right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} \leq 2C\tau (\log n)^{\frac{d_x+d_o+1}{2}} n^{-\frac{\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}} \end{align*} for some constant $C>0$ independent of $n$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition D.2
nodes.statement: The proposition is proved through the following triangular inequality \begin{align*} \left\|T\left(f_{\ast} - \left[\bar{f}_{\lambda}\right]\right)\right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} &\leq \left\|T\left(f_{\ast} - \left[f_{\lambda}\right]\right)\right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} + \left\|T\left(\left[\bar{f}_{\lambda}\right] - [f_{\lambda}]\right)\right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} \\ &\leq n^{-\frac{\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}} + n^{-\frac{\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}} (\log n)^{\frac{d_x+d_o+1}{2}} \\ &\leq 2 n^{-\frac{\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}} (\log n)^{\frac{d_x+d_o+1}{2}}. \end{align*} The second last inequality holds by using \Cref{prop: approx_error} for the first term and \Cref{prop: projected_est_error} for the second term, which holds with $P^n$-probability $\geq 1- 4e^{-\tau}$.

nodes.name: Stage I error in terms of CME error
nodes.statement: Fix $\tau\geq 1$. Suppose that the assumptions of \Cref{prop:cme_rate} hold. Suppose that $n > A_{\lambda,\tau}$ with $A_{\lambda,\tau}$ defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:FS_thm_16_const}, and $\tilde{n} \geq 1$ satisfies Eq. \eqref{eq:m_sufficient_large} in the main text. We have with $P^{n+\tilde{n}}$-probability $\geq 1 - 28e^{-\tau}$, the following inequality holds \begin{align*} &\left\|T [\hat{f}_{\lambda}] - T [\bar{f}_{\lambda}] \right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})}\\ &\lesssim \tau \lambda^{-\frac{1}{2}} \left(\frac{\left\|\hat{F}_{\xi}-F_*\right\|_{\mathcal{G}}}{\sqrt{n}}+\left\|\left[F_*-\hat{F}_{\xi}\right]\right\|_{L^2\left(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}; \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}\right)}\right) \left(1 + \|\bar{f}_{\lambda}\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}\right). \end{align*} Under the same probabilistic event, the bounds in \Cref{prop:cme_rate} also hold.
assumptions: Fix $\tau\geq 1$. Suppose that the assumptions of \Cref{prop:cme_rate} hold. Suppose that $n > A_{\lambda,\tau}$ with $A_{\lambda,\tau}$ defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:FS_thm_16_const}, and $\tilde{n} \geq 1$ satisfies Eq. \eqref{eq:m_sufficient_large} in the main text.
conclusions: $P^{n+\tilde{n}}$-probability $\geq 1 - 28e^{-\tau}$, the following inequality holds \begin{align*} &\left\|T [\hat{f}_{\lambda}] - T [\bar{f}_{\lambda}] \right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})}\\ &\lesssim \tau \lambda^{-\frac{1}{2}} \left(\frac{\left\|\hat{F}_{\xi}-F_*\right\|_{\mathcal{G}}}{\sqrt{n}}+\left\|\left[F_*-\hat{F}_{\xi}\right]\right\|_{L^2\left(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}; \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}\right)}\right) \left(1 + \|\bar{f}_{\lambda}\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}\right). \end{align*} Under the same probabilistic event, the bounds in \Cref{prop:cme_rate} also hold.
nodes.label: prop:T_hat_f_bar_f

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition D.3
nodes.statement: We find \begin{align*} &\left\|T [\hat{f}_{\lambda}] - T [\bar{f}_{\lambda}] \right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} = \left\|[\hat{h}_{\lambda}] - [\bar{h}_{\lambda}] \right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} \leq \left\|C_{FO}^{\frac{1}{2}}\left(\hat{h}_{\lambda} - \bar{h}_{\lambda}\right)\right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}} . \end{align*} The last step follows from Lemma 12 of \cite{fischer2020sobolev}. We can proceed by plugging in the closed form expressions from Eq.~\eqref{eq:closed_form_h_lambdas} to have \begin{small} \begin{align*} &\left\|C_{FO}^{\frac{1}{2}}\left(\hat{h}_{\lambda} - \bar{h}_{\lambda}\right)\right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}}\\ = & \left\|C_{FO}^{\frac{1}{2}}\left(\left(\hat{C}_{\hat{F}O} + \lambda\right)^{-1}\frac{1}{n}\boldsymbol{\Phi}_{\hat{F}O}^{\ast}\mathbf Y - \left(\hat{C}_{FO} + \lambda\right)^{-1}\frac{1}{n}\boldsymbol{\Phi}_{FO}^{\ast}\mathbf Y\right)\right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}}\\ \leq & \left\|C_{FO}^{\frac{1}{2}}(C_{FO} + \lambda)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right\|\cdot \left\|(C_{FO} + \lambda)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left(\left(\hat{C}_{\hat{F}O} + \lambda\right)^{-1}\frac{1}{n}\boldsymbol{\Phi}_{\hat{F}O}^{\ast}\mathbf Y - \left(\hat{C}_{FO} + \lambda\right)^{-1}\frac{1}{n}\boldsymbol{\Phi}_{FO}^{\ast}\mathbf Y\right)\right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}}\\ \leq & \left\|(C_{FO} + \lambda)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left(\left(\hat{C}_{\hat{F}O} + \lambda\right)^{-1}\frac{1}{n}\boldsymbol{\Phi}_{\hat{F}O}^{\ast}\mathbf Y - \left(\hat{C}_{FO} + \lambda\right)^{-1}\frac{1}{n}\boldsymbol{\Phi}_{FO}^{\ast}\mathbf Y\right)\right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}}\\ \leq & S_{-1} + S_{0}, \end{align*} \end{small} where we define \begin{align*} S_{-1} &:= \left\|(C_{FO} + \lambda)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left(\hat{C}_{\hat{F}O} + \lambda\right)^{-1} \frac{1}{n}\left(\boldsymbol{\Phi}_{\hat{F}O} - \boldsymbol{\Phi}_{FO}\right)^{\ast}\mathbf Y\right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}}\\ S_0 &= \left\|(C_{FO} + \lambda)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left(\hat{C}_{\hat{F}O} + \lambda\right)^{-1}\left(\hat{C}_{FO} - \hat{C}_{\hat{F}O}\right) \left(\hat{C}_{FO} + \lambda\right)^{-1}\frac{1}{n}\boldsymbol{\Phi}_{FO}^{\ast}\mathbf Y\right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}} \end{align*} We bound $S_{-1}$ with $P^{n+\tilde{n}}$-high probability by \Cref{lem:thm11_meunier} and $S_{0}$ in $P^{n+\tilde{n}}$-high probability by \Cref{lem:thm12_meunier}. We thus have, with $P^{n+\tilde{n}}$-probability $\geq 1 - 28e^{-\tau}$, the following bound \begin{align*} &\quad \left\|C_{FO}^{\frac{1}{2}}\left(\hat{h}_{\lambda} - \bar{h}_{\lambda}\right)\right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}} \\ &\leq c \tau\sqrt{n}\left(\frac{\left\| \hat{F}_{\xi} -F_\ast \right\|_{\mathcal{G}}}{\sqrt{n}} + \left\| \left[\hat{F}_\xi -F_*\right] \right\|_{L^2\left(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}; \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}\right)}\right)\left(\|\bar{h}_\lambda\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}} + 1\right). \end{align*} $\|\bar{h}_\lambda\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}} = \|\bar{f}_{\lambda}\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}$ since $V$ is a metric surjection.
nodes.statement_short: Write the Stage I error via closed forms of $\hat h_\lambda,\bar h_\lambda$ and bound the two resulting terms with Lemmas D.2 and D.3.

nodes.name: Learning rate for the conditional mean embedding (CME rate)
nodes.statement: Suppose Assumption \ref{assn: technical} in the main text holds. Suppose $k_{\mathcal{O}}: \mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{O} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $k_{\mathcal{Z}}: \mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$ are Mat\'{e}rn reproducing kernels whose RKHSs $\mathcal{H}_O$ and $\mathcal{H}_Z$ are norm equivalent to $W_2^{t_o}(\mathcal{O})$ and $W_2^{t_z}(\mathcal{Z})$ with $m_o > t_o > d_o/2$, $m_z > t_z > d_z/2$ and $\frac{m_z}{t_z} \wedge \frac{m_o}{t_o} \leq 2$. Define $m^{\dag}=(m_z t_z^{-1}) \wedge (m_o t_o^{-1})$ and $d^{\dag}= (d_z t_z^{-1}) \vee(d_o t_o^{-1})$. For $\zeta > 0$ arbitrarily small, we take $\xi = \tilde{n}^{-\frac{1}{m^{\dag} + d^{\dag}/2 + \zeta}}$, then with $P^{\tilde{n}}$-probability at least $1- 4e^{-\tau}$, we have \begin{align*} \left\|\left[\hat{F}_\xi -F_*\right]\right\|_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}; \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x})} \leq J\tau \tilde{n}^{-\frac{1}{2}\frac{ m^{\dag}}{m^{\dag} + d^{\dag}/2 + \zeta}} , \quad \left\|\hat{F}_\xi -F_*\right\|_{\mathcal{G}} \leq J \tau \tilde{n}^{-\frac{1}{2}\frac{m^{\dag} - 1}{m^{\dag} + d^{\dag}/2 + \zeta}} . \end{align*} $J$ is a constant independent of $\tilde{n}$.
assumptions: Suppose Assumption \ref{assn: technical} in the main text holds. Suppose $k_{\mathcal{O}}: \mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{O} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $k_{\mathcal{Z}}: \mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$ are Mat\'{e}rn reproducing kernels whose RKHSs $\mathcal{H}_O$ and $\mathcal{H}_Z$ are norm equivalent to $W_2^{t_o}(\mathcal{O})$ and $W_2^{t_z}(\mathcal{Z})$ with $m_o > t_o > d_o/2$, $m_z > t_z > d_z/2$ and $\frac{m_z}{t_z} \wedge \frac{m_o}{t_o} \leq 2$. Define $m^{\dag}=(m_z t_z^{-1}) \wedge (m_o t_o^{-1})$ and $d^{\dag}= (d_z t_z^{-1}) \vee(d_o t_o^{-1})$. For $\zeta > 0$ arbitrarily small, we take $\xi = \tilde{n}^{-\frac{1}{m^{\dag} + d^{\dag}/2 + \zeta}}$,
conclusions: $P^{\tilde{n}}$-probability at least $1- 4e^{-\tau}$, we have \begin{align*} \left\|\left[\hat{F}_\xi -F_*\right]\right\|_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}; \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x})} \leq J\tau \tilde{n}^{-\frac{1}{2}\frac{ m^{\dag}}{m^{\dag} + d^{\dag}/2 + \zeta}} , \quad \left\|\hat{F}_\xi -F_*\right\|_{\mathcal{G}} \leq J \tau \tilde{n}^{-\frac{1}{2}\frac{m^{\dag} - 1}{m^{\dag} + d^{\dag}/2 + \zeta}} . \end{align*} $J$ is a constant independent of $\tilde{n}$.
nodes.statement_short: With Matérn Stage I kernels and $\xi=\tilde n^{-1/(m^\dagger+d^\dagger/2+\zeta)}$, the CME estimator converges in $L^2$ and in $\mathcal{G}$-norm at the stated rates.
nodes.label: prop:cme_rate

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition D.4
nodes.statement: We are going to apply \citet[Theorem 3]{JMLR:v25:23-1663} to obtain the desired result. To this end, we need to verify the assumptions (EVD) and (SRC) made in \cite{JMLR:v25:23-1663}. Note that we let the assumption (EMB) of \cite{JMLR:v25:23-1663} be trivially verified with $\alpha = 1$, as we prove in \Cref{prop:F_ast_sobolev} that $F_{\ast} \in [\mathcal{G}]^\beta$ with $\beta > 1$, therefore $\beta + p > 1 + p > 1 = \alpha$ falls in Case 2 of Theorem 3 of \cite{JMLR:v25:23-1663}. \vspace{3mm} \noindent \underline{\textit{Verification of (EVD)}} Let $\phi_{Z}$ (resp. $\phi_{O}$) denote the feature map of $\mathcal{H}_{Z}$ (resp. $\mathcal{H}_{O}$). Define $C_{ZO}:\mathcal{H}_Z \otimes \mathcal{H}_O \to \mathcal{H}_Z \otimes \mathcal{H}_O$ as the covariance operator. \begin{align*} C_{ZO} = \iint_{\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}} (\phi_Z(\mathbf z) \otimes \phi_O(\mathbf o)) \otimes (\phi_Z(\mathbf z) \otimes \phi_O(\mathbf o)) p_{ZO}(\mathbf z, \mathbf o) \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf z \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o . \end{align*} We also define another two auxiliary covariance operators $\bar{C}_Z:\mathcal{H}_Z\to \mathcal{H}_Z$ and $\bar{C}_O:\mathcal{H}_O\to \mathcal{H}_O$. \begin{align*} \bar{C}_Z = \int_{\mathcal{Z}} \phi_Z(\mathbf z) \otimes \phi_Z(\mathbf z) p_ {Z}(\mathbf z)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf z, \quad \bar{C}_O = \int_{\mathcal{O}} \phi_O(\mathbf o) \otimes \phi_O(\mathbf o)p_O(\mathbf o)\; \mathrm{d}\mathbf o . \end{align*} Since $k_Z$ and $k_O$ are bounded, $C_{ZO}, \bar{C}_Z, \bar{C}_O$ are all self-adjoint compact operators. From \cite{edmunds1996function} and \cite{fischer2020sobolev}[Section 4], we have $\lambda_i(\bar{C}_Z) \asymp i^{-2 t_z/d_z}$ and $\lambda_i(\bar{C}_O) \asymp i^{-2 t_o/d_o}$. We know from Assumption \ref{assn: technical} that $P_{ZO}$ is equivalent to the Lebesgue measure, so by Jensen's inequality, we have $C_{ZO} \leq \bar{C}_Z \otimes \bar{C}_O$, where $\otimes$ here denotes an operator tensor product. Hence, from Lemma 17 of \cite{meunier2024nonparametricinstrumentalregressionkernel} we have $\lambda_i(C_{ZO}) \leq \lambda_i(\bar{C}_Z \otimes \bar{C}_O)$. Finally, from \Cref{lem:tensor_evd} we have \begin{align*} \lambda_i(C_{ZO}) \leq \lambda_i(\bar{C}_Z \otimes \bar{C}_O) \lesssim i^{-2 t_z/d_z \wedge 2 t_o/d_o + \zeta} \end{align*} for any $\zeta > 0$. Therefore, we have proved that (EVD) hold with $1/p = 2 t_z/d_z \wedge 2 t_o/d_o - \zeta$. Hence, $p = d^{\dag}/2 + \zeta$ for any $\zeta > 0$. \vspace{3mm} \noindent \underline{\textit{Verification of (SRC)}} Let $\beta = m^{\dag}$. By the definition of vector-valued interpolation space in \cite{JMLR:v25:23-1663}[Definition 2] and the Assumption that $P_{ZO}$ is equivalent to the Lebesgue measure, we have that \begin{align*} [\mathcal{G}]^{\beta} &\cong \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x} \otimes [L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}), \mathcal{H}_Z \otimes \mathcal{H}_O]_{\beta, 2} \\ &\stackrel{(a)}{\cong} \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x} \otimes [L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}), W^{t_z}_2(\mathcal{Z}) \otimes W^{t_o}_2(\mathcal{O})]_{\beta, 2} \\ &\stackrel{(b)}{\cong} \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x} \otimes W^{t_z \beta}_2(\mathcal{Z}) \otimes W^{t_o \beta}_2(\mathcal{O})\\ &\stackrel{(\ast)}{\supseteq} \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}\otimes W^{m_z}_2(\mathcal{Z}) \otimes W^{m_o}_2(\mathcal{O})\\ &\stackrel{(c)}{\cong} \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}\otimes MW^{m_z,m_o}_{2}(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O};\mathbb{R})\\ &\stackrel{(d)}{\cong} MW^{m_z,m_o}_{2}(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O};\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}). \end{align*} where in $(a)$ we use Corollary 10.13 and Theorem 10.46 of \cite{wendland2004scattered}, in $(b)$ we use \Cref{lem:tensor_interpolation}, in $(c)$ we use proposition 3.1 of \cite{SICKEL2009748}, which shows $MW^{m_z, m_o}_2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}) \cong W^{m_z}_2(\mathcal{Z}) \otimes W^{m_o}_2(\mathcal{O})$, and in $(d)$ we use \Cref{lem:vv_mss}. Furthermore, the inclusion in $(\ast)$ is a continuous embedding. We show in \Cref{prop:F_ast_sobolev} that under \Cref{assn: technical}, $\|F_{\ast}\|_{MW^{m_z,m_o}_{2}(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O};\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x})}$ is bounded by a constant. Hence we deduce from the above embedding that \begin{align} F_{\ast}\in [\mathcal{G}]^{\beta}, \quad \beta = m^{\dag} = \frac{m_z}{t_z} \wedge \frac{m_o}{t_o}. \end{align} Hence $\|F_{\ast}\|_{[\mathcal{G}]^{\beta}} \leq C$ for some constant $C>0$. Hence $F_{\ast}$ satisfies (SRC) in \cite{JMLR:v25:23-1663} with $\beta=m^{\dag}$. Now we use Case 2 in Theorem 3 of \cite{JMLR:v25:23-1663} to obtain the following result: if we take $\xi = \tilde{n}^{-\frac{1}{m^{\dag} + d^{\dag}/2 + \zeta}}$, then for any $0\leq \gamma < m^{\dag}$, the following bound on the $\gamma$-norm \begin{align*} \left\|\left[\hat{F}_\xi -F_*\right]\right\|_{\gamma}^2 \leq \tau^2 \tilde{n}^{-\frac{m^{\dag} - \gamma}{m^{\dag} + d^{\dag}/2 + \zeta}} . \end{align*} holds with $P^{\tilde{n}}$-probability at least $1 - 4e^{-\tau}$. Therefore, noting that $m^{\dag}> 1$, by taking $\gamma=0$ and $\gamma=1$, we obtain with $P^{\tilde{n}}$-probability at least $1 - 4e^{-\tau}$, \begin{align*} \left\|\left[\hat{F}_\xi -F_*\right]\right\|_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}; \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x})} \leq \tau \tilde{n}^{-\frac{1}{2}\frac{m^{\dag}}{m^{\dag} + d^{\dag}/2 + \zeta}} , \quad \left\|\hat{F}_\xi -F_*\right\|_{\mathcal{G}} \leq \tau \tilde{n}^{-\frac{1}{2}\frac{m^{\dag} - 1}{m^{\dag} + d^{\dag}/2 + \zeta}} . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the vector-valued KRR rate of Li et al. (Theorem 3) after verifying eigenvalue decay (EVD) via tensor products and the source condition (SRC) via mixed Sobolev regularity.

nodes.name: Embedding chain for (SRC) verification
nodes.statement: F_{\ast}\in [\mathcal{G}]^{\beta}, \quad \beta = m^{\dag} = \frac{m_z}{t_z} \wedge \frac{m_o}{t_o}.

nodes.name: Mixed Sobolev norm of the CME

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition D.5
nodes.statement: Notice that, by definition of $F_{\ast}$, \begin{align*} \|F_{\ast}\|_{MW^{m_z, m_o}_2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O};\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x})} &= \left\|\int_{\mathcal{X}} \phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x)p(\mathbf x|\cdot, \cdot)\;\mathrm{d} \mathbf x \right\|_{MW^{m_z, m_o}_2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O};\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x})} \\ &\leq \int_{\mathcal{X}} \left\|\phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x)p(\mathbf x|\cdot,\cdot )\right\|_{MW^{m_z, m_o}_2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O};\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x})}\;\mathrm{d} \mathbf x . \end{align*} In the last inequality above, we use \cite{Hytönen2016AnalysisBanachSpaces}[Proposition 1.2.11]. Next, notice that \begin{align*} &\quad \left\|\phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x) p(\mathbf x \mid \cdot,\cdot)\right\|_{MW^{m_z, m_o}_2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O};\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x})}^2 \\ &= \sum_{|\boldsymbol\alpha|\leq m_z} \sum_{|\boldsymbol\beta|\leq m_o} \int_{\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}} \left\|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z} \partial^{\boldsymbol\beta}_{\mathbf o} \left(\phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x) p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z, \mathbf o) \right) \right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}}^2 \;\mathrm{d} \mathbf z \;\mathrm{d} \mathbf o \\ &= \sum_{|\boldsymbol\alpha|\leq m_z} \sum_{|\boldsymbol\beta|\leq m_o} \int_{\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}} \left\|\phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x) \partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z} \partial^{\boldsymbol\beta}_{\mathbf o} p(\mathbf x \mid \mathbf z, \mathbf o) \right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}}^2 \;\mathrm{d} \mathbf z \;\mathrm{d} \mathbf o \\ &\leq \sum_{|\boldsymbol\alpha|\leq m_z} \sum_{|\boldsymbol\beta|\leq m_o} \int_{\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O}} \left|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z} \partial^{\boldsymbol\beta}_{\mathbf o} p(\mathbf x| \mathbf z, \mathbf o) \right|^2 \;\mathrm{d} \mathbf z \;\mathrm{d} \mathbf o \\ &\leq \binom{m_z + d_z -1}{d_z -1} \binom{m_o + d_o-1}{d_o -1} \rho^2 . \end{align*} In the last step, $\binom{m_z + d_z -1}{d_z -1}$ shows up as the evaluation of $\sum_{|\boldsymbol\alpha| \leq m_z} 1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition D.6
nodes.statement: Fix $p>0$. We combine the results of \Cref{prop: approx_error} with the inequality immediately preceding this proposition to find, for $\hat{\rho}\geq 1$, there exists a constant $C_1, C_2, C_3$ independent of $\lambda, M_n, n, \gamma_x, \gamma_o, B, V, \hat{\rho}$ such that , with probability $\geq 1 - 5e^{-\hat{\rho}}$ the following bound holds \begin{align*} &\quad \lambda \|\bar{f}_{\lambda}\|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{XO}} \\ &\stackrel{(a)}{\leq} C_1\hat{\rho}\left(\lambda \|f_{\lambda}\|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{XO}} + \|T(f_{\lambda} - f_{\ast})\|^2_{L^2(P_{ZO})} + M_n^{2+2p}\left(\frac{\max\{4, \tilde{c}_p\}^{2p}\gamma_x^{-d_x}\gamma_o^{-d_o}}{\lambda^{p}n}\right) + \frac{M_n^2}{n}\right)\\ &\stackrel{(b)}{\leq} C_2\hat{\rho}\left(n^{-\frac{2(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}} + M_n^{2+2p}\left(\frac{\max\{4, \tilde{c}_p\}^{2p}\gamma_x^{-d_x}\gamma_o^{-d_o}}{\lambda^{p}n}\right) + \frac{M_n^2}{n}\right)\\ &\stackrel{(c)}{=} C_2\hat{\rho}\left(n^{-\frac{2(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}\left(1 + M_n^{2+2p}\frac{\max\{4, \tilde{c}_p\}^{2p}}{\lambda^{p}}\right) + \frac{M_n^2}{n}\right)\\ &\stackrel{(d)}{\leq}C_3 \hat{\rho}n^{-\frac{2(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}} n^{2p}. \end{align*} In the above derivations, $(a)$ holds by $\lambda=n^{-1}$, $(b)$ holds by the conclusion of \Cref{prop: approx_error}, $(c)$ holds by the choice of $\gamma_x,\gamma_o$ as functions of $n$, $(d)$ holds \emph{for sufficiently large $n\geq 1$}, since $p$ is fixed and $n^{p} > M_n^{2+2p} = \left(1 + \sigma\sqrt{\frac{\ln n + \hat{\rho}}{c}}\right)^{2+2p}$ for sufficiently large $n\geq 1$, and $n^{-\frac{2(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}} \geq \frac{M_n^2}{n}$ for sufficiently large $n\geq 1$. In particular, the constant $C_3$ depends on $p$.

nodes.name: Vector-valued mixed Sobolev space as a tensor product
nodes.statement: Let $\Omega_1,\Omega_2$ be two open sets in $\mathbb{R}^{n_1}$ and $\mathbb{R}^{n_2}$ respectively. Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a Hilbert space. Then we have \begin{align*} MW^{m,p}(\Omega_1\times \Omega_2, \mathcal{H}) \cong W^{m}(\Omega_1, W^{p}(\Omega_2,\mathcal{H})) \cong W^m(\Omega_1)\otimes W^p(\Omega_2)\otimes \mathcal{H} \end{align*}
assumptions: Let $\Omega_1,\Omega_2$ be two open sets in $\mathbb{R}^{n_1}$ and $\mathbb{R}^{n_2}$ respectively. Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a Hilbert space.
conclusions: \begin{align*} MW^{m,p}(\Omega_1\times \Omega_2, \mathcal{H}) \cong W^{m}(\Omega_1, W^{p}(\Omega_2,\mathcal{H})) \cong W^m(\Omega_1)\otimes W^p(\Omega_2)\otimes \mathcal{H} \end{align*}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma D.1
nodes.statement: We adapt the proof of \cite{aubin2011applied}[Theorem 12.7.2]. Let $f\in W^{m}(\Omega_1, W^{p}(\Omega_2,\mathcal{H}))$. Then $f\in L^2(\Omega_1, W^p(\Omega_2,\mathcal{H}))$ such that $\partial_1^{\alpha}f\in L^2(\Omega_1, W^p(\Omega_2,\mathcal{H}))$ for $|\alpha|\leq m$. As explained in \cite{Hytönen2016AnalysisBanachSpaces}[Definition 2.5.1], to say that $\partial_1^{\alpha}f\in L^2(\Omega_1, W^p(\Omega_2,\mathcal{H}))$ is equivalent to saying that for every $\phi \in C^{\infty}_{c}(\Omega_1)$, we have \begin{align} \int_{\Omega_1}f(x,\cdot)\partial^{\alpha}_{1}\phi(x)\;\mathrm{d}x = (-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_{\Omega_1}(\partial^{\alpha}_{1}f)(x,\cdot)\phi(x)\;\mathrm{d}x \end{align} belongs to $W^p(\Omega_2,\mathcal{H})$. But this exactly says that $f\in MW^{m,p}(\Omega_1\times \Omega_2,\mathcal{H})$. Thus the first isometric isomorphism is proved. The second isomorphism is proved by two successive applications of \citet[Theorem 12.7.1]{aubin2011applied}, namely the fact that the Hilbert-space valued Sobolev space $W^m(\Omega,\mathcal{H})$ is isometrically isomorphic to the Hilbertian tensor product $W^m(\Omega)\otimes \mathcal{H}$.
nodes.statement_short: Characterise vector-valued weak derivatives (Hytönen) to identify the iterated Sobolev space, then use tensor-product identification.

nodes.name: Vector-valued weak derivative identity (eq:vv_weak)
nodes.statement: \int_{\Omega_1}f(x,\cdot)\partial^{\alpha}_{1}\phi(x)\;\mathrm{d}x = (-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_{\Omega_1}(\partial^{\alpha}_{1}f)(x,\cdot)\phi(x)\;\mathrm{d}x

nodes.name: Eigenvalue decay of tensor product operators
nodes.statement: Suppose the eigenvalues of the operator $\Sigma_1$ satisfy $\mu_{1, i} \asymp i^{-1/p_1}$ and the eigenvalues of the operator $\Sigma_2$ satisfy $\mu_{2, i} \asymp i^{-1/p_2}$. Then the eigenvalues of their tensor product $\Sigma_1 \otimes \Sigma_2$ satisfy, for any $\zeta > 0$, \begin{align*} \lambda_{i}(\Sigma_1 \otimes \Sigma_2) \leq i^{- 1/ p_1 \wedge 1/ p_2 + \zeta}. \end{align*}
assumptions: Suppose the eigenvalues of the operator $\Sigma_1$ satisfy $\mu_{1, i} \asymp i^{-1/p_1}$ and the eigenvalues of the operator $\Sigma_2$ satisfy $\mu_{2, i} \asymp i^{-1/p_2}$.
conclusions: the eigenvalues of their tensor product $\Sigma_1 \otimes \Sigma_2$ satisfy, for any $\zeta > 0$, \begin{align*} \lambda_{i}(\Sigma_1 \otimes \Sigma_2) \leq i^{- 1/ p_1 \wedge 1/ p_2 + \zeta}. \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:tensor_evd

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma D.4
nodes.statement: Suppose $\left( \mu_{1, i} \right)_{i \in \mathbb{N}^+}$ (resp. $\left( \mu_{2, j} \right)_{j \in \mathbb{N}^+}$) are the eigenvalues of $\Sigma_1$ (resp. $\Sigma_2$) with corresponding eigenfunctions $\left( q_{1, i} \right)_{i \in \mathbb{N}^+}$ (resp. $\left( q_{2, j} \right)_{j \in \mathbb{N}^+}$). By definition of operator tensor product, we have \begin{align*} \left( \Sigma_1 \otimes \Sigma_2 \right) (q_{1, i} \otimes q_{2, j} ) = \left( \Sigma_1 q_{1, i} \right) \otimes \left( \Sigma_2 q_{2, j} \right) = \mu_{1, i} \mu_{2, j} (q_{1, i} \otimes q_{2, j} ) . \end{align*} Therefore, for any $i \in \mathbb{N}^+, j \in \mathbb{N}^+$ we obtain that $\mu_{1, i} \cdot \mu_{2, j}$ is the eigenvalue of $\Sigma_1 \otimes_{op} \Sigma_2$ with corresponding eigenfunction $q_{1, i} \otimes q_{2, j}$. Therefore the eigenvalues of $\Sigma_1 \otimes_{op} \Sigma_2$ equal the tensor product of two sequences $(\mu_{1, i})_{i\in \mathbb{N}^+}$ and $(\mu_{2, j})_{j \in \mathbb{N}^+}$. Without loss of generality, we assume $p_1 \leq p_2$ so that $\mu_{1, i} \leq \mu_{2, i}$ for $i$ large enough. Denote $(\sigma_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}^+}$ as the tensor product of two sequences $(\mu_{2, i})_{i\in \mathbb{N}^+}$ and $(\mu_{2, j})_{j \in \mathbb{N}^+}$ rearranged in a non-increasing order. Hence, we have $\lambda_{n}(\Sigma_1 \otimes \Sigma_2) \leq \sigma_n$. From \cite{krieg2018tensor}, we have \begin{align*} \sigma_n \leq n^{- 1/p_2} (\log n)^{1/p_2} \leq n^{- 1/p_2 + \zeta}, \end{align*} for any $\zeta > 0$. It concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Eigenvalues of a tensor product are products of eigenvalues; bound the reordered product sequence with Krieg (2018).

nodes.name: Approximation error of anisotropic convolution for Besov functions
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{X} = [0,1]^d$. Let $f : \mathbb{R}^{d} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $f \in B_{2,q}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathcal{X}) \cap L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with $\boldsymbol{s} = [s_1, \ldots, s_d]^\top$. Recall $K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}$ defined in Eq. \eqref{eq:K_function} with $\boldsymbol{\gamma} = [\gamma_1, \ldots, \gamma_d]^\top \in (0,1]^d$. Then, we have \begin{align*} \left\|\left[K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}\ast f\right] - f\right\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})} \leq C_0 |f|_{B_{2,q}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathcal{X})} \cdot \max\{\gamma_1^{s_1}, \ldots, \gamma_d^{s_d}\} \end{align*} for some constant $C_0$ that only depends on $d, \boldsymbol{s}$.
assumptions: Let $\mathcal{X} = [0,1]^d$. Let $f : \mathbb{R}^{d} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $f \in B_{2,q}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathcal{X}) \cap L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with $\boldsymbol{s} = [s_1, \ldots, s_d]^\top$. Recall $K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}$ defined in Eq. \eqref{eq:K_function} with $\boldsymbol{\gamma} = [\gamma_1, \ldots, \gamma_d]^\top \in (0,1]^d$.
conclusions: \begin{align*} \left\|\left[K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}\ast f\right] - f\right\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})} \leq C_0 |f|_{B_{2,q}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathcal{X})} \cdot \max\{\gamma_1^{s_1}, \ldots, \gamma_d^{s_d}\} \end{align*} for some constant $C_0$ that only depends on $d, \boldsymbol{s}$.
nodes.label: lem:hang_prop_3

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma D.5
nodes.statement: Notice that \begin{align*} \begin{aligned} &\quad K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}} * f(\mathbf x) =\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \sum_{j=1}^r\binom{r}{j}(-1)^{1-j} \frac{1}{j^d}\left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{d} \frac{1}{\gamma_i} \right) \exp\left( -2 \sum_{i=1}^d \frac{(x_i - t_i)^2}{j^2 \gamma_i^2} \right) f(\boldsymbol{t}) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t} \\ & =\sum_{j=1}^r\binom{r}{j}(-1)^{1-j} \frac{1}{j^d} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{d} \frac{1}{\gamma_i} \right) \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \exp\left( -2 \sum_{i=1}^d \frac{(x_i - t_i)^2}{j^2 \gamma_i^2} \right) f(\boldsymbol{t}) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t} \\ & =\sum_{j=1}^r\binom{r}{j}(-1)^{1-j} \frac{1}{j^d}\left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \left( \prod_{i=1}^{d} \frac{1}{\gamma_i} \right) \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \exp\left( -2 \sum_{i=1}^d \frac{h_i^2}{\gamma_i^2} \right) f(\mathbf x + j \boldsymbol{h}) j^d \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} \\ & =\sum_{j=1}^r\binom{r}{j}(-1)^{1-j} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) f(\mathbf x + j \boldsymbol{h} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} \\ & = \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \left(\sum_{j=1}^r \binom{r}{j}(-1)^{1-j} f( \mathbf{x} + j \boldsymbol{h} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma} )\right) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} . \end{aligned} \end{align*} Next, since $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} $ = 1, we have that \begin{align*} &\quad \left\| [K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}} * f] - f\right\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})}^2 \\ &= \int_{\mathcal{X}} \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \left(\sum_{j=0}^r \binom{r}{j}(-1)^{1-j} f( \mathbf{x} + j \boldsymbol{h} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma} )\right) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} \right)^2 \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \\ &= \int_{\mathcal{X}} \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \left(\sum_{j=0}^r \binom{r}{j}(-1)^{2r + 1 - j} f( \mathbf{x} + j \boldsymbol{h} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma} )\right) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} \right)^2 \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \\ &= \int_{\mathcal{X}} \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} (-1)^{r+1} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \Delta_{\boldsymbol{h} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}}^r f(\mathbf x) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} \right)^2 \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x . \end{align*} Where the last step follows from the definition of modulus of smoothness in Eq. \eqref{eq:module_smoothness}. Then, from Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have \begin{small} \begin{align} &\leq \int_{\mathcal{X}} \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h}\right) \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \left| \Delta_{\boldsymbol{h} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}}^r f(\mathbf x) \right|^2 \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} \right) \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \nonumber \\ &= \int_{\mathcal{X}} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \left| \Delta_{\boldsymbol{h} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}}^r f(\mathbf x) \right|^2 \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \nonumber \\ &= \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \left\| \Delta_{\boldsymbol{h} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}}^r f \right\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})}^2 \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} . \end{align} \end{small} Define $N := \min\{\gamma_1^{-s_1}, \ldots, \gamma_d^{-s_d}\}$. Since $f \in B_{2,q}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathcal{X})$, we have \begin{align*} &|f|_{B_{2,q}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathcal{X})} \geq |f|_{B_{2,\infty}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathcal{X})} := \sup_{t} \left( t^{-1} \omega_{r, 2} \left(f, t^{\frac{1}{s_1}}, \ldots, t^{\frac{1}{s_d}}, \mathcal{X} \right) \right) \\ &\geq \left( \left( \sum_{i=1}^d h_i^{s_i} \right) N^{-1} \right)^{-1} \omega_{r, 2} \left(f, \left( \sum_{i=1}^d h_i^{s_i} \right)^{\frac{1}{s_1}} N^{-\frac{1}{s_1}}, \ldots, \left( \sum_{i=1}^d h_i^{s_i} \right)^{\frac{1}{s_d}} N^{-\frac{1}{s_d}}, \mathcal{X} \right) \\ &\geq N \left( \sum_{i=1}^d h_i^{s_i} \right)^{-1} \omega_{r, 2} \left(f, h_1 \gamma_1, \ldots, h_d \gamma_d, \mathcal{X} \right) \\ &\geq N \left( \sum_{i=1}^d h_i^{s_i} \right)^{-1} \left\| \Delta_{\boldsymbol{h} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}}^r f \right\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})} . \end{align*} As a result, we have $ \| \Delta_{\boldsymbol{h} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}}^r f\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})} \leq |f|_{B_{2,q}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathcal{X})} N^{-1} (\sum_{i=1}^d h_i^{s_i})$. Plugging the above back to Eq.~\eqref{eq:K_gamma_f_f_diff_Delta}, we obtain \begin{align*} \left\| K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}} * f - f\right\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})}^2 &\leq \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \left( |f|_{B_{2,q}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathcal{X})} N^{-1} \left(\sum_{i=1}^d h_i^{s_i}\right) \right)^2 \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} \\ &\leq |f|_{B_{2,q}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathcal{X})}^2 N^{-2} d \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \left(\sum_{i=1}^d h_i^{2 s_i}\right) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} . \end{align*} Notice that \begin{align*} C_0^2 := d \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \left(\sum_{i=1}^d h_i^{2 s_i}\right) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} = d \sum_{i=1}^d \int_{\mathbb{R}} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \exp\left( -2 h_i^2 \right) h_i^{2 s_i }dh_i, \end{align*} which is the sum of $s_i$-th moment of a one dimensional Gaussian distribution $\mathcal{N}(0, 1/4)$ from $i=1$ to $i=d$. Finally, we obtain \begin{align*} \left\| K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}} * f - f\right\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})}^2 &\leq C_0^2 |f|_{B_{2,q}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathcal{X})}^2 N^{-2} = C_0^2 |f|_{B_{2,q}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathcal{X})}^2 \left( \max\{\gamma_1^{s_1}, \ldots, \gamma_d^{s_d}\} \right)^2 . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Express $K_\gamma*f-f$ via finite differences, apply Cauchy–Schwarz and the Besov modulus of smoothness, then sum Gaussian moments.

nodes.name: Convolution error via finite differences (eq:K_gamma_f_f_diff_Delta)
nodes.statement: &\leq \int_{\mathcal{X}} \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h}\right) \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \left| \Delta_{\boldsymbol{h} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}}^r f(\mathbf x) \right|^2 \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} \right) \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \nonumber \\ &= \int_{\mathcal{X}} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \left| \Delta_{\boldsymbol{h} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}}^r f(\mathbf x) \right|^2 \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \nonumber \\ &= \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \left\| \Delta_{\boldsymbol{h} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}}^r f \right\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})}^2 \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} .
nodes.label: eq:K_gamma_f_f_diff_Delta

nodes.name: RKHS norm of K_gamma * f
nodes.statement: Given a function $f:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}$, we have \begin{align*} \left\|K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}\ast f \right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}} \leq \left(\prod_{i=1}^{d}\gamma_i^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right)\pi^{-\frac{d}{4}}(2^r - 1)\|f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)}. \end{align*}
conclusions: Given a function $f:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}$, we have \begin{align*} \left\|K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}\ast f \right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}} \leq \left(\prod_{i=1}^{d}\gamma_i^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right)\pi^{-\frac{d}{4}}(2^r - 1)\|f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)}. \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:hang_prop_4

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma D.6
nodes.statement: Following the same arguments in the proof of proposition 4 in \cite{hang2021optimal}, we have $ K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}} \ast f \in \mathcal{H}_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}$. For a function $f:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}$, we define $\tau_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}f(\mathbf x) = f(\boldsymbol{\gamma}\odot \mathbf x)$. We have, for all $\mathbf x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, \begin{align*} \tau_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}\left(K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}} \ast f\right)(\mathbf x) &= \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}} \left( \boldsymbol{\gamma} \odot \mathbf x - \boldsymbol{t} \right) f(\boldsymbol{t}) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t} \\ &= \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}K_{\mathbf{1}}\left(\frac{\boldsymbol{\gamma} \odot \mathbf x - \boldsymbol{t}}{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}\right)\left(\prod_{i=1}^{d}\frac{1}{\gamma_i} \right)f(\boldsymbol{t})\;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}\\ &= \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}K_{\mathbf{1}}\left(\mathbf x - \frac{\boldsymbol{t}}{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}\right)\left(\prod_{i=1}^{d}\frac{1}{\gamma_i} \right)f\left( \boldsymbol{t} \right)\;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}\\ &= \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}K_{\mathbf{1}}\left(\mathbf x - \boldsymbol{t}\right)f\left(\boldsymbol{t} \odot\boldsymbol{\gamma}\right)\;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}\\ &= (K_{\mathbf{1}}\ast (\tau_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}f))(\mathbf x) . \end{align*} Proposition 4.37 of \cite{steinwart2008support} can be generalized to anisotropic case which shows that for any $f \in \mathcal{H}_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}$, $\tau_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}} f \in \mathcal{H}_{X, \mathbf{1}}$ and $\tau_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}: \mathcal{H}_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}} \to \mathcal{H}_{X, \mathbf{1}}$ is an isometric isomorphism. Hence we have \begin{align*} \left\|K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}\ast f \right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}} &= \left\|\tau_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}\left(K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}\ast f\right) \right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{X, \mathbf{1}}}\\ &= \left\|K_{\mathbf{1}}\ast (\tau_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}f)\right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{X, \mathbf{1}}}\\ &\leq \pi^{-\frac{d}{4}}(2^r - 1) \|\tau_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)}\\ &= \left(\prod_{i=1}^{d}\gamma_i^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right)\pi^{-\frac{d}{4}}(2^r - 1)\|f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)}, \end{align*} where the second last inequality follows from \cite{eberts2013optimal}[Theorem 2.3] setting $\gamma=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Rescale $f$ to unit bandwidth and use the (anisotropic) Gaussian RKHS norm of $K_1*f$ as in Hang & Steinwart Prop. 4.

nodes.name: RKHS norm of K_gamma_x * K_gamma_o * f
nodes.statement: Let $f:\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}\to \mathbb{R}$ and \begin{align*} \gamma_x = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{d_x}}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}},\quad \gamma_o = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}. \end{align*} Recall $K_{\gamma_x}:\mathbb{R}^{d_x} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $K_{\gamma_o}:\mathbb{R}^{d_o} \to \mathbb{R}$ defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:K_function}, then we have \begin{align*} \|K_{\gamma_x} \ast K_{\gamma_o} \ast f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} \leq C_{1} n^{\frac{1}{2} \frac{1+\frac{d_o}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}} \|f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})}, \end{align*} for some constant $C_1$ that only depends on $d_x,d_o,s_x,s_o$.
assumptions: Let $f:\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}\to \mathbb{R}$ and \begin{align*} \gamma_x = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{d_x}}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}},\quad \gamma_o = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}. \end{align*} Recall $K_{\gamma_x}:\mathbb{R}^{d_x} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $K_{\gamma_o}:\mathbb{R}^{d_o} \to \mathbb{R}$ defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:K_function}
conclusions: \begin{align*} \|K_{\gamma_x} \ast K_{\gamma_o} \ast f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} \leq C_{1} n^{\frac{1}{2} \frac{1+\frac{d_o}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}} \|f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})}, \end{align*} for some constant $C_1$ that only depends on $d_x,d_o,s_x,s_o$.
nodes.label: cor:hang_prop_4_obs_cov

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary D.1
nodes.statement: The proof is a direct application of \Cref{lem:hang_prop_4}.
nodes.statement_short: Direct consequence of Lemma D.6 with the chosen lengthscales.

nodes.name: RKHS norm of the low-pass filtered convolution
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma_x = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{d_x}}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}$, $\gamma_o = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}$. Let $\iota_{x,\gamma_x^{-1}} : \mathbb{R}^{d_x} \to \mathbb{R}$ be an indicator function over $\{\boldsymbol{\omega}_x: \|\boldsymbol{\omega}_x\|_2 \leq \gamma_x^{-1} \}$ and $K_{\gamma_o}: \mathbb{R}^{d_x} \to \mathbb{R}$ be as defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:K_function}. Then we have \begin{align*} \|\mathcal{F}^{-1}[\iota_{x,\gamma_x^{-1}}] \ast K_{\gamma_o} \ast f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} \lesssim 2^{r} n^{\frac{1}{2} \frac{1+\frac{d_o}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}} \|f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})} . \end{align*}
assumptions: Let $\gamma_x = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{d_x}}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}$, $\gamma_o = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}$. Let $\iota_{x,\gamma_x^{-1}} : \mathbb{R}^{d_x} \to \mathbb{R}$ be an indicator function over $\{\boldsymbol{\omega}_x: \|\boldsymbol{\omega}_x\|_2 \leq \gamma_x^{-1} \}$ and $K_{\gamma_o}: \mathbb{R}^{d_x} \to \mathbb{R}$ be as defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:K_function}.
conclusions: \begin{align*} \|\mathcal{F}^{-1}[\iota_{x,\gamma_x^{-1}}] \ast K_{\gamma_o} \ast f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} \lesssim 2^{r} n^{\frac{1}{2} \frac{1+\frac{d_o}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}} \|f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})} . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:mixed_convolution

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma D.7
nodes.statement: In contrast to the notation used in the rest of the document (with the exception of \Cref{lem:l2toprojected_illp}), in this proof, we use $\mathcal{F}$ to denote the unitary Fourier operator on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})$, we use $\mathcal{F}_x$ to denote the unitary Fourier operator on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})$, and we use $\mathcal{F}_o$ to denote the unitary Fourier operator on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})$. We let $\otimes: L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})\times L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})\to L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})$ denotes the tensor product mapping, where $(f\otimes g)(\mathbf x,\mathbf o) = f(\mathbf x)g(\mathbf o)$ for all $(\mathbf x,\mathbf o)\in \mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}$. By considering a convergent sequence to $f_1$ in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})\cap L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})$, and similarly for $f_2$, we can show that \begin{align*} \mathcal{F}[f\otimes g] = \mathcal{F}_x[f]\otimes \mathcal{F}_o[g] \end{align*} for $f\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})$ and $g\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})$. At the start of \Cref{sec:proof_upper}, we proved that for $f\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})$, $f\ast \mathcal{F}^{-1}[\iota_{x,\gamma_x^{-1}}] \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})$. Since $\|K_{\gamma_o}\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}= 1$ \citep[Section 4.1.2]{Giné_Nickl_2015}, we have \begin{align*} \|(f\ast \mathcal{F}^{-1}[\iota_{x,\gamma_x^{-1}}])\ast K_{\gamma_o}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})}^2 &\stackrel{(a)}{=} \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x}}\|(f\ast \mathcal{F}^{-1}[\iota_{x,\gamma_x^{-1}}])(\mathbf x,\cdot) \ast K_{\gamma_o}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\\ &\stackrel{(b)}{\leq} \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x}} \|(f\ast \mathcal{F}^{-1}[\iota_{x,\gamma_x^{-1}}])(\mathbf x,\cdot)\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})} \|K_{\gamma_o}\|^2_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\\ & = \|f\ast \mathcal{F}^{-1}[\iota_{x,\gamma_x^{-1}}]\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})}. \end{align*} where in $(a)$, $(f\ast \mathcal{F}^{-1}[\iota_{x,\gamma_x^{-1}}])(\mathbf x,\cdot)$ is a slice function of any representative of $f\ast \mathcal{F}^{-1}[\iota_{x,\gamma_x^{-1}}]\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})$, and $(b)$ follows from Young's Convolution Inequality. Hence we can apply $\mathcal{F}$ to $f\ast \mathcal{F}^{-1}[\iota_{x,\gamma_x^{-1}}]\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})$ and we find \begin{align*} \mathcal{F}\left[\mathcal{F}_x^{-1}[\iota_{x,\gamma_x^{-1}}] \ast K_{\gamma_o} \ast f\right] = (\iota_{x,\gamma_x^{-1}}\otimes \mathcal{F}_o[K_{\gamma_o}]) \cdot \mathcal{F}[f]. \end{align*} For $\phi(\mathbf x,\mathbf o) = \exp(- \gamma_x^{-2} \|\mathbf x\|_2^2) \cdot \exp(- \gamma_o^{-2} \|\mathbf o\|_2^2)$, its Fourier transform is \begin{align*} \mathcal{F}[\phi](\boldsymbol{\omega}_x,\boldsymbol{\omega}_o) = \pi^{d_x/2+d_o/2} \gamma_x^{d_x} \exp\left(-\frac{1}{4} \gamma_x^{2} \|\boldsymbol{\omega}_x\|_2^2\right) \cdot \gamma_o^{d_o}\exp\left(-\frac{1}{4} \gamma_o^{2} \|\boldsymbol{\omega}_o\|_2^2\right). \end{align*} Hence, by definition of Gaussian RKHS norm~\citep[Theorem 10.12]{wendland2004scattered}, \begin{align*} &\quad \left\| \mathcal{F}_x^{-1}[\iota_{x,\gamma_x^{-1}}]\ast K_{\gamma_o} \ast f\right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}^2 \\ &= \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}} \frac{\left(\iota_{x,\gamma_x^{-1}}(\boldsymbol{\omega}_x) \cdot \mathcal{F}[f](\boldsymbol{\omega}_x,\boldsymbol{\omega}_o) \cdot \mathcal{F}_o[K_{\gamma_o}](\boldsymbol{\omega}_o)\right)^2}{\pi^{d_x/2+d_o/2} \gamma_x^{d_x} \exp\left(-\frac{1}{4} \gamma_x^{2} \|\boldsymbol{\omega}_x\|_2^2\right) \cdot \gamma_o^{d_o}\exp(-\frac{1}{4} \gamma_o^{2} \|\boldsymbol{\omega}_o\|_2^2)} \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{\omega}_x \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{\omega}_o \\ &\lesssim \gamma_x^{-d_x} \gamma_o^{-d_o} \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_o}}\int_{\{\boldsymbol{\omega}_x: \|\boldsymbol{\omega}_x\|_2 \leq \gamma_x^{-1} \}} \frac{\left( \mathcal{F}[f](\boldsymbol{\omega}_x,\boldsymbol{\omega}_o) \cdot \mathcal{F}_o[K_{\gamma_o}](\boldsymbol{\omega}_o)\right)^2}{\exp\left(-\frac{1}{4} \gamma_x^{2} \|\boldsymbol{\omega}_x\|_2^2\right) \cdot \exp(-\frac{1}{4} \gamma_o^{2} \|\boldsymbol{\omega}_o\|_2^2)} \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{\omega}_x \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{\omega}_o \\ &\lesssim \gamma_x^{-d_x} \gamma_o^{-d_o} \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}} \exp\left(\frac{1}{4} \gamma_o^{2} \|\boldsymbol{\omega}_o\|_2^2\right)\left(\mathcal{F}[f](\boldsymbol{\omega}_x,\boldsymbol{\omega}_o) \cdot \mathcal{F}_o[K_{\gamma_o}](\boldsymbol{\omega}_o)\right)^2 \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{\omega}_x \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{\omega}_o . \end{align*} Since $K_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o) := \sum_{j=1}^r\binom{r}{j}(-1)^{1-j} \frac{1}{j^{d_o}\gamma_o^{d_o}}\left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp( -2 j^{-2} \gamma_o^{-2} \|\mathbf o\|_2^2)$, so we have \begin{align*} \mathcal{F}_o[K_{\gamma_o}](\boldsymbol{\omega}_o) = \sum_{j=1}^r\binom{r}{j}(-1)^{1-j} \exp\left(-\frac{1}{8} j^2 \gamma_o^2 \|\boldsymbol{\omega}_o\|_2^2\right) . \end{align*} Consequently, we have \begin{align*} &\quad \left\| \mathcal{F}^{-1}[\iota_{x,\gamma_x^{-1}}]\ast K_{\gamma_o} \ast f\right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}^2 \\ &\lesssim \gamma_x^{-d_x} \gamma_o^{-d_o} \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}} \frac{\left(\mathcal{F}[f](\boldsymbol{\omega}_x,\boldsymbol{\omega}_o) \cdot \sum_{j=1}^r\binom{r}{j}(-1)^{1-j} \exp(-\frac{1}{8} j^2 \gamma_o^2 \|\boldsymbol{\omega}_o\|_2^2) \right)^2}{\exp(-\frac{1}{4} \gamma_o^{2} \|\boldsymbol{\omega}_o\|_2^2)} d\boldsymbol{\omega}_x d\boldsymbol{\omega}_o \\ &\leq \gamma_x^{-d_x} \gamma_o^{-d_o} 2^{2r} \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}} \left(\mathcal{F}[f](\boldsymbol{\omega}_x,\boldsymbol{\omega}_o) \right)^2 d\boldsymbol{\omega}_x d\boldsymbol{\omega}_o \\ &= \gamma_x^{-d_x} \gamma_o^{-d_o} 2^{2r} \| f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})}^2 . \end{align*} where the last equality follows by Plancherel's Theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Fourier-side computation: the low-pass filtered function has bounded Gaussian-RKHS weighted Fourier norm on the frequency ball.

nodes.name: Fourier characterisation of the anisotropic Gaussian RKHS norm
nodes.statement: Let $\boldsymbol{\gamma} = (\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_d)\in (0,1)^{d}$. Let $k_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}$ be the anisotropic Gaussian kernel on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and let $\mathcal{H}_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}$ be the RKHS associated with $k_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}$. Then \begin{align*} \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} |\mathcal{F}[f](\boldsymbol{\omega})|^2\exp\left(\frac{\|\boldsymbol{\omega}\odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}\|_{2}^{2}}{4}\right) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{\omega} = 2^{d} \pi^{d/2} \left(\prod_{i=1}^{d} \gamma_i\right) \|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}}^2 \end{align*}
assumptions: Let $\boldsymbol{\gamma} = (\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_d)\in (0,1)^{d}$. Let $k_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}$ be the anisotropic Gaussian kernel on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and let $\mathcal{H}_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}$ be the RKHS associated with $k_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}$.
conclusions: \begin{align*} \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} |\mathcal{F}[f](\boldsymbol{\omega})|^2\exp\left(\frac{\|\boldsymbol{\omega}\odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}\|_{2}^{2}}{4}\right) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{\omega} = 2^{d} \pi^{d/2} \left(\prod_{i=1}^{d} \gamma_i\right) \|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}}^2 \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:unit_ball_grkhs

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma D.8
nodes.statement: We define $\phi_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}(\mathbf x) = \exp(-\sum_{j=1}^{d} \gamma_j^{-2} x_j^2)$. Then \begin{align*} \mathcal{F}[\phi_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}](\boldsymbol{\omega}) &= \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\phi_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}(\mathbf x)\exp(-i\langle \mathbf x, \boldsymbol{\omega}\rangle) \mathrm{d}\mathbf x \\ &= \left(\prod_{i=1}^{d}\gamma_i\right) \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\phi_{X,1}(\mathbf x)\exp\left(-i\left\langle \mathbf x, \boldsymbol{\omega} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}\right\rangle\right)\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\\ &= \pi^{d/2} \left(\prod_{i=1}^{d}\gamma_i\right)\exp\left(-\frac{\|\boldsymbol{\omega}\odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}\|_{2}^{2}}{4}\right) \end{align*} where the last step follows from \cite{wendland2004scattered}[Theorem 5.20]. By \cite{kanagawa2018gaussianprocesseskernelmethods}[Theorem 2.4], we have \begin{align*} \|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}}^2 &= (2\pi)^{-d} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \frac{|\mathcal{F}[f](\boldsymbol{\omega})|^2}{\mathcal{F}[\phi_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}](\boldsymbol{\omega})} d \boldsymbol{\omega} \\ &=(2\pi)^{-d} \pi^{d/2} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} |\mathcal{F}[f](\boldsymbol{\omega})|^2 \left(\prod_{i=1}^{d}\gamma_i\right)^{-1}\exp\left(\frac{\|\boldsymbol{\omega}\odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}\|_{2}^{2}}{4}\right) \mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{\omega}\; \\ &= 2^{-d} \pi^{-d/2} \left(\prod_{i=1}^{d} \gamma_i\right)^{-1} \int |\mathcal{F}[f](\boldsymbol{\omega})|^2 \exp\left(\frac{\|\boldsymbol{\omega}\odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}\|_{2}^{2}}{4}\right) \mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{\omega} \end{align*} whence the Lemma follows.
nodes.statement_short: Fourier characterisation of the Gaussian RKHS norm (Wendland Thm 10.12 / Kanagawa et al. Thm 2.4).

nodes.name: From projected to unprojected error on the Gaussian RKHS
nodes.statement: Suppose that \Cref{ass:T_frequency_ill_posedness} in the main text holds, and suppose $\gamma_x^{\delta_x} = \gamma_o^{\delta_o}$ for some positive constant $\delta_x, \delta_o$. Suppose $f\in \mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}$ with $\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}^2 \leq Cn$ for some constant $C>0$. Then, \begin{align} \|f\|_{L^2(P_{XO})} &\lesssim \gamma_x^{-d_x\eta_0} (\log (\gamma_x^{-\delta_x}))^{\frac{d_x\eta_0}{2}} \|Tf\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} \nonumber \\ &\qquad + \gamma_x^{-d_x\eta_0} (\log (\gamma_x^{-\delta_x}))^{\frac{d_x\eta_0}{2}}\gamma_x^{\frac{1}{8} \delta_x} (n \gamma_x^{d_x}\gamma_o^{d_o})^{\frac{1}{2}} . \end{align} In particular, for \begin{align*} \gamma_x = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{d_x}}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}},\quad \gamma_o = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}. \end{align*} and $\frac{1}{8} \delta_x = 2s_x + d_x\eta_1 + d_x \eta_0$, $\delta_x = \delta_o \frac{d_x}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)$. Then, we have \begin{align*} \|f\|_{L^2(P_{XO})} \lesssim \gamma_x^{-d_x\eta_0} (\log n)^{\frac{d_x\eta_0}{2}} \|Tf\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} + n^{-\frac{\frac{s_x}{d_x} }{1+(2 + \frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}. \end{align*}
assumptions: Suppose that \Cref{ass:T_frequency_ill_posedness} in the main text holds, and suppose $\gamma_x^{\delta_x} = \gamma_o^{\delta_o}$ for some positive constant $\delta_x, \delta_o$. Suppose $f\in \mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}$ with $\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}^2 \leq Cn$ for some constant $C>0$.
conclusions: \begin{align} \|f\|_{L^2(P_{XO})} &\lesssim \gamma_x^{-d_x\eta_0} (\log (\gamma_x^{-\delta_x}))^{\frac{d_x\eta_0}{2}} \|Tf\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} \nonumber \\ &\qquad + \gamma_x^{-d_x\eta_0} (\log (\gamma_x^{-\delta_x}))^{\frac{d_x\eta_0}{2}}\gamma_x^{\frac{1}{8} \delta_x} (n \gamma_x^{d_x}\gamma_o^{d_o})^{\frac{1}{2}} . \end{align} In particular, for \begin{align*} \gamma_x = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{d_x}}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}},\quad \gamma_o = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}. \end{align*} and $\frac{1}{8} \delta_x = 2s_x + d_x\eta_1 + d_x \eta_0$, $\delta_x = \delta_o \frac{d_x}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)$. Then, we have \begin{align*} \|f\|_{L^2(P_{XO})} \lesssim \gamma_x^{-d_x\eta_0} (\log n)^{\frac{d_x\eta_0}{2}} \|Tf\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} + n^{-\frac{\frac{s_x}{d_x} }{1+(2 + \frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: For $f$ in the Gaussian RKHS with $\|f\|^2\lesssim n$, $\|f\|_{L^2}\lesssim\gamma_x^{-d_x\eta_0}(\log n)^{d_x\eta_0/2}\|Tf\|$ plus a negligible high-frequency term.
nodes.label: lem:l2toprojected_illp

nodes.name: Lower bound on the operator norm of C_FO
nodes.statement: Suppose \Cref{assn: technical} hold, and let \begin{align*} \gamma_x = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{d_x}}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}, \quad \gamma_o = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}. \end{align*} Then, for sufficiently large $n\geq 1$, we have \begin{align*} \|C_{FO}\| \geq a\left(\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{4}\right)^{\frac{d_x+d_o}{2}} n^{-\frac{1}{2}\frac{1+\frac{d_o}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}} . \end{align*}
assumptions: Suppose \Cref{assn: technical} hold, and let \begin{align*} \gamma_x = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{d_x}}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}, \quad \gamma_o = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}. \end{align*}
conclusions: for sufficiently large $n\geq 1$, we have \begin{align*} \|C_{FO}\| \geq a\left(\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{4}\right)^{\frac{d_x+d_o}{2}} n^{-\frac{1}{2}\frac{1+\frac{d_o}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}} . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem: C_f_op_norm_lower_bound

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma D.10
nodes.statement: By definition of the operator norm, we have \begin{align*} &\quad \|C_{FO}\|^2 \\ &= \sup_{\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} = 1}\left\langle f, \mathbb{E}[(F_{\ast}(Z, O) \otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(O))\otimes (F_{\ast}(Z, O) \otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(O))]f\right\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}\\ =& \sup_{\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} = 1} \mathbb{E} \left[ \left(\mathbb{E}[f(X,O)|Z,O] \right)^2 \right]\\ \geq & \sup_{\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} = 1} \left( \mathbb{E}_{ZO \sim P_{ZO}} \left[\mathbb{E}[f(X,O)|Z,O]\right] \right)^2\\ =& \sup_{\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} = 1} \mathbb{E}[f(X,O)]^2 \\ =& \|\mu_{XO}\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}^2 , \end{align*} where $\mu_{XO} := \mathbb{E}_{P_{XO}}[\phi_{\gamma_x}(X) \otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(O)]$. Notice that \begin{align*} &\|\mu_{XO} \|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}^2\\ &= \left\langle \iint_{\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{X}} \phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x) \otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o) p_{XO}(\mathbf x,\mathbf o)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o, \right. \\ &\qquad\qquad \left. \iint_{\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{X}} \phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x') \otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o') p_{XO}(\mathbf x',\mathbf o')\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x'\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o'\right\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}\\ &= \iint_{\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{X}} \iint_{\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{X}} K_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o,\mathbf o') K_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x,\mathbf x')p_{XO}(\mathbf x,\mathbf o) p_{XO}(\mathbf x', \mathbf o')\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x'\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o'\\ &\stackrel{(a)}{\geq} a^2\int_{[1/4,3/4]^{d_o}}\int_{[1/4,3/4]^{d_o}} K_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o,\mathbf o')\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o'\int_{[1/4,3/4]^{d_x}}\int_{[1/4,3/4]^{d_x}} K_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x,\mathbf x') \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x'\\ &\stackrel{(b)} = a^2 \left(\gamma_x \sqrt{\pi} \left[\frac{\mathrm{erf}\left(\frac{1}{2\gamma_x}\right)}{2} + \gamma_x\frac{\exp\left(-\frac{1}{4\gamma_x^2}\right)-1}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right]\right)^{d_x} \\ &\qquad\qquad \cdot \left(\gamma_o \sqrt{\pi} \left[\frac{\mathrm{erf}\left(\frac{1}{2\gamma_o}\right)}{2} + \gamma_o\frac{\exp\left(-\frac{1}{4\gamma_o^2}\right)-1}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right]\right)^{d_o}, \end{align*} where $\mathrm{erf}(x) := \frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi}}\int^{x}_{-x}\exp\left(-t^2\right)\;\mathrm{d}t$ is the standard error function of normal distribution. Step $(a)$ holds by \Cref{assn: technical} and step $(b)$ holds by using \Cref{lem:gaussian_kernel_embedding}. We plug in $\gamma_x = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{d_x}}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}$, $\gamma_o = n^{-\frac{\frac{1}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}$ to obtain \begin{align*} \|\mu_{XO}\|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} &\stackrel{(i)}{\geq} a^2\left(\sqrt{\pi}\gamma_x/4\right)^{d_x}\left(\sqrt{\pi}\gamma_o/4\right)^{d_o} = a^2 (\sqrt{\pi}/4)^{d_x+d_o} n^{-\frac{1+\frac{d_o}{s_o}(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}, \end{align*} where $(i)$ holds for sufficiently large $n\geq 1$ because $\mathrm{erf}(x)\geq \frac{1}{2}$ when $x\geq 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound $\|C_{FO}\|$ by testing on the kernel mean embedding of $P_{XO}$ restricted to $[1/4,3/4]$ and compute Gaussian integrals (Lemma D.11).

nodes.name: Gaussian kernel integral over [1/4,3/4]^d
nodes.statement: Let $k_{\gamma} : \mathbb{R}^{d}\times \mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}$ be the Gaussian kernel with length scale $\gamma\in (0,1]$. Then we have, \begin{align*} \int_{[1/4,3/4]^{d}}\int_{[1/4,3/4]^{d}} k_{\gamma}(\mathbf x, \mathbf x') \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \mathrm{d} \mathbf x' = \left(\gamma \sqrt{\pi} \left[\frac{\mathrm{erf}\left(\frac{1}{2\gamma}\right)}{2} + \gamma\frac{\exp\left(-\frac{1}{4\gamma^2}\right)-1}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right]\right)^{d_x}. \end{align*} Here, $\mathrm{erf}(x) := \frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi}}\int^{x}_{-x}\exp\left(-t^2\right)\;\mathrm{d}t$ is the standard error function.
assumptions: Let $k_{\gamma} : \mathbb{R}^{d}\times \mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}$ be the Gaussian kernel with length scale $\gamma\in (0,1]$.
conclusions: \begin{align*} \int_{[1/4,3/4]^{d}}\int_{[1/4,3/4]^{d}} k_{\gamma}(\mathbf x, \mathbf x') \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \mathrm{d} \mathbf x' = \left(\gamma \sqrt{\pi} \left[\frac{\mathrm{erf}\left(\frac{1}{2\gamma}\right)}{2} + \gamma\frac{\exp\left(-\frac{1}{4\gamma^2}\right)-1}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right]\right)^{d_x}. \end{align*} Here, $\mathrm{erf}(x) := \frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi}}\int^{x}_{-x}\exp\left(-t^2\right)\;\mathrm{d}t$ is the standard error function.
nodes.label: lem:gaussian_kernel_embedding

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma D.11
nodes.statement: Since $k_{\gamma}(\mathbf x, \mathbf x^\prime) = \prod_{i=1}^{d} \exp\left(-\frac{(x_i - x_i')^2}{\gamma^2}\right)$, it suffices to prove the following result \begin{align*} \int_{1/4}^{3/4} \int_{1/4}^{3/4} k_{\gamma}(x_i, x_i') \;\mathrm{d} x_i \mathrm{d} x_i' = \gamma^2 \sqrt{\pi} \left[\frac{\mathrm{erf}\left(\frac{1}{2\gamma}\right)}{2\gamma} + \frac{\exp\left(-\frac{1}{4\gamma^2}\right)-1}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right]. \end{align*} Notice that \begin{align*} &\int_{1/4}^{3/4} \exp \left(-\frac{(x_i - x_i')^2}{\gamma^2} \right) \;\mathrm{d} x_i\\ &= \gamma \int_{(1/4-x_i^\prime) / \gamma}^{(3/4-x_i^\prime) / \gamma} \exp(-x^2) \;\mathrm{d}x \\ &=\gamma \int^{(3/4-x_i')/\gamma}_{-\infty}\exp(-x^2) \;\mathrm{d}x - \gamma \int^{(1/4-x_i')/\gamma}_{-\infty}\exp(-x^2)\;\mathrm{d}x\\ &=\gamma\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}\left(1+\mathrm{erf}\left(\frac{3/4-x_i'}{\gamma}\right)\right) - \gamma\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}\left(1-\mathrm{erf}\left(\frac{x_i'-1/4}{\gamma}\right)\right)\\ &=\gamma\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}\left(\mathrm{erf}\left(\frac{3/4-x_i'}{\gamma}\right) + \mathrm{erf}\left(\frac{x_i'-1/4}{\gamma}\right)\right). \end{align*} Therefore, we have \begin{align*} &\quad \int_{1/4}^{3/4} \int_{1/4}^{3/4} \exp \left(-\frac{(x_i - x_i')^2}{\gamma^2} \right) \;\mathrm{d} x_i \;\mathrm{d} x_i^\prime \\ &= \gamma \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2} \int_{1/4}^{3/4} \mathrm{erf}\left(\frac{3/4-x_i'}{\gamma}\right) + \mathrm{erf}\left(\frac{x_i'-1/4}{\gamma}\right) \;\mathrm{d} x_i^\prime \\ &= \gamma^2 \sqrt{\pi} \int_{0}^{\frac{1}{2\gamma}} \mathrm{erf}(y) \;\mathrm{d} y \\ &= \gamma^2 \sqrt{\pi} \left[\frac{\mathrm{erf}\left(\frac{1}{2\gamma}\right)}{2\gamma} + \frac{\exp\left(-\frac{1}{4\gamma^2}\right)-1}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right] . \end{align*} where the last inequality holds by using the identity \begin{align*} \int \mathrm{erf}(x) d x = x \cdot \mathrm{erf}(x) + e^{-x^2} / \sqrt{\pi} + C. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Factorise over coordinates and compute one-dimensional Gaussian integrals via the error function.

onumber \ \stackrel{(b)}{\geq} &  rac{\sqrt{|V_\mathfrak{K}|}}{\sqrt{|V_\mathfrak{K}|} + 1} \left( 1 -  rac{\epsilon_0^2 n2^{-2\mathfrak{K} rac{\underline{s}d_x}{s_x} \eta_1}2^{-2\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}} }{\zeta^{-d_x}2^{\mathfrak{K} rac{\underline{s}d_x}{s_x} + \mathfrak{K} rac{\underline{s}d_o}{s_o}}} - rac{1}{2 \log |V_\mathfrak{K}|}ight) 
onumber \ \geq &  rac{\sqrt{|V_\mathfrak{K}|}}{\sqrt{|V_\mathfrak{K}|} + 1} \left( 1 - \epsilon_0^2 \zeta^{d_x} n 2^{-\mathfrak{K} rac{\underline{s}}{s_x}\left(2d_x\eta_1 + 2s_x + d_x +  rac{d_o}{s_o}s_xight)} - rac{1}{2 \log |V_\mathfrak{K}|}ight).

nodes.statement: Let $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$, $f\in B_{2,q}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $K\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)$, then \begin{align*} \|K\ast f \|_{B_{2,q}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathbb{R}^d)} \leq \|K\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)}\|f\|_{B_{2,q}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathbb{R}^d)} \end{align*}
