nodes.name: Besov norm of band-pass masked B-spline sums
nodes.statement: Let $M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}: \mathbb{R}^{d_x}\to\mathbb{R}, M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}:\mathbb{R}^{d_o}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:Bspline_main}. Let $\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}:\mathbb{R}^{d_x}\to\mathbb{R}$ be an indicator function over a measurable set $S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)\subset\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ for each ${\boldsymbol\ell}_o$ in Eq.~\eqref{eq:calL}. Define $f(\mathbf x,\mathbf o):= \sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}(M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}} \ast \mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}])(\mathbf x) \cdot M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}(\mathbf o)$. Then we have $\|f\|_{B^{s_x,s_o}_{2,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})}\lesssim 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s} - \mathfrak{K}\frac{\underline{s}}{s_x}\frac{d_x}{2}}$.
assumptions: Let $M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}: \mathbb{R}^{d_x}\to\mathbb{R}, M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}:\mathbb{R}^{d_o}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:Bspline_main}. Let $\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}:\mathbb{R}^{d_x}\to\mathbb{R}$ be an indicator function over a measurable set $S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)\subset\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ for each ${\boldsymbol\ell}_o$ in Eq.~\eqref{eq:calL}. Define $f(\mathbf x,\mathbf o):= \sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}(M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}} \ast \mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}])(\mathbf x) \cdot M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}(\mathbf o)$.
conclusions: $\|f\|_{B^{s_x,s_o}_{2,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})}\lesssim 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s} - \mathfrak{K}\frac{\underline{s}}{s_x}\frac{d_x}{2}}$.
nodes.label: lem:new_besov_mask

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma E.3
nodes.statement: By definition of Besov norm in \citet{leisner_nonlinear_wavelet_approximation_2003}[Eq. (2.2)], for any $r > \max\{s_x, s_o\}$, we have \begin{small} \begin{align*} \|f\|_{B^{s_x,s_o}_{2,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})} &\asymp \underbrace{\sup_{0<t<1}\left[t^{-1}\omega^{\mathbf x}_{r,2}(f,t^{1/s_x},\dots,t^{1/s_x})\right]}_{(I)} + \underbrace{\sup_{0<t<1}\left[t^{-1}\omega^{\mathbf o}_{r,2}(f,t^{1/s_o},\dots,t^{1/s_o})\right]}_{(II)}, \end{align*} \end{small} where $\omega_{r,2}^{\mathbf x}$ (respectively $\omega_{r,2}^{\mathbf o}$) denotes the \emph{partial} modulus of smoothness in the $\mathbf x$ (respectively $\mathbf o$)-direction, and we restrict the supremum from $t\in (0,\infty)$ to $t\in (0,1)$ by \citet[Theorem 10.1]{devore1993constructive}. Specifically, define $(\tau_{\mathbf{h}}g)(\mathbf x) := g(\mathbf x + \mathbf{h})$ and $\Delta^{r}_{\mathbf{h}} := (\tau_{\mathbf{h}} - \mathrm{id})^r$, we write \begin{align*} \omega^{\mathbf x}_{r,2}(f, t^{1/s_x},\dots, t^{1/s_x}) :=\sup_{|h_i|\leq t^{1/s_x}}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_o}}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x}} \left|\Delta^{r}_{\boldsymbol{h}}(f(\cdot, \mathbf o))(\mathbf x)\right|^2 \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}, \end{align*} and $\omega_{r,2}^{\mathbf o}$ is defined similarly. We first bound $(I)$. We have \begin{align*} \tau_{\mathbf{h}}(K\ast g)(\mathbf x) = (K\ast g)(\mathbf x + \mathbf{h}) = (K \ast (\tau_{\mathbf{h}}g))(\mathbf x) . \end{align*} We thus have $\Delta^{r}_{\mathbf{h}}(K\ast g) = K\ast \left(\Delta^{r}_{\mathbf{h}}g\right)$. Thus we have \begin{align*} &\omega^{\mathbf x}_{r,2}(f, t^{1/s_x},\dots, t^{1/s_x})\\ =&\sup_{|h_i|\leq t^{1/s_x}}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_o}}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x}} \left|\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o} ( (\Delta_{\boldsymbol{h}}^r M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}) \ast \mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}])(\mathbf x) M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}(\mathbf o)\right|^2 \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\ =&\sup_{|h_i|\leq t^{1/s_x}}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o'}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x}} ( (\Delta_{\boldsymbol{h}}^r M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}) \ast \mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}])(\mathbf x) \overline{( (\Delta_{\boldsymbol{h}}^r M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}) \ast \mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o')}])(\mathbf x)} \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \right. \\ &\qquad \left. \cdot \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_o}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}(\mathbf o) M_{k,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o'}(\mathbf o) \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\ \stackrel{(a)}{=}&\sup_{|h_i|\leq t^{1/s_x}}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|\mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}]\ast (\Delta^r_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}})\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}^2 \|M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\ \stackrel{(b)}{\leq}& \sup_{|h_i|\leq t^{1/s_x}}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|\Delta^r_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}^2 \|M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\ =& \left(\sup_{|h_i|\leq t^{1/s_x}}\|\Delta^r_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\right)\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\ \stackrel{(c)}{\leq} & \sup_{|h_i|\leq t^{1/s_x}}\|\Delta^r_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\\ =& \omega_{r,2}(M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}},t^{1/s_x},\dots,t^{1/s_x}). \end{align*} In the above derivations, \begin{itemize} \item we use $\mathrm{supp}(M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o})\cap \mathrm{supp}(M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}) = \emptyset$ if ${\boldsymbol\ell}_o\neq {\boldsymbol\ell}_o'$ in $(a)$, \item we use in $(b)$ the inequality \begin{align} \begin{aligned} &\quad \|\mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}] \ast (\Delta^r_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}})\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})} = \|\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)} \cdot \mathcal{F}[\Delta^r_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}]\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})} \\ &\leq \|\mathcal{F}[\Delta_{\boldsymbol{h}}^rM_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}]\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})} = \|\Delta_{\boldsymbol{h}}^rM_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}, \end{aligned} \end{align} \item we use $ \sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})} \leq 2^{\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}d_o}{s_o}}2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}d_o}{s_o}}\|M_{0\boldsymbol{0}}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})} \leq 1$ in $(c)$. Indeed, note that $\|M_{0\boldsymbol{0}}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})} = \|\iota_{m}\|^{2d_o}_{L^2(\mathbb{R})} \leq \|\iota_{m}\|^{2d_o}_{L^1(\mathbb{R})} = 1$. \end{itemize} Thus we have \begin{align*} (I)&\leq \sup_{t>0}\left[t^{-1}\omega_{r,2}\left(M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}},t^{\frac{1}{s_x}},\dots,t^{\frac{1}{s_x}}\right)\right] \asymp |M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}|_{B^{s_x}_{2,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})} \asymp 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}\left(1 -\frac{d_x}{2s_x}\right)}, \end{align*} where we bound $(I)$ by an isotropic Besov norm, and we use the sequential Besov norm equivalence \citep{devore1988interpolation}[Theorem 5.1] (see also \citet[Theorem 3.4]{leisner_nonlinear_wavelet_approximation_2003} applied to $B^{s_x}_{2,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})$) in the last equality. Now we bound $(II)$. Notice that \begin{align*} &\omega^{\mathbf o}_{r,2}(f,t^{1/s_o},\dots, t^{1/s_o})\\ \stackrel{(a)}{\lesssim} &\omega_{s_o,2}^{\mathbf o}(f,t^{1/s_o},\dots, t^{1/s_o})\\ \stackrel{(b)}{\lesssim} &2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\omega^{\mathbf o}_{s_o,2}\left(f,2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{1/s_o},\dots, 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{1/s_o}\right)\\ =&2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}} \sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{1/s_o}}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}} \left|\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}(\mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}] \ast M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}})(\mathbf x) \cdot (\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}} M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o})(\mathbf o) \right|^2 \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\ =&2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}} t^{1/s_o}}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o'}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x}} (\mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}]\ast M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}})(\mathbf x) \cdot \overline{\mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o^\prime)}]\ast M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}}(\mathbf x)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \right. \\ &\qquad \left. \cdot \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_o}}(\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o})(\mathbf o)\cdot (\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o'})(\mathbf o) \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\ \stackrel{(c)}{=}& 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{1/s_o}}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|\mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}] \ast M_{k,{\boldsymbol\ell}_x}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})} \cdot \|\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\ \stackrel{(d)}{\leq} & 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{1/s_o}}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})} \cdot \|\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\ = & 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\left( \sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}} t^{1/s_o}}\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\ \stackrel{(e)}{=} & 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\left( \sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}} t^{1/s_o}}\left\|\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\left(\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\right)\right\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\ \stackrel{(f)}{=} & 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\left( \sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}} t^{1/s_o}}\left\|\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\right)\right\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\ = &2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\left(\omega_{s_o,2}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o},2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{\frac{1}{s_o}},\dots,2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{\frac{1}{s_o}}\right)^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}. \end{align*} In the above derivations, \begin{itemize} \item we use $r=s_x\vee s_o \geq s_o$ and Minkowski's inequality in $(a)$ (this is also sometimes referred to as the reverse Marchaud inequality, see \cite{KOLOMOITSEV2020105423}[Property 8]), \item we use \cite{leisner_nonlinear_wavelet_approximation_2003}[Theorem 2.1.1] in $(b)$, which we can apply since $2^{\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}\geq 1$, \item we deduce from Eq. \eqref{eq:Bspline_main} that \begin{align*} \mathrm{supp}(M_{k{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}) = \bigtimes_{j=1}^{d_o}\left[2^{-\left\lfloor\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}\right\rfloor}\ell_{o,j} , 2^{-\left\lfloor\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}\right\rfloor}(\mathfrak{m}+\ell_{o,j})\right]. \end{align*} We also see that \begin{align*} \mathrm{supp}(\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}) = \bigtimes_{j=1}^{d_o}\left[2^{-\left\lfloor\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}\right\rfloor}\ell_{o,j} - s_oh_j , 2^{-\left\lfloor\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}\right\rfloor}(\mathfrak{m}+\ell_{o,j})\right] \end{align*} We deduce that a sufficient condition to guarantee that \begin{align*} \mathrm{supp}\left(\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\right)\cap\mathrm{supp}\left(\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o'}\right) = \emptyset \end{align*} if ${\boldsymbol\ell}_o\neq {\boldsymbol\ell}_o'$ is given by \begin{align*} (\forall j=1,\dots,d_o),\; |h_j|\leq 2^{-\left\lfloor\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}\right\rfloor}\frac{\mathfrak{m}-1}{s_o}. \end{align*} Since $\mathfrak{m}-1\geq s_o$ by choice, and we have for all $i = 1,\dots, d_o$, $|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{1/s_o}\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}$, this sufficient condition is satisfied. Hence \begin{align} \left\langle \Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o},\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o'}\right\rangle_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})} = \left\|\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\right\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}^2\delta_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o'}. \end{align} \item we use Plancherel's Theorem in $(d)$, in a similar way as in Eq. \eqref{eq:plancherel_indicator_inequality}, \item we use Eq. \eqref{eq:lemedotfiveortho} again for step $(e)$, \item we use linearity of $\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}$ for step $(f)$. \end{itemize} Thus we have shown that, for $q=\infty$, \begin{align*} (II) &\lesssim 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\sup_{t>0}\left[t^{-1}\omega_{s_o,2}\left(\sum_ {{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}, 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{\frac{1}{s_o}},\dots, 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{\frac{1}{s_o}}\right)\right]\\ &\lesssim \|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\sup_{t>0}\left[\left(t2^{-\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\right)^{-1}\omega_{s_o,2}\left(\sum_ {{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}, 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{\frac{1}{s_o}},\dots, 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{\frac{1}{s_o}}\right)\right]\\ &\stackrel{(a)}{\lesssim} \|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\sup_{t>0}\left[\int_{t}^{\infty} w^{-s_o}\omega_{s_o+1}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}, w,\dots,w\right)\;\frac{\mathrm{d}w}{w}\right]\\ &\leq \|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\int_{0}^{\infty} w^{-s_o}\omega_{s_o+1}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}, w,\dots,w\right)\;\frac{\mathrm{d}w}{w}\\ &\asymp \|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\left\|\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\right\|_{B^{s_o}_{2,1}(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\\ &\stackrel{(b)}{\lesssim} 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}d_x}{2s_x}}2^{\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}(s_o - d_o/2)}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}1\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\ &\lesssim 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}\left(1 - \frac{d_x}{2s_x}\right)}, \end{align*} where we use the Marchaud-type estimate \citet[Chapter 2, Eq. (10.3)]{devore1993constructive} in $(a)$, we use the sequential Besov norm equivalence \cite{devore1988interpolation}[Theorem 5.1] (see also \citep[Theorem 3.3.3]{leisner_nonlinear_wavelet_approximation_2003}) in $(b)$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the Besov seminorm separately in $x$ (term I) and $o$ (term II) using disjoint supports of the $o$-splines, Plancherel and Leisner's Theorem 2.1.1.

nodes.name: Plancherel indicator inequality (eq:plancherel_indicator_inequality)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} &\quad \|\mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}] \ast (\Delta^r_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}})\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})} = \|\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)} \cdot \mathcal{F}[\Delta^r_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}]\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})} \\ &\leq \|\mathcal{F}[\Delta_{\boldsymbol{h}}^rM_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}]\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})} = \|\Delta_{\boldsymbol{h}}^rM_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}, \end{aligned}
nodes.label: eq:plancherel_indicator_inequality

nodes.name: Orthogonality of o-splines (eq:lemedotfiveortho)
nodes.statement: \left\langle \Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o},\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o'}\right\rangle_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})} = \left\|\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\right\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}^2\delta_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o'}.
nodes.label: eq:lemedotfiveortho

nodes.statement:
Given $\mathcal{D}_1 = \{(\tilde{\mathbf z}_i, \tilde{\mathbf o}_i, \tilde{\mathbf x}_i)\}_{i=1}^{\tilde{n}}$ sampled i.i.d from
the joint distribution $P_{XZO}$, a regularized estimator of $F_\ast$ is obtained as the solution to the following optimization problem:
\begin{talign} \hat{F}_{\xi} := \underset{F \in \mathcal{G}}{arg\,min } \frac{1}{\tilde{n}} \sum_{i=1}^{\tilde{n}} \left\|\phi_{X}(\tilde{\mathbf x}_i) - F(\tilde{\mathbf z}_i, \tilde{\mathbf o}_i)\right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{X}}^2 + \xi\|F\|_{\mathcal{G}}^2,
\end{talign}
where $\xi >0 $ denotes the Stage I regularization parameter.
nodes.name: Stage I: CME regression
nodes.statement_short: Estimate $F_*$ by Tikhonov-regularised vector-valued KRR on $\mathcal{D}_1$.

nodes.statement: \textit{Stage II.} In Stage II, we perform regularized least squares regression in the RKHS $\mathcal{H}_{XO,2}$, using features derived from the estimated conditional mean embedding $\hat{F}_{\xi}$. Specifically, the features are $\hat{F}_{\xi}(Z, O) \otimes \phi_{O,2}(O)$.
nodes.name: Stage II features
nodes.statement_short: Form features $\hat F_\xi(Z,O)\otimes\phi_{O,2}(O)$.

nodes.name: Stage II: KRR on features
nodes.statement_short: Regularised least squares of $y_i$ on the Stage II features over $\mathcal{H}_{XO,2}$.

nodes.statement:
The proof of \Cref{thm:upper_rate} is given in \Cref{sec:proof_upper} in the Supplement. Here we give an outline of our proof to facilitate a deeper understanding of both the assumptions and the results. Define $\bar{f}_{\lambda}$ as the oracle estimator for Stage II with access to the true conditional mean embedding $F_\ast$ and recall $\hat{f}_{\lambda}$ for comparison:
\begin{align}
    \bar{f}_{\lambda} &:= \underset{f\in \mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}{\arg\min} \lambda \|f\|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} + \frac{1}{n}\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n}( y_i - \langle f, F_\ast(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) \otimes \phi_{O, \gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i) \rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} )^2 . \\
    \hat{f}_{\lambda} &:= \underset{f\in \mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}{\arg\min} \lambda \|f\|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} + \frac{1}{n}\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n}( y_i - \langle f, \hat{F}_{\xi}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) \otimes \phi_{O, \gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i) \rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} )^2 .
\end{align}
The proof can be summarized in 3 steps.
We upper bound $\|T[\hat{f}_\lambda]-T[\bar{f}_\lambda]\|_{L^2\left(P_{Z O}\right)}$ in \textit{Step 1} and upper bound $\|T[\bar{f}_\lambda]-T f_*\|_{L^2(P_{Z O})}$ in \textit{Step 2}, which induce an upper bound on $\|T[\hat{f}_\lambda]-T f_*\|_{L^2(P_{Z O})}$ via a triangular inequality. In \textit{Step 3}, we apply the partial measure of ill-posedness to obtain an upper bound on $\|[\hat{f}_\lambda]- f_*\|_{L^2(P_{XO})}$. 
We highlight our technical contributions in each step with \Cref{rem:tensor_krr} and \Cref{rem:no_clipping}.
nodes.name: Oracle estimator and three-step plan
nodes.statement_short: Define the oracle Stage II estimator with the true CME and outline the three steps.

nodes.statement:
\textit{Step 1} We upper bound $\|T[\hat{f}_\lambda]-T[\bar{f}_\lambda]\|_{L^2\left(P_{Z O}\right)}$. By their definition in Eq.~\eqref{eq:hat_f_lambda_main} and Eq.~\eqref{eq:bar_f_lambda_main}, the discrepancy between $\hat{f}_\lambda$ and $\bar{f}_\lambda$ arises solely from the difference between $\hat{F}_{\xi}$ and $F_\ast$; hence it corresponds to Stage I error. First, we prove in \Cref{prop:T_hat_f_bar_f} that $\|T[\hat{f}_\lambda]-T[\bar{f}_\lambda]\|_{L^2\left(P_{Z O}\right)}$ can be upper bounded by an expression involving $\|\hat{F}_{\xi}-F_*\|_{\mathcal{G}}$ and $\|F_*-\hat{F}_{\xi}\|_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}; \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x})}$, where we recall that $\mathcal{G}$ denotes the unique vector-valued RKHS induced by
the operator-valued kernel $K$ defined in Eq. \eqref{eq:op_val_kernel}. 
To obtain high-probability upper bounds on both of these quantities, we adapt the existing optimal learning rates on CME from \citet{lietal2022optimal} to our setting with a tensor product RKHS. 
The fact that we require upper learning rate for $\|F_*-\hat{F}_{\xi}\|_{\mathcal{G}}$ imposes the conditions $m_o>t_o$ and $m_z>t_z$, so the CME $F_\ast$ lies in a smoother space than RKHS $\mathcal{G}$. Specifically, $F_{\ast}$ belongs to the \emph{power space} $[\mathcal{G}]^{m^{\dag}}$ (See Eq.~\eqref{eq:F_ast_power_space}).
In addition, the constraints $2 t_o>m_o$ and $2 t_z>m_z$ reflect the saturation effect inherent in Tikhonov regularization~\citep{bauer2007regularization, lu2024saturation, meunier2024optimalratesvectorvaluedspectral}. 
These constraints can be removed to allow for greater smoothness of $F_\ast$ by employing spectral regularization~\citep{meunier2024optimalratesvectorvaluedspectral}. 
The appearance of an arbitrarily small $\zeta>0$ in Stage I regularization parameter $\xi$ reflects the fact that, after reordering, the eigenvalues of the tensor product operator exhibit slower decay than those of the individual components, owing to an extra logarithmic term~\citep{krieg2018tensor}.

\begin{rem}[Tensor product kernel ridge regression] In the above step, we generalize the upper learning rate for vector-valued kernel ridge regression to the setting of tensor product kernels (See \Cref{prop:cme_rate}). Although tensor product kernels have been widely used in kernel-based hypothesis tests~\citep{gretton2007kernel,GreGyo10,SejGreBer13,gretton2015characteristic,ZhaFilGreSej18,AlbLaurMarMey22,szabo2018characteristic},  kernel independent component analysis \citep{BacJor02,SheJegGre09},  and feature selection \citep{SonSmoGreBedetal12,LiPogSutGre21}, they have  been less well studied  in kernel ridge regression, with the exception of \citet{hang2021optimal} for Gaussian kernels. Our analysis is also applicable to real-valued kernel ridge regression with tensor product kernels.
\end{rem}
nodes.name: Step 1: Stage I error
nodes.statement_short: Bound the projected Stage I error via CME learning rates in a tensor-product RKHS.

nodes.statement:
\textit{Step 2} We upper bound $\|T[\bar{f}_\lambda]-T f_*\|_{L^2(P_{Z O})}$. We follow the approach in \citet{blanchard2018optimal, meunier2024nonparametricinstrumentalregressionkernel}, where it is observed (in the standard NPIV case) that this term corresponds to the learning risk of a kernel ridge regression problem with an appropriately defined RKHS $\mathcal{H}_{FO} \subseteq \{\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O}\to \mathbb{R}\}$, namely the RKHS induced by the feature map $(\mathbf z,\mathbf o)\mapsto F_{\ast}(\mathbf z,\mathbf o)\otimes \phi_{O,2}(\mathbf o)$. We refer the reader to \Cref{sec:defi_H_FO} in the Supplement for the definition of $\mathcal{H}_{FO}$. Our construction is adapted from \citet[Appendix E.1.2]{meunier2024nonparametricinstrumentalregressionkernel}. However, unlike \citet{blanchard2018optimal, meunier2024nonparametricinstrumentalregressionkernel} who only consider fixed RKHSs, we employ tensor product Gaussian RKHS $\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x, \gamma_o}$ with \emph{adaptive} length-scales $\gamma_x, \gamma_o$ (as in Eq.~\eqref{eq:lengthscale_main}) to capture the anisotropic smoothness of $f_\ast \in B^{s_x, s_o}_{2,\infty}(\mathcal{X}\times \mathcal{O})$~\citep{hang2021optimal}. 
When $\eta_1 = 0$, our choice of length-scales $\gamma_x, \gamma_o$ coincides with that of kernel ridge regression in \citet{hang2021optimal}. 
The logarithmic factor \smash{$(\log n)^{\frac{d_x+d_o+1}{2}}$} in Eq.~\eqref{eq:upper_rate} arises from the entropy numbers of the Gaussian RKHS in this step (see \Cref{sec:capacity} in the Supplement and \citet[Proposition 1]{hang2021optimal}). 
\begin{rem}[Gaussian kernel ridge regression with Besov space target functions] To establish learning rates for kernel ridge regression, there are two main techniques in the literature: the empirical process technique~\citep{steinwart2008support,steinwart2009optimal} and the integral operator technique~\citep{fischer2020sobolev,Lin_2020,smale2007learning,caponnetto2007optimal,blanchard2018optimal}. Previous works on Gaussian kernel ridge regression with Besov space targets~\citep{eberts2013optimal, hang2021optimal,hamm2021adaptive}  rely on an oracle inequality proved via empirical process techniques~\citep[Theorem 7.23]{steinwart2008support}, which necessitates a clipping operation on the estimator. 
    On the other hand, the integral operator technique avoids the clipping operation, but it requires the target $f_\ast$ in a power space of the RKHS---a condition known as the source condition~\citep[SRC]{fischer2020sobolev}---which does not hold for Besov space targets and Gaussian RKHSs. 

    In our proof in step 2, we prove an upper learning rate of Gaussian kernel ridge regression with Besov space target functions \emph{without} clipping the estimator.
    Specifically, we combine the two techniques above, in that we bound the approximation error with \citet{hang2021optimal}, while we bound the estimation error with the integral operator technique~\citep{fischer2020sobolev}.
    To be precise, define 
    \begin{align} f_{\lambda} := arg\,min_{f\in \mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}\lambda\|f\|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} + \|T([f] - f_{\ast})\|^2_{L^2(P_{ZO})}. 
    \end{align}
    The learning risk $ \|T([\bar{f}_{\lambda}] - f_\ast) \|_{L^2(P_{ZO})}$ can be decomposed into an estimation error term $\|T([\bar{f}_{\lambda}] - [f_{\lambda}])\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})}$ and an approximation error term $\|T([f_{\lambda}] - f_{\ast})\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})}$. 
    We upper bound the estimation error with \citet[Theorem 16]{fischer2020sobolev}, once we prove that the RKHS $\mathcal{H}_{FO}$ satisfies an \emph{embedding property} (see \citet[EMB]{fischer2020sobolev}), which avoids the clipping operation.
    We upper bound the approximation error with \citet[Theorem 4]{hang2021optimal}, which avoids the source condition. 
\end{rem}
nodes.name: Step 2: Stage II error
nodes.statement_short: Bound the projected Stage II error as KRR risk in $\mathcal{H}_{FO}$ with adaptive Gaussian lengthscales.

nodes.name: Step 3: remove T
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality, then partial ill-posedness with auxiliary $f_{aux}$ to pass from projected to $L^2$ risk.

nodes.statement:
We give an outline of our proof for \Cref{thm:lower_rate} to facilitate a deeper
understanding of both the assumptions and the results. The full proof is in \Cref{sec:NPIR_lower_appendix} in the Supplementary. The primary strategy in deriving minimax lower bounds is to construct a family of distributions that are similar enough so that they are statistically indistinguishable, but for which the target function of interest is maximally separated. 
This implies no estimator can have error uniformly smaller than this separation.
nodes.name: Strategy
nodes.statement_short: Construct statistically indistinguishable but well-separated hypotheses.

nodes.statement:
Following prior work in the literature~\citep{chen2011rate,meunier2024nonparametricinstrumentalregressionkernel}, we observe that NPIV-O in Eq.~\eqref{eq:npiv_o_intro} is statistically more challenging than the reduced form non-parametric indirect regression with observed covariates (NPIR-O) with a \emph{known} operator $T:L^2(P_{XO})\to L^2(P_{ZO})$. The NPIR-O model is defined below
\begin{align} Y= (Tf_*)(Z, O) + \upsilon,
\end{align}
where $\upsilon$ is a random variable such that $\mathbb{E}[\upsilon\mid Z,O] = 0$, and it satisfies \Cref{ass:subgaussian}, and where $T$ satisfies \Cref{ass:T_injective}, \Cref{ass:T_contractivity} and the associated conditional distribution $P_{X\mid Z,O}$ satisfies \Cref{assn: technical}. We refer the reader to \Cref{sec:npir_reduction} in the Supplementary Material for a detailed definition of the NPIR-O model class. We formally prove in \Cref{lem:npir_o_more_informative} in the Supplementary that it suffices to construct a minimax lower bound for the NPIR-O model.
nodes.name: Reduction to NPIR-O
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the NPIR-O model with known $T$.

nodes.statement:
To this end, we adapt Theorem 20 of \cite{fischer2020sobolev}, which is itself an adaptation of Proposition 2.3 of \citet{Tsybakov}. Recall that the \emph{Kullback-Leibler divergence} of two probability measures $P_1, P_2$ on some measurable space $(\Omega,\mathcal{A})$ is given by $\mathrm{KL}(P_1,P_2) := \int_{\Omega}\log (\frac{\mathrm{d}P_1}{\mathrm{d}P_2} )\;\mathrm{d}P_1$ 
if $P_1$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $P_2$, and $+\infty$ otherwise.
nodes.name: Recall KL divergence and Fischer–Steinwart Theorem 20
nodes.statement_short: Recall the KL divergence used in the Fano-type bound.

nodes.name: Family of Gaussian conditional laws
nodes.statement_short: Build $P_i$ with $Y|Z,O\sim N(Tf_i,\sigma^2)$ via a fixed marginal and a smooth copula.

nodes.statement:
Concretely, we fix $P_{ZO}$ to be the Lebesgue measure over $\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O}$. Without loss of generality, we take $\mathcal{X} = [-0.5, 0.5]^{d_x}$ rather than $[0,1]^{d_x}$.  By working with a symmetric domain, we exploit the fact that even functions have real-valued Fourier transforms, which simplify our subsequent calculations. We fix $P_{X}$ via the density function
\begin{talign} p_X(\mathbf x)\propto \prod_{i=1}^{d_x} g_i(x_i), \quad g_i(x_i) := \exp\left(-\frac{2}{1 - 4x_i^2}\right) \mathbbm{1}_{x_i \in [-0.5, 0.5]},
\end{talign}
where each $g_i$ is a smooth, compactly supported \emph{bump function}. We fix an arbitrary smooth copula~\citep{nelsen2006introduction}, such that $P_{X\mid Z,O}$ satisfies \Cref{assn: technical} and $T$ satisfies \Cref{ass:T_contractivity} with parameter $\eta_1>0$.
nodes.name: Fix marginals and copula
nodes.statement_short: Lebesgue $P_{ZO}$, bump-density $P_X$ on a symmetric cube, smooth copula.

nodes.statement:
The main technical challenge of the minimax lower bound is the construction of the function class $\mathfrak{F}$ whose each element $f_i$ induces a conditional distribution $P_{X\mid Z, O}$.
Our goal is to design $\mathfrak{F}$ so that it satisfies three desirable properties: 1) we want $\mathfrak{F}\in B_{2,\infty}^{s_x,s_o}(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})$ as per \Cref{ass:f_ast}. 
2) we want the size of $\mathfrak{F}$ to be large to enable the application of \citet[Theorem 20]{fischer2020sobolev}. 
3) we want all elements of $\mathfrak{F}$ to exhibit high partial Fourier frequency such that after applying $T$, the resulting functions become difficult to distinguish. 
This increases the intrinsic difficulty of the problem and yields a tighter lower bound. 
The construction of such a function class satisfying the first two properties is standard and can be achieved using anisotropic B-splines~\citep{ibragimov1984asymptotic, suzuki2021deep,schmidt2020nonparametric}. 
However, the third property poses a challenge: the Fourier transform of B-splines has full support. 
Consequently, conventional B-splines cannot enforce the desired partial high-frequency restriction. To address this limitation, we convolve the B-splines with a high frequency bandpass filter in the $X$-direction. 
Since convolution acts as a smoothing operator, the function class constructed with such modified B-splines remains in the Besov space.
nodes.name: Three desired properties of the class
nodes.statement_short: Need Besov membership, large size, and high partial Fourier frequency.

nodes.statement:
To start with, we introduce the definition of anisotropic B-splines~\citep{leisner_nonlinear_wavelet_approximation_2003}. 


\begin{defi}[Anisotropic B-spline \citep{leisner_nonlinear_wavelet_approximation_2003}] The cardinal B-spline of order $\mathfrak{m}\in \mathbb{N}$ is defined as the repeated $\mathfrak{m}$ times convolution $\iota_{\mathfrak{m}} = \iota_{0}\ast \dots \ast \iota_0$ where $\iota_0$ is the indicator function $\mathbbm{1}_{[0,1]}$. Let $d$ denote the ambient dimension, and let $\boldsymbol{s} = (s_1,\dots, s_d)$ denote a smoothness vector. Define the notation $\underline{s} = \min(s_1,\dots,s_{d})$ and $s_i^\prime := \frac{\underline{s}}{s_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq d$.  The (anisotropic) B-spline  of order $\mathfrak{m}$ with resolution $\mathfrak{K} \in \mathbb{N}_+$ and location vector $ {\boldsymbol\ell} \in  \prod_{i=1}^{d}\{-\mathfrak{m},-\mathfrak{m}+1,\dots, 2^{\left\lfloor \mathfrak{K} s_i^\prime \right\rfloor} \}$ is defined as $M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}}(\mathbf x) = \prod_{i=1}^{d} \iota_{\mathfrak{m}} (2^{\lfloor \mathfrak{K} s_i^\prime \rfloor}x_i - \ell_i)$.
\end{defi}
\noindent

Let $\mathfrak{m} > s_x \vee s_o$ be a non-negative even integer. 
The resolution $\mathfrak{K} = \mathfrak{K}(n)$ is defined later in Eq.~\eqref{eq:choice_k_lb}, such that $\mathfrak{K} \to \infty$ as $n\to\infty$.
nodes.name: Anisotropic B-splines
nodes.statement_short: Introduce anisotropic B-splines and the resolution $\mathfrak{K}$.

nodes.statement:
The B-spline basis in the $O$-direction follows the standard construction. Define the set of location vectors $\mathcal{L}_O$ and the associated B-splines
\begin{talign} \mathcal{L}_O := \left\{ 2 \mathfrak{m} \mathbb{N}\cap \left\{0, \dots, 2^{\left\lfloor \mathfrak{K}\frac{\underline{s}}{s_o}\right\rfloor}\right\}\right\}^{d_o} , \quad M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}(\mathbf o) = \prod_{j=1}^{d_o}\iota_{\mathfrak{m}}\left(2^{\left\lfloor \frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}\right\rfloor} o_j - \ell_{o,j}\right).
\end{talign}
Note that here we enforce all location vectors to be a multiple of $2\mathfrak{m}$ such that the $\{M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\}_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o\in\mathcal{L}_O}$ have disjoint supports, which will simplify the calculations later on.
nodes.name: O-direction basis
nodes.statement_short: Disjointly supported B-splines in $o$.

nodes.name: X-direction band-pass basis
nodes.statement_short: Convolve B-splines with inverse Fourier transforms of high-frequency boxes; convolution theorem gives high-frequency support.

nodes.statement:
Define the basis $\Omega_{\mathfrak{K}({\boldsymbol\ell}_x,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}(\mathbf x,\mathbf o) := \Omega_{\mathfrak{K}{\boldsymbol\ell}_x}(\mathbf x) \cdot M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}(\mathbf o)$ and the set of all location vectors $\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_X\times\mathcal{L}_O$. 
We have $|\mathcal{L}| \asymp \zeta^{-d_x}2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}(\frac{d_x}{s_x} + \frac{d_o}{s_o})}$. 
We construct a function class $\mathfrak{F}$ as follows:
\begin{talign} \mathfrak{F}:= \left\{f_{\mathbf v}: f_{\mathbf v}(\mathbf x,\mathbf o) =  2^{-\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}\left(1 - \frac{d_x}{2s_x}\right)} \sum_{({\boldsymbol\ell}_x,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o)\in \mathcal{L}} \beta_{\mathbf v({\boldsymbol\ell}_x,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}\Omega_{\mathfrak{K}({\boldsymbol\ell}_x,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}(\mathbf x,\mathbf o)\,\middle\vert\,  \mathbf v\in \{0,1\}^{|\mathcal{L}|}\right\},
\end{talign}
where $\beta_{\mathbf v({\boldsymbol\ell}_x,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}\in\{0,1\}$ is the value assigned by $\mathbf v\in \{0,1\}^{|\mathcal{L}|}$ to the location vector $({\boldsymbol\ell}_x,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o)\in\mathcal{L}$. 
Specifically, for each $f_{\mathbf v}\in\mathfrak{F}$ and for a fixed $\mathbf o\in\mathcal{O}$, we can see that $f_{\mathbf v}(\cdot, \mathbf o)$ is constructed by applying a sum of \emph{frequency masks} indexed by ${\boldsymbol\ell}_x\in\mathcal{L}_X$ to the original B-spline $M_{\mathfrak{K},-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}$,
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{F}[f_{\mathbf v}(\cdot, \mathbf o)](\boldsymbol{\omega}_x) = \mathcal{F}\left[M_{\mathfrak{K},-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\right](\boldsymbol{\omega}_x) \cdot \Big(  \sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o\in \mathcal{L}_O} \underbrace{ \sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_x \in \mathcal{L}_X} \beta_{\mathbf v({\boldsymbol\ell}_x,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o)} \mathbbm{1}_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_x}\left(2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_x}}\boldsymbol{\omega}_x\right)}_{\text{frequency masks}} M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}(\mathbf o) \Big).
\end{align*}
\Cref{fig:masks_visualisation} is provided to illustrate this effect of frequency masking.
nodes.name: Function class F
nodes.statement_short: Define the hypercube class $\mathfrak{F}$ of masked spline sums.

nodes.name: Besov membership and Gaussian models
nodes.statement_short: Show $\mathfrak{F}\subseteq\mathfrak{S}$ and define the Gaussian conditional laws $P_v$.

nodes.name: Separation and KL bounds
nodes.statement_short: Gilbert–Varshamov pruning gives $L^2$ separation and small KL divergence.

nodes.statement: Finally, we take $\zeta = (\log n)^2$, we apply \citet[Theorem 20]{fischer2020sobolev} and the general reduction scheme in \citet[Section 2.2]{Tsybakov} to obtain the desired minimax lower bound.
nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement_short: Choose $\zeta$ and apply Fischer–Steinwart Theorem 20 with Tsybakov's reduction.

nodes.name: Test function
nodes.statement_short: Define a band-limited $f_{\gamma,\epsilon}$ on the annulus.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T

nodes.name: Apply both assumptions
nodes.statement_short: $f_{\gamma,\epsilon}$ lies in LF and HF; combine both inequalities.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T

nodes.name: Let epsilon to 0
nodes.statement_short: Divide by the norm and let $\epsilon\to0$.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T

nodes.statement: Taking the limit $\gamma\to 1$ in Eq.~\eqref{eq:lem_eta_key}, we find $c_0c_1 \geq 1$. Then since Eq.~\eqref{eq:lem_eta_key} holds for all $\gamma\in (0,1)$, we find that $\eta_1\leq \eta_0$.
nodes.name: Conclude eta_1 <= eta_0
nodes.statement_short: Let $\gamma\to1$ and use the inequality for all $\gamma$.
nodes.section: A Examples for the partial smoothing effect of T

nodes.name: Stage 1 closed form
nodes.statement_short: Kernel ridge closed form for $\hat F_\xi$ via the Stage I Gram matrix.

nodes.name: Stage 2 closed form
nodes.statement_short: Dual KRR solution with Gram $(J^TK_{\tilde X\tilde X}J)\odot K_{OO;2}$ and prediction at a test point.

nodes.name: Eigenvalue decay
nodes.statement_short: Corollary C.1 and Lemma C.1 with $p=1/\log n$ bound $\mu_{FO,i}$.

nodes.statement:
Next, we use \cite[Proposition 3]{caponnetto2007optimal} (with error corrected in \cite{sutherland2021fixingerrorcaponnettovito}) to obtain
\begin{align}
    \mathcal{N}_{FO}(\lambda) &\leq \frac{\pi/(2\log n)}{\sin(\pi/(2\log n))}\left( (C \log n)^{2(d_x+d_o+1) \log n}(\gamma_x^{d_x}\gamma_o^{d_o})^{-2\log n} \right)^{\frac{1}{2\log n}}\lambda^{-(2\log n)^{-1}}\nonumber\\
    &= \frac{\pi/(2\log n)}{\sin(\pi/(2\log n))} (C\log n)^{(d_x+d_o+1)} \left(\gamma_x^{d_x}\gamma_o^{d_o}\right)^{-1}\lambda^{-(2\log n)^{-1}}\nonumber\\
    &\stackrel{(i)}{\leq} 3C^{(d_x+d_o+1)} (\log n)^{(d_x+d_o+1)} 
    \left(\gamma_x^{d_x}\gamma_o^{d_o}\right)^{-1}n^{(2\log n)^{-1}}\nonumber\\
    &\stackrel{(ii)}{=} 3\sqrt{e} C^{(d_x+d_o+1)} (\log n)^{(d_x+d_o+1)} \left(\gamma_x^{d_x}\gamma_o^{d_o}\right)^{-1}\nonumber\\
    &= C'(\log n)^{d_x+d_o + 1} \left(\gamma_x^{d_x}\gamma_o^{d_o}\right)^{-1}\nonumber,
\end{align}
where $C' = \sqrt{e} 3C^{(d_x+d_o+1)}$. 
In the above chain of derivations, $(i)$ holds because $\frac{t}{\sin t} \leq 3$ for $t \leq \pi/2$ and $\pi/(2\log n) \leq \pi/2$ and $(ii)$ holds because $n^{\frac{1}{2\log n}} = \sqrt{e}$ for $n > 1$.
nodes.name: Effective dimension
nodes.statement_short: Caponnetto–De Vito Proposition 3 converts eigendecay into the effective-dimension bound.

nodes.name: Cover of the Gaussian RKHS ball
nodes.statement_short: Fix an $\epsilon$-net of the unit ball of $\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}$.

nodes.name: Lift f to g
nodes.statement_short: Represent $f=Vg$ with $\|g\|\le1+\tilde\epsilon$ and pick a close net point.

nodes.name: Jensen bound
nodes.statement_short: Jensen's inequality shows $Vg_i$ form a net of $B_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}}$.

nodes.statement: Hence $e_i(\mathrm{id}: \mathcal{H}_{FO}\hookrightarrow L^2(P_{ZO})) \leq \epsilon(1+\tilde{\epsilon})$. Since $\epsilon > e_i(\mathrm{id}:\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}\hookrightarrow L^2(P_{XO}))$ and $\tilde{\epsilon}>0$ are arbitrary, it follows that $e_i(\mathrm{id}:\mathcal{H}_{FO}\hookrightarrow L^2(P_{ZO}))\leq e_i(\mathrm{id}:\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}\hookrightarrow L^2(P_{XO}))$.
nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement_short: Let $\epsilon,\tilde\epsilon$ approach their limits.

nodes.name: Embed into mixed Sobolev
nodes.statement_short: Lemma C.3.

nodes.name: Interpolation space into L-infinity
nodes.statement_short: Lemmas C.6 and C.5.

nodes.name: Change of measure
nodes.statement_short: Lemma C.4 transfers to $L^2(P_{ZO})$.

nodes.statement: Finally, by \cite{steinwart2012mercer}[Theorem 4.6], $(L^2(P_{ZO}), [\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(P_{ZO})})_{\theta,2} \cong [\mathcal{H}_{FO}]^{\theta}_{L^2(P_{ZO})}$ with the constant of equivalence depends only on $\theta$. Putting it back to Eq. \eqref{eq: chain_embedding} completes the proof of the proposition.
nodes.name: Identify with power space
nodes.statement_short: Interpolation space equals the power space.

nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{id}: \mathcal{H}_{FO}\hookrightarrow L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})$ denote the canonical inclusion map. Since we have $(\ker \mathrm{id})^{\perp} \cong [\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})}$, we may represent an arbitrary element of $[\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})}$ as $[f]$, where $f\in (\ker \mathrm{id})^{\perp}$. Moreover, we have $\|[f]\|_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})} = \|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}}$. We fix $f$ for the remainder of the proof.
nodes.name: Representative f
nodes.statement_short: Fix a representative in $(\ker\,\mathrm{id})^\perp$.

nodes.statement:
Let $\boldsymbol\alpha \in \mathbb{N}^{d_z}$ with $|\boldsymbol\alpha| \leq m_z$ and $\boldsymbol\beta\in \mathbb{N}^{d_o}$ with $|\boldsymbol\beta| \leq m_o$, we have for any $f\in\mathcal{H}_{FO}$,
\begin{small}
\begin{align*}
    &\left\|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta}_{\mathbf o}f\right\|^2_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O};\mathbb{R})} = \int_{\mathcal{Z}}\int_{\mathcal{O}} \left(\partial_{\mathbf z}^{\boldsymbol\alpha}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta}_{\mathbf o}f(\mathbf z,\mathbf o)\right)^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf z\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\
    \stackrel{(a)}{=}& \int_{\mathcal{Z}}\int_{\mathcal{O}}\left(\partial_{\mathbf z}^{\boldsymbol\alpha}\partial_{\mathbf o}^{\boldsymbol\beta}\int_{\mathcal{X}} w(\mathbf x,\mathbf o) p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\right)^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf z\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\
    \stackrel{(b)}{=}& \int_{\mathcal{Z}}\int_{\mathcal{O}}\left(\sum_{\boldsymbol\beta_1+\boldsymbol\beta_2 = \boldsymbol\beta}\binom{\boldsymbol\beta}{\boldsymbol\beta_1}\int_{\mathcal{X}} \partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}_{\mathbf o} w(\mathbf x,\mathbf o) \partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_2}_{\mathbf o}p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\right)^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf z\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\
    \stackrel{(c)}{\leq}& \int_{\mathcal{Z}}\int_{\mathcal{O}}\left(\sum_{\boldsymbol\beta_1+\boldsymbol\beta_2 = \boldsymbol\beta}\binom{\boldsymbol\beta}{\boldsymbol\beta_1}\left(\int_{\mathcal{X}} \left(\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}_{\mathbf o} w(\mathbf x,\mathbf o) \right)^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \left(\int_{\mathcal{X}} \left(\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_2}_{\mathbf o}p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\right)^2 \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf z\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\
    \leq & \left(\sum_{\boldsymbol\beta_1+\boldsymbol\beta_2 = \beta}\binom{\boldsymbol\beta}{\boldsymbol\beta_1}\right)^2 \left(\max_{\boldsymbol\beta_2\leq \beta}\sup_{\mathbf x,\mathbf z,\mathbf o}\left|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_2}_{\mathbf o}p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\right|^2\right) \int_{\mathcal{Z}}\int_{\mathcal{O}} \max_{\boldsymbol\beta_1\leq \beta} \int_{\mathcal{X}}\left(\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}_{\mathbf o}w(\mathbf x,\mathbf o)\right)^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf z\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\
    =& \left(\sum_{\boldsymbol\beta_1+\boldsymbol\beta_2 = \beta}\binom{\boldsymbol\beta}{\boldsymbol\beta_1}\right)^2 \left(\max_{\boldsymbol\beta_2\leq \beta}\sup_{\mathbf x,\mathbf z,\mathbf o}\left|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_2}_{\mathbf o}p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\right|^2\right) \max_{\boldsymbol\beta_1\leq \beta} \int_{\mathcal{O}}\int_{\mathcal{X}}\left(\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}_{\mathbf o}w(\mathbf x,\mathbf o)\right)^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\
    \stackrel{(d)}{=}& c_{m_o, d_o}\left(\max_{\boldsymbol\beta_2\leq \beta}\sup_{\mathbf x,\mathbf z,\mathbf o}\left|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_2}_{\mathbf o}p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\right|^2\right)  \gamma_o^{-2|\beta|} \|w\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}^2\\
    \leq & c_{m_o,d_o} \left(\max_{\boldsymbol\alpha\leq m_z}\max_{\boldsymbol\beta\leq m_o}\sup_{\mathbf x,\mathbf z,\mathbf o}\left|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta}_{\mathbf o}p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\right|^2\right)  \gamma_o^{-2m_o} \|w\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}^2 ,
\end{align*}
\end{small}
where $(a)$ follows from the fact that, for any $f\in\mathcal{H}_{FO}$, there exists $w\in\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}$ such that $f(\mathbf z,\mathbf o) = \langle w, F_{\ast}(\mathbf z,\mathbf o)\otimes\phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o)\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} = \int_{\mathcal{X}}w(\mathbf x,\mathbf o)p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x$ and $\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}} = \|w\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}$.
nodes.name: Derivative bound chain
nodes.statement_short: Bound mixed derivatives of $f$ by density derivatives and $\gamma_o^{-m_o}\|w\|$.

nodes.statement: $(b)$ follows from generalized Leibniz's rule and differentiation under the integral sign \cite{klenke2013probability}[Theorem 6.28], $(c)$ follows from a Cauchy-Schwarz inequality.
nodes.name: Justify (b),(c)
nodes.statement_short: Leibniz rule, differentiation under the integral, Cauchy–Schwarz.

nodes.statement:
$(d)$ follows from the following arguments.

From \citet[Theorem 4.21]{steinwart2008support}, we know that 
for any $w\in \mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}$, there exists $g\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})$ such that 
\begin{align*}
    w(\mathbf x,\mathbf o) = \langle g, \Phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x)\Phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o)\rangle_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})},\quad \|w\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} = \|g\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})},
\end{align*}
with $\Phi_{\gamma_x}: \mathcal{X}\to L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x}), \Phi_{\gamma_o}: \mathcal{O}\to L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})$ defined in \citet[Lemma 4.45]{steinwart2008support}.
We have
\begin{align*}
    &\int_{\mathcal{O}} \int_{\mathcal{X}}\left(\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}_{\mathbf o}w(\mathbf x,\mathbf o)\right)^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\
    =& \int_{\mathcal{O}}\int_{\mathcal{X}}\left(\partial_{\mathbf o}^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}} g(\mathbf x',\mathbf o')\Phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x)(\mathbf x')\Phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o)(\mathbf o')\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x'\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o'\right)^{2}\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\
    \stackrel{(i)}{=}& \int_{\mathcal{O}}\int_{\mathcal{X}}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}} g(\mathbf x',\mathbf o')\Phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x)(\mathbf x')\partial_{\mathbf o}^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}(\Phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o)(\mathbf o'))\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x'\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o'\right)^{2}\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\
    \leq &  \|g\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})}\int_{\mathcal{O}}\int_{\mathcal{X}}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}} \left(\Phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x)(\mathbf x')\partial_{\mathbf o}^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}(\Phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o)(\mathbf o'))\right)^{2}\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x'\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o'\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\
    = & \|g\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})}\int_{\mathcal{O}}\int_{\mathcal{X}}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x}}(\Phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x)(\mathbf x'))^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x'\right) \left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_o}}\left(\partial_{\mathbf o}^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}(\Phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o)(\mathbf o'))\right)^{2}\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o'\right)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\
    \stackrel{(ii)}{=} & \|g\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})}\int_{\mathcal{O}} \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_o}}\left(\partial_{\mathbf o}^{\boldsymbol\beta_1}(\Phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o)(\mathbf o'))\right)^{2}\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o'\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\\
    \stackrel{(iii)}{\leq} & \|g\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})}c_{\boldsymbol\beta_1, d_o}\gamma_o^{-2|\boldsymbol\beta_1|} \\
    = & \|w\|^2_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} c_{\boldsymbol\beta_1, d_o}\gamma_o^{-2|\boldsymbol\beta_1|},
\end{align*}
where we're allowed to exchange differentiation and integration in $(i)$ using the differentiation lemma \cite{klenke2013probability}[Theorem 6.28], $(ii)$ follows from the fact that
\begin{align*}
    \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x}}(\Phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x)(\mathbf x'))^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x' = \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x}} \left(\frac{2^{d_x/2}}{\pi^{d_x/4}\gamma_x^{d_x/2}}\exp\left(-2\frac{\|\mathbf x - \mathbf x'\|^2_{2}}{\gamma_x^2}\right)\right)^2\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x' = 1,
\end{align*}
and $(iii)$ follows from the proof of \cite{steinwart2008support}[Theorem 4.48]. Here $c_{\boldsymbol\beta_1,d_o}$ is a constant only depending on $\boldsymbol\beta_1,d_o$.
nodes.name: Justify (d)
nodes.statement_short: Derivatives of Gaussian feature maps scale like $\gamma_o^{-|\beta_1|}$.

nodes.statement:
Hence we've shown
\begin{align*}
    &\|f\|^2_{MW^{m_z,m_o}_2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O};\mathbb{R})}\\
    = & \sum_{\boldsymbol\alpha\leq m_z, \boldsymbol\beta\leq m_o}\left\|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta}_{\mathbf o}f\right\|^2_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O};\mathbb{R})}\\
    \lesssim & \sum_{\boldsymbol\alpha \leq m_z, \boldsymbol\beta\leq m_o} \left(\max_{\boldsymbol\alpha\leq m_z}\max_{\boldsymbol\beta\leq m_o}\sup_{\mathbf x,\mathbf z,\mathbf o}\left|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta}_{\mathbf o}p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\right|^2\right)  \gamma_o^{-2m_o} \|w\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}^2\\
    = & \left(\sum_{\alpha \leq m_z, \boldsymbol\beta\leq m_o} 1\right) \left(\max_{\boldsymbol\alpha\leq m_z}\max_{\boldsymbol\beta\leq m_o}\sup_{\mathbf x,\mathbf z,\mathbf o}\left|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z}\partial^{\boldsymbol\beta}_{\mathbf o}p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z,\mathbf o)\right|^2\right)  \gamma_o^{-2m_o} \|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}}^2 \\
    \lesssim &\rho^2 \gamma_o^{-2m_o} \|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}}^2 \\
    = & \rho^2 \gamma_o^{-2m_o} \|[f]\|_{[\mathcal{H}_{FO}]_{L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O})}}^2 .
\end{align*}
The second last inequality holds by Assumption \ref{assn: technical}.
This concludes the proof.
nodes.name: Sum over multi-indices
nodes.statement_short: Sum to get the mixed Sobolev norm bound.

nodes.statement:
We adapt the proof of \cite{kanagawa2018gaussianprocesseskernelmethods}[Lemma A.2, Corollary 4.13].
We have, for any $x \in (L^2(\mathcal{Z}), W)_{\theta,2}$,
\begin{align*}
    \|x\|_{\left(L^2(\mathcal{Z}), W\right)_{\theta,2}}&=  \left(\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(t^{-\theta}K\left(t,x;L^2(\mathcal{Z}),W\right)\right)^{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}t}{t}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\&= \left(\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(t^{-\theta}\inf_{y\in W}\left\{\|x-y\|_{L^2(\mathcal{Z})} + t\|y\|_{W}\right\}\right)^{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}t}{t}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    &\leq \left(\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(t^{-\theta}\inf_{y\in \mathcal{H}}\left\{\|x-y\|_{L^2(\mathcal{Z})} + t\|y\|_{W}\right\}\right)^{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}t}{t}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    &\leq \left(\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(t^{-\theta}\inf_{y\in \mathcal{H}}\left\{\|x-y\|_{L^2(\mathcal{Z})} + tc\|y\|_{\mathcal{H}}\right\}\right)^{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}t}{t}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    &= c^\theta \left(\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(\left(tc \right)^{-\theta}\inf_{y\in \mathcal{H}}\left\{\|x-y\|_{L^2(\mathcal{Z})} + tc \|y\|_{\mathcal{H}}\right\}\right)^{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}t}{t}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    &= c^{\theta}\left(\int_{0}^{\infty}\left(t^{-\theta}K\left(t,x;L^2(\mathcal{Z}),\mathcal{H}\right)\right)^{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}t}{t}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    &= c^{\theta}\|x\|_{\left(L^2(\mathcal{Z}), \mathcal{H}\right)_{\theta,2}} .
\end{align*}
Notice that we correct an error in \cite{kanagawa2018gaussianprocesseskernelmethods} which obtained the exponent $-\theta$ instead of $\theta$ due to an error in the change of variables argument in $(a)$.
nodes.name: Compare K-functionals
nodes.statement_short: Compare norms of the two interpolation spaces.

nodes.statement: Now we have proved that $(L^2(\mathcal{Z}), \mathcal{H})_{\theta,2} \hookrightarrow (L^2(\mathcal{Z}), W)_{\theta,2}$ and $\left\| (L^2(\mathcal{Z}), \mathcal{H})_{\theta,2} \hookrightarrow (L^2(\mathcal{Z}), W)_{\theta,2} \right\| \leq c^\theta$.
nodes.name: Intermediate embedding
nodes.statement_short: Record the embedding with norm $c^\theta$.

nodes.statement: On the other hand, by assumption, we have $(L^2(\mathcal{Z}), W)_{\theta,2} \hookrightarrow L^\infty(\mathcal{Z})$. Consequently, we have $(L^2(\mathcal{Z}), \mathcal{H})_{\theta,2} \hookrightarrow W(L^2(\mathcal{Z}), W)_{\theta,2} \hookrightarrow L^{\infty}(\mathcal{Z})$. The embedding norm is bounded by $c^{\theta}c_0$, where $c_0$ depends only on $\theta$, $m$, and $d_z$.
nodes.name: Compose embeddings
nodes.statement_short: Compose with the assumed $L^\infty$ embedding.

nodes.statement: See \cite[Equation 1.13]{schmeisser2007recent} for the result where the domain is $\mathbb{R}^{d_z+d_o}$. By \cite{devore1993besov}, there exists a continuous extension operator $\mathcal{E}: MW^{s_o,s_z}_2([0,1]^{d_o+d_z})\to MW^{s_o,s_z}_2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o + d_z})$ such that $\|\mathcal{E}[f]\|_{MW^{s_o,s_z}_2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o+d_z})} \leq C' \|f\|_{MW^{s_o,s_z}_2([0,1]^{d_o+d_z})}$ holds for some universal constant $C^\prime$.
nodes.name: Known result and extension
nodes.statement_short: Result on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and an extension operator.

nodes.statement: Hence, for $f\in MW^{s_o,s_z}_2([0,1]^{d_o+d_z})$, we thus have $\|f\|_{L^{\infty}([0,1]^{d_o+d_z})}\leq \|\mathcal{E}[f]\|_{L^\infty}(\mathbb{R}^{d_o+d_z}) \leq C \|\mathcal{E}[f]\|_{MW^{s_o,s_z}_2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o+d_z})} \leq C' \|f\|_{MW^{s_o,s_z}_2([0,1]^{d_o+d_z})}$, for some universal constants $C,C'>0$.
nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement_short: Restrict the bound to the cube.

nodes.statement:
We prove in Eq.~\eqref{eq:Tf_Tf_aux} in \Cref{sec:approx_main} that $
\left\| T f_\ast -  T f_{\mathrm{aux}} \right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} \leq n^{-\frac{\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}$, so we continue from above to obtain, with $P^n$-probability $\geq 1 - 2e^{-\tau}$, 
\begin{align} (\ast) \lesssim \gamma_x^{-d_x\eta_0} (\log n)^{\frac{d_x\eta_0}{2}} \left\| T \left[\hat{f}_{\lambda}\right] -  T f_{\ast} \right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} + n^{-\frac{\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1 - \eta_0}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}} (\log n)^{\frac{d_x\eta_0}{2}} .
\end{align}
Note the last term of Eq.~\eqref{eq:unprojected_amplified_projected_example} is subsumed by the second term above since $\eta_0 \geq \eta_1$.

nodes.statement: We are going to apply \citet[Theorem 3]{JMLR:v25:23-1663} to obtain the desired result. To this end, we need to verify the assumptions (EVD) and (SRC) made in \cite{JMLR:v25:23-1663}. Note that we let the assumption (EMB) of \cite{JMLR:v25:23-1663} be trivially verified with $\alpha = 1$, as we prove in \Cref{prop:F_ast_sobolev} that $F_{\ast} \in [\mathcal{G}]^\beta$ with $\beta > 1$, therefore $\beta + p > 1 + p > 1 = \alpha$ falls in Case 2 of Theorem 3 of \cite{JMLR:v25:23-1663}.
nodes.name: Plan
nodes.statement_short: Verify (EVD) and (SRC) for Li et al. Theorem 3.

nodes.name: Verification of (EVD)
nodes.statement_short: Eigendecay of the tensor-product covariance.

nodes.statement:
\underline{\textit{Verification of (SRC)}}
Let $\beta = m^{\dag}$. By the definition of vector-valued interpolation space in \cite{JMLR:v25:23-1663}[Definition 2] and the Assumption that $P_{ZO}$ is equivalent to the Lebesgue measure, we have that
\begin{align*}
    [\mathcal{G}]^{\beta} &\cong \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x} \otimes [L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}), \mathcal{H}_Z \otimes \mathcal{H}_O]_{\beta, 2} \\
    &\stackrel{(a)}{\cong} \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x} \otimes [L^2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}), W^{t_z}_2(\mathcal{Z}) \otimes W^{t_o}_2(\mathcal{O})]_{\beta, 2} \\
    &\stackrel{(b)}{\cong} \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x} \otimes W^{t_z \beta}_2(\mathcal{Z}) \otimes W^{t_o \beta}_2(\mathcal{O})\\
    &\stackrel{(\ast)}{\supseteq} \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}\otimes W^{m_z}_2(\mathcal{Z}) \otimes W^{m_o}_2(\mathcal{O})\\
    &\stackrel{(c)}{\cong} \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}\otimes MW^{m_z,m_o}_{2}(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O};\mathbb{R})\\
    &\stackrel{(d)}{\cong} MW^{m_z,m_o}_{2}(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O};\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}).
\end{align*}
where in $(a)$ we use Corollary 10.13 and Theorem 10.46 of \cite{wendland2004scattered}, in $(b)$ we use \Cref{lem:tensor_interpolation}, in $(c)$ we use proposition 3.1 of \cite{SICKEL2009748}, which shows $MW^{m_z, m_o}_2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}) \cong W^{m_z}_2(\mathcal{Z}) \otimes W^{m_o}_2(\mathcal{O})$, and in $(d)$ we use \Cref{lem:vv_mss}. Furthermore, the inclusion in $(\ast)$ is a continuous embedding. We show in \Cref{prop:F_ast_sobolev} that under \Cref{assn: technical}, $\|F_{\ast}\|_{MW^{m_z,m_o}_{2}(\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O};\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x})}$ is bounded by a constant. Hence we deduce from the above embedding that 
\begin{align} F_{\ast}\in [\mathcal{G}]^{\beta}, \quad \beta = m^{\dag} = \frac{m_z}{t_z} \wedge \frac{m_o}{t_o}.
\end{align}
Hence $\|F_{\ast}\|_{[\mathcal{G}]^{\beta}} \leq C$ for some constant $C>0$. Hence $F_{\ast}$ satisfies (SRC) in \cite{JMLR:v25:23-1663} with $\beta=m^{\dag}$.
nodes.name: Verification of (SRC)
nodes.statement_short: $F_*$ lies in $[\mathcal{G}]^{m^\dagger}$ via mixed Sobolev regularity.

nodes.statement_short: Obtain the $L^2$ and $\mathcal{G}$-norm rates.

nodes.statement:
Next, notice that
\begin{align*}
    &\quad \left\|\phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x) p(\mathbf x \mid \cdot,\cdot)\right\|_{MW^{m_z, m_o}_2(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O};\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x})}^2 \\
    &= \sum_{|\boldsymbol\alpha|\leq m_z} \sum_{|\boldsymbol\beta|\leq m_o} \int_{\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}} \left\|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z} \partial^{\boldsymbol\beta}_{\mathbf o} \left(\phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x) p(\mathbf x\mid \mathbf z, \mathbf o) \right) \right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}}^2 \;\mathrm{d} \mathbf z \;\mathrm{d} \mathbf o \\
    &= \sum_{|\boldsymbol\alpha|\leq m_z} \sum_{|\boldsymbol\beta|\leq m_o} \int_{\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}} \left\|\phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x) \partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z} \partial^{\boldsymbol\beta}_{\mathbf o} p(\mathbf x \mid \mathbf z, \mathbf o) \right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}}^2 \;\mathrm{d} \mathbf z \;\mathrm{d} \mathbf o \\
    &\leq \sum_{|\boldsymbol\alpha|\leq m_z} \sum_{|\boldsymbol\beta|\leq m_o} \int_{\mathcal{Z}\times \mathcal{O}} \left|\partial^{\boldsymbol\alpha}_{\mathbf z} \partial^{\boldsymbol\beta}_{\mathbf o} p(\mathbf x| \mathbf z, \mathbf o) \right|^2 \;\mathrm{d} \mathbf z \;\mathrm{d} \mathbf o \\ 
    &\leq \binom{m_z + d_z -1}{d_z -1} \binom{m_o + d_o-1}{d_o -1} \rho^2  .
\end{align*}
In the last step, $\binom{m_z + d_z -1}{d_z -1}$ shows up as the evaluation of $\sum_{|\boldsymbol\alpha| \leq m_z} 1$.

nodes.statement:
Secondly, we verify the assumptions of \citet[Theorem 7.23]{steinwart2008support}. By \citet[Example 7.3]{steinwart2008support}, the \emph{supremum bound} is satisfied for $B = 4M_n^2$ and the \emph{variance bound} is satisfied for $V = 16M_n^2$ and $\nu=1$. 
Define $D_{ZO}=\{\mathbf z_i, \mathbf o_i\}_{i=1}^n$ and $L^2(D_{ZO})$ as the $L^2$ space with respect to the empirical data measure $D_{ZO}$.

nodes.statement:
For the third term, we note that $(\forall \mathbf o\in \mathbb{R}^{d_o})$, 
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{F}[\left((f_{\ast} - f_{\ast , \mathrm{low}}) \ast K_{\gamma_o} - (f_{\ast} - f_{\ast, \mathrm{low}}) \ast K_{\gamma_o} \ast K_{\gamma_x}\right)(\cdot, \mathbf o)] 
\end{align*}
is supported on the complement of $\{\mathbf x: \|\mathbf x\| \leq \gamma_x^{-1}\}$ (see~Eq. \eqref{eq:f_ast_low}). Thus it follows from \Cref{ass:T_contractivity} that
\begin{align*}
    &\quad \left\| T\left((f_{\ast} - f_{\ast , \mathrm{low}}) \ast K_{\gamma_o} - (f_{\ast} - f_{\ast, \mathrm{low}}) \ast K_{\gamma_o} \ast K_{\gamma_x}\right) \right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})}^2 \\
    &\leq \gamma_x^{2d_x\eta_1}\left\| (f_{\ast} - f_{\ast , \mathrm{low}}) \ast K_{\gamma_o} - (f_{\ast} - f_{\ast, \mathrm{low}}) \ast K_{\gamma_o} \ast K_{\gamma_x} \right\|_{L^2(P_{XO})}^2\\
    &\stackrel{(i)}{\lesssim} \gamma_x^{2d_x\eta_1+ 2s_x}\cdot \left|(f_{\ast} - f_{\ast , \mathrm{low}}) \ast K_{\gamma_o}\right|^2_{B^{s_x,s_o}_{2,q}(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})}\\
    &\stackrel{(ii)}{\leq} \gamma_x^{2d_x\eta_1+ 2s_x}\cdot \left|f_{\ast} \ast K_{\gamma_o}\right|^2_{B^{s_x,s_o}_{2,q}(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})}\\
    &\stackrel{(iii)}{\leq} \gamma_x^{2d_x\eta_1+ 2s_x}\cdot \left|f_{\ast}\right|^2_{B^{s_x,s_o}_{2,q}(\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o})} \|K_{\gamma_o}\|^2_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\\
    &\stackrel{(iv)}{\lesssim} n^{-\frac{2(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}. 
\end{align*}
In the above derivations, $(i)$ follows by using \Cref{lem:hang_prop_3} for $\boldsymbol{\gamma} = (\underbrace{\gamma_x,\dots,\gamma_x}_{d_x},\underbrace{0,\dots,0}_{d_o})$ and the Assumption that $P_{XO}$ admits a bounded density, $(ii)$ follows from the proof of \Cref{lem:new_besov_mask}, $(iii)$ follows from \Cref{lem:besov_young}, and $(iv)$ follows by the fact that $\|K_{\gamma_o}\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R})}= 1$ \citep[Section 4.1.2]{Giné_Nickl_2015} and \Cref{ass:f_ast} in the main text.

\begin{align} \lambda \| f_\lambda\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}^2 + \left\|T\left(f_{\ast} - \left[f_{\lambda}\right]\right)\right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})}^2 \leq n^{-\frac{2(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}{1+(2+\frac{d_o}{s_o})(\frac{s_x}{d_x}+\eta_1)}}.

The proof concludes here.

From Eq. \eqref{eq:error_translate} and \cite{fischer2020sobolev}[Lemma 12], we have
\begin{align} \left\| [\bar{h}_{\lambda}] - [h_{\lambda}]\right\|_{L^2(P_{ZO})} \leq \left\|C_{FO}^{\frac{1}{2}}\left(\bar{h}_{\lambda} - h_{\lambda}\right)\right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{FO}} =: (\ast)
\end{align}
Next, we will upper bound $(\ast)$ using Theorem 16 from \citet{fischer2020sobolev}. To apply this result, we must verify the underlying assumptions and control the auxiliary quantities specified in Theorem 16 from \citet{fischer2020sobolev}.

nodes.statement:
First, we are going to verify the (MOM) condition.
By \Cref{ass:subgaussian}, we know that
\begin{align*}
    \int_{\mathbb{R}}\left|y- (T f_\ast)(\mathbf z, \mathbf o)\right|^m p(y \mid \mathbf z, \mathbf o)dy &= \mathbb{E}\left[|\upsilon|^m\mid Z=\mathbf z,O=\mathbf o\right] \\
    &\leq (\sqrt{2}C\sigma)^m(m/2)^{\frac{m}{2}} \leq \frac{1}{2}(2C\sigma)^mm! 
\end{align*}
by \citet[Eq. (2.15)]{vershynin2018high}, for some universal constant $C>0$. Hence the (MOM) condition of \cite{fischer2020sobolev} is satisfied.
