nodes.statement: We adapt the proof of \cite{aubin2011applied}[Theorem 12.7.2]. Let $f\in W^{m}(\Omega_1, W^{p}(\Omega_2,\mathcal{H}))$. Then $f\in L^2(\Omega_1, W^p(\Omega_2,\mathcal{H}))$ such that $\partial_1^{\alpha}f\in L^2(\Omega_1, W^p(\Omega_2,\mathcal{H}))$ for $|\alpha|\leq m$.
nodes.name: Setup
nodes.statement_short: Take $f$ in the iterated Sobolev space.

nodes.statement:
As explained in \cite{Hytönen2016AnalysisBanachSpaces}[Definition 2.5.1], to say that $\partial_1^{\alpha}f\in L^2(\Omega_1, W^p(\Omega_2,\mathcal{H}))$ is equivalent to saying that for every $\phi \in C^{\infty}_{c}(\Omega_1)$, we have
    \begin{align} \int_{\Omega_1}f(x,\cdot)\partial^{\alpha}_{1}\phi(x)\;\mathrm{d}x = (-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_{\Omega_1}(\partial^{\alpha}_{1}f)(x,\cdot)\phi(x)\;\mathrm{d}x
    \end{align}
    belongs to $W^p(\Omega_2,\mathcal{H})$.
nodes.name: Weak derivative characterisation
nodes.statement_short: Vector-valued weak derivatives tested against $C_c^\infty$ functions.

nodes.statement: But this exactly says that $f\in MW^{m,p}(\Omega_1\times \Omega_2,\mathcal{H})$. Thus the first isometric isomorphism is proved. The second isomorphism is proved by two successive applications of \citet[Theorem 12.7.1]{aubin2011applied}, namely the fact that the Hilbert-space valued Sobolev space $W^m(\Omega,\mathcal{H})$ is isometrically isomorphic to the Hilbertian tensor product $W^m(\Omega)\otimes \mathcal{H}$.
nodes.name: Identify spaces
nodes.statement_short: This is the definition of $MW^{m,p}$; tensor identification gives the rest.

nodes.name: Factorise S_0 and bound term (A)
nodes.statement_short: Bound $S_0$ by a product of terms (A),(B),(C); bound (A) by Fischer–Steinwart Lemma 17.

nodes.statement:
\underline{Upper bound for term $(C)$}. Define
\begin{align*}
    \tilde{\boldsymbol{\Phi}}_{\hat{F}O} : \mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o} \to \mathbb{R}^{n} &= \left[ \left( \hat{F}_\xi(\mathbf z_1, \mathbf o_1) \otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_1) \right) ,\dots, \left( \hat{F}_\xi(\mathbf z_n, \mathbf o_n) \otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_n) \right) \right]^{\ast}\\
    \tilde{\boldsymbol{\Phi}}_{FO} : \mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o} \to \mathbb{R}^{n} &= \left[\left( F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_1, \mathbf o_1)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_1) \right),\dots, \left( F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_n, \mathbf o_n) \otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_1) \right) \right]^{\ast} .
\end{align*}
An immediate consequence is that $V \tilde{\boldsymbol{\Phi}}_{\hat{F}O}^\ast = \boldsymbol{\Phi}_{\hat{F}O}^\ast$ and $V \tilde{\boldsymbol{\Phi}}_{FO}^\ast = \boldsymbol{\Phi}_{FO}^\ast$ for $V$ defined following \Cref{defi:H_F} and $\boldsymbol{\Phi}_{\hat{F}O}, \boldsymbol{\Phi}_{FO}$ defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:bPhi_FO}.
Hence, we have
\begin{align*}
    (C) &= \left\|\hat{C}_{\hat{F}O}-\hat{C}_{FO}\right\| \\
    &= \left\| \frac{1}{n} \boldsymbol{\Phi}_{F O}^{\ast} \boldsymbol{\Phi}_{F O} - \frac{1}{n} \boldsymbol{\Phi}_{\hat{F} O}^\ast \boldsymbol{\Phi}_{\hat{F} O} \right\| \\
    &= \left\| \frac{1}{n} V \tilde{\boldsymbol{\Phi}}_{F O}^{\ast} \tilde{\boldsymbol{\Phi}}_{F O} V^\ast - \frac{1}{n} V \tilde{\boldsymbol{\Phi}}_{\hat{F} O}^\ast \tilde{\boldsymbol{\Phi}}_{\hat{F} O} V^\ast \right\| \\
    &= \left\| \frac{1}{n} \tilde{\boldsymbol{\Phi}}_{F O}^{\ast} \tilde{\boldsymbol{\Phi}}_{F O} - \frac{1}{n} \tilde{\boldsymbol{\Phi}}_{\hat{F} O}^\ast \tilde{\boldsymbol{\Phi}}_{\hat{F} O} \right\|\\ 
    &= \left\|\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(\hat{F}_\xi(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)\right) \otimes \left(\hat{F}_\xi(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)\right) \right. \\
    &\quad\quad \left. - \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} \left(F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i)\otimes\phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)\right)\otimes \left(F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i)\otimes\phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)\right) \right\|.
\end{align*}
The second last equality holds because $V:\mathcal{H}_{XO} \to \mathcal{H}_{FO}$ is an isometry. 
We start with the following decomposition
\begin{align*}
    &\left(\hat{F}_\xi(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)\right)\otimes\left(\hat{F}_\xi(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)\right) \\
    & \quad\quad - \left(F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i)\otimes\phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)\right) \otimes \left(F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i)\otimes\phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)\right) \\
    =&\left(\left(\hat{F}_\xi(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) - F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) \right) \otimes\phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)\right) \otimes \left(\left(\hat{F}_\xi(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) - F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) \right)\otimes\phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)\right) \\ &+ \left(\left(\hat{F}_\xi(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) - F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) \right)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)\right)\otimes (F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)) \\
    &+ (F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)) \otimes \left(\left(\hat{F}_\xi(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) - F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) \right)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)\right).
\end{align*}
Thus we have
\begin{small}
\begin{align*}
    (C)&\leq \left\|\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(\left(\hat{F}_\xi(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) - F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) \right)\otimes\phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)\right) \otimes \left(\left(\hat{F}_\xi(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) - F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) \right)\otimes\phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)\right) \right\| \nonumber \\
    &+ 2\left\|\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(\left(\hat{F}_\xi(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) - F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) \right)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)\right)\otimes (F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i))\right\|\nonumber\\
    &\leq \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} \left\| \left(\left(\hat{F}_\xi(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) - F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) \right)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)\right) \otimes \left(\left(\hat{F}_\xi(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) - F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) \right)\otimes\phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)\right) \right\| \nonumber \\
    &+ 2\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} \left\|\left(\left(\hat{F}_\xi(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) - F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) \right)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i)\right)\otimes (F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i)\otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i))\right\|\nonumber  \\
    &\leq \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left\|\hat{F}_\xi (\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) -F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) \right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}}^2  + \frac{2}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left\|\hat{F}_\xi (\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i) -F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i)\right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}},
\end{align*}
\end{small}
where in the last step we use $\|a\otimes b\|_{H_1\otimes H_2} = \|a\|_{H_1}\|b\|_{H_2}$ for $a\in H_1$, $b\in H_2$ for Hilbert spaces  $H_1,H_2$~\citep[Eq. (3)]{gretton2005measuring}, $\|\phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i) \otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o_i) \| \leq 1$ and $\|F_{\ast}(\mathbf z_i,\mathbf o_i)\|_{\mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}} \leq 1$. 
Note that the last line is exactly analyzed in the proof of \citet[Lemma 7]{meunier2024nonparametricinstrumentalregressionkernel}. Their analysis employs a Hoeffding's concentration bounds with respect to Stage 2 samples $\mathcal{D}_2$, and \emph{conditioned} on Stage 1 samples $\mathcal{D}_1$ to show that, conditioned on $\mathcal{D}_1$, 
\begin{align} (C) \leq J_0 \left( \sqrt{\frac{\tau}{n}}\left\|F_{\ast}-\hat{F}_{\xi}\right\|_{\mathcal{G}}+\left\|F_*-[\hat{F}_{\xi}] \right\|_{L^2\left(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}; \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}\right)}  \right)
\end{align}
with $P^n$-probability $\geq 1 - 4e^{-\tau}$, under the assumptions that 
\begin{align} \left\|F_\ast -[\hat{F}_{\xi}] \right\|_{L^2\left(\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{O}; \mathcal{H}_{X,\gamma_x}\right)} \vee \left\|F_\ast -\hat{F}_{\xi}\right\|_{\mathcal{G}} \leq 1.
\end{align} 
We note that the independence of $\mathcal{D}_1$ and $\mathcal{D}_2$ is implicitly used in this step to ensure that $\mathcal{D}_2$ remains i.i.d. after conditioning on $\mathcal{D}_1$. $J_0$ is a constant independent of $n,\tilde{n}$.
Denote as $\mathfrak{D}$ the $P^{\tilde{n}}$-probabilistic event that the bounds in \Cref{prop:cme_rate} hold (which has $P^{\tilde{n}}$-probability $\geq 1 - 4e^{-\tau}$). Under this event $\mathfrak{D}$ along with the fact that $\tilde{n}$ satisfies Eq. \eqref{eq:m_sufficient_large}, Eq.~\eqref{eq:F_ast_F_xi_small_1} is satisfied so Eq.~\eqref{eq:bound_C} holds. Additionally, from Eq.~\eqref{eq:bound_C}, a sufficient condition for $(C)\leq \frac{1}{6n}$ is given by $
\tilde{n} \geq (6 J J_0 \tau^{\frac{3}{2}} n)^{2\frac{m^{\dag}+d^{\dag}/2+\zeta}{m^{\dag}}} \vee (36 J^2 J_0^2 \tau^2 n)^{\frac{m^{\dag} + d^{\dag}/2 + \zeta}{m^{\dag} - 1}}$, which is satisfied since $\tilde{n}$ satisfies Eq. \eqref{eq:m_sufficient_large}.
nodes.name: Term (C)
nodes.statement_short: Hoeffding bounds conditional on Stage I and CME rates.

nodes.name: Term (B)
nodes.statement_short: Rudi et al. Proposition 7.

nodes.statement: Under the event $\mathfrak{D}$, the upper bounds $(A)\leq 2$, $(B)\leq 6/5$, $(C)\leq \frac{1}{6}$ hold simultaneously with $P^{n}$-probability $\geq 1 - 6e^{-\tau}$. Since $\mathfrak{D}$ holds with $P^{\tilde{n}}$-probability $\geq 1 - 4e^{-\tau}$, by independence of Stage 1 and Stage 2 samples (which is a consequence of the sample splitting strategy), we have that the above upper bounds hold simultaneously with $P^{n+\tilde{n}}$-probability $\geq \left(1 - 6e^{-\tau}\right)\left(1 - 4e^{-\tau}\right) \geq 1 - 10e^{-\tau}$.
nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement_short: Combine the three bounds.

nodes.statement:
Suppose $\left( \mu_{1, i} \right)_{i \in \mathbb{N}^+}$ (resp. $\left( \mu_{2, j} \right)_{j \in \mathbb{N}^+}$) are the eigenvalues of $\Sigma_1$ (resp. $\Sigma_2$) with corresponding eigenfunctions $\left( q_{1, i} \right)_{i \in \mathbb{N}^+}$ (resp. $\left( q_{2, j} \right)_{j \in \mathbb{N}^+}$). 
By definition of operator tensor product, we have
\begin{align*}
    \left( \Sigma_1 \otimes \Sigma_2 \right) (q_{1, i} \otimes q_{2, j} ) = \left( \Sigma_1  q_{1, i} \right) \otimes \left( \Sigma_2 q_{2, j} \right) = \mu_{1, i} \mu_{2, j} (q_{1, i} \otimes q_{2, j} ) .
\end{align*}
Therefore, for any $i \in \mathbb{N}^+, j \in \mathbb{N}^+$ we obtain that $\mu_{1, i} \cdot \mu_{2, j}$ is the eigenvalue of $\Sigma_1 \otimes_{op} \Sigma_2$ with corresponding eigenfunction $q_{1, i} \otimes q_{2, j}$. 
Therefore the eigenvalues of $\Sigma_1 \otimes_{op} \Sigma_2$ equal the tensor product of two sequences $(\mu_{1, i})_{i\in \mathbb{N}^+}$ and $(\mu_{2, j})_{j \in \mathbb{N}^+}$.
nodes.name: Eigenvalues of tensor products
nodes.statement_short: Eigenvalues of $\Sigma_1\otimes\Sigma_2$ are products.

nodes.statement:
Without loss of generality, we assume $p_1 \leq p_2$ so that $\mu_{1, i} \leq \mu_{2, i}$ for $i$ large enough. 
Denote $(\sigma_n)_{n\in \mathbb{N}^+}$ as the tensor product of two sequences $(\mu_{2, i})_{i\in \mathbb{N}^+}$ and $(\mu_{2, j})_{j \in \mathbb{N}^+}$ rearranged in a non-increasing order. Hence, we have $\lambda_{n}(\Sigma_1 \otimes \Sigma_2) \leq \sigma_n$.
From \cite{krieg2018tensor}, we have 
\begin{align*}
    \sigma_n \leq n^{- 1/p_2} (\log n)^{1/p_2} \leq n^{- 1/p_2 + \zeta},
\end{align*}
for any $\zeta > 0$.
It concludes the proof.
nodes.name: Krieg bound
nodes.statement_short: Bound the reordered product sequence.

nodes.name: Write as finite differences
nodes.statement_short: Express $K_\gamma*f-f$ via $r$-th differences.

nodes.statement:
Next, since $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} $ = 1, we have that
\begin{align*}
    &\quad \left\| [K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}} * f] - f\right\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})}^2 \\
    &= \int_{\mathcal{X}} \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \left(\sum_{j=0}^r \binom{r}{j}(-1)^{1-j} f( \mathbf{x} + j \boldsymbol{h} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma} )\right) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} \right)^2 \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \\
    &= \int_{\mathcal{X}} \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \left(\sum_{j=0}^r \binom{r}{j}(-1)^{2r + 1 - j} f( \mathbf{x} + j \boldsymbol{h} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma} )\right) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} \right)^2 \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \\
    &= \int_{\mathcal{X}} \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} (-1)^{r+1} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \Delta_{\boldsymbol{h} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}}^r f(\mathbf x) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} \right)^2 \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x .
\end{align*}
Where the last step follows from the definition of modulus of smoothness in Eq. \eqref{eq:module_smoothness}.
nodes.name: Integral representation
nodes.statement_short: Use the Gaussian integral normalisation.

nodes.name: Cauchy–Schwarz
nodes.statement_short: Move to the modulus of smoothness.

nodes.statement:
Define $N := \min\{\gamma_1^{-s_1}, \ldots, \gamma_d^{-s_d}\}$.
Since $f \in B_{2,q}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathcal{X})$, 
we have
\begin{align*}
    &|f|_{B_{2,q}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathcal{X})} \geq |f|_{B_{2,\infty}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathcal{X})} := \sup_{t} \left( t^{-1} \omega_{r, 2} \left(f, t^{\frac{1}{s_1}}, \ldots, t^{\frac{1}{s_d}}, \mathcal{X} \right) \right) \\
    &\geq \left( \left( \sum_{i=1}^d h_i^{s_i} \right) N^{-1} \right)^{-1} \omega_{r, 2} \left(f, \left( \sum_{i=1}^d h_i^{s_i} \right)^{\frac{1}{s_1}} N^{-\frac{1}{s_1}}, \ldots, \left( \sum_{i=1}^d h_i^{s_i} \right)^{\frac{1}{s_d}} N^{-\frac{1}{s_d}}, \mathcal{X} \right) \\
    &\geq N \left( \sum_{i=1}^d h_i^{s_i} \right)^{-1} \omega_{r, 2} \left(f, h_1 \gamma_1, \ldots, h_d \gamma_d, \mathcal{X} \right) \\
    &\geq N \left( \sum_{i=1}^d h_i^{s_i} \right)^{-1} \left\| \Delta_{\boldsymbol{h} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}}^r f \right\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})} .
\end{align*}
As a result, we have $ \| \Delta_{\boldsymbol{h} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}}^r f\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})} \leq |f|_{B_{2,q}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathcal{X})} N^{-1} (\sum_{i=1}^d h_i^{s_i})$.
Plugging the above back to Eq.~\eqref{eq:K_gamma_f_f_diff_Delta}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
    \left\| K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}} * f - f\right\|_{L^2(\mathcal{X})}^2 &\leq \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \left( |f|_{B_{2,q}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathcal{X})} N^{-1} \left(\sum_{i=1}^d h_i^{s_i}\right) \right)^2 \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} \\
    &\leq |f|_{B_{2,q}^{\boldsymbol{s}}(\mathcal{X})}^2 N^{-2} d \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac{d}{2}} \exp\left( -2 \| \boldsymbol{h}\|^2 \right) \left(\sum_{i=1}^d h_i^{2 s_i}\right) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{h} .
\end{align*}
nodes.name: Besov bound on differences
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\|\Delta^r f\|$ by the Besov seminorm.

nodes.name: Gaussian moments
nodes.statement_short: Sum Gaussian moments.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement_short: Combine.

nodes.statement: Following the same arguments in the proof of proposition 4 in \cite{hang2021optimal}, we have $ K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}} \ast f \in \mathcal{H}_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}$.
nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the unit-bandwidth case.

nodes.statement:
For a function $f:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}$, we define $\tau_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}f(\mathbf x) = f(\boldsymbol{\gamma}\odot \mathbf x)$. We have, for all $\mathbf x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, 
\begin{align*}
    \tau_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}\left(K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}} \ast f\right)(\mathbf x) &= \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}} \left( \boldsymbol{\gamma} \odot \mathbf x - \boldsymbol{t} \right) f(\boldsymbol{t}) \;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t} \\
    &=  \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}K_{\mathbf{1}}\left(\frac{\boldsymbol{\gamma} \odot \mathbf x - \boldsymbol{t}}{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}\right)\left(\prod_{i=1}^{d}\frac{1}{\gamma_i} \right)f(\boldsymbol{t})\;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}\\
    &= \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}K_{\mathbf{1}}\left(\mathbf x - \frac{\boldsymbol{t}}{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}\right)\left(\prod_{i=1}^{d}\frac{1}{\gamma_i} \right)f\left( \boldsymbol{t} \right)\;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}\\
    &= \int_{\mathbb{R}^d}K_{\mathbf{1}}\left(\mathbf x - \boldsymbol{t}\right)f\left(\boldsymbol{t} \odot\boldsymbol{\gamma}\right)\;\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{t}\\
    &= (K_{\mathbf{1}}\ast (\tau_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}f))(\mathbf x) .
\end{align*}
nodes.name: Rescaling
nodes.statement_short: Rescale $f$ and rewrite the convolution.

nodes.statement:
Proposition 4.37 of \cite{steinwart2008support} can be generalized to anisotropic case which shows that for any  
$f \in \mathcal{H}_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}$, $\tau_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}} f \in \mathcal{H}_{X, \mathbf{1}}$ and 
$\tau_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}: \mathcal{H}_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}} \to \mathcal{H}_{X, \mathbf{1}}$ is an isometric isomorphism.  Hence we have
\begin{align*}
    \left\|K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}\ast f \right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}} &= \left\|\tau_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}\left(K_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}\ast f\right) \right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{X, \mathbf{1}}}\\
    &= \left\|K_{\mathbf{1}}\ast (\tau_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}f)\right\|_{\mathcal{H}_{X, \mathbf{1}}}\\
    &\leq \pi^{-\frac{d}{4}}(2^r - 1) \|\tau_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)}\\
    &= \left(\prod_{i=1}^{d}\gamma_i^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right)\pi^{-\frac{d}{4}}(2^r - 1)\|f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)},
\end{align*}
where the second last inequality follows from \cite{eberts2013optimal}[Theorem 2.3] setting $\gamma=1$.

nodes.statement:
We define $\phi_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}(\mathbf x) = \exp(-\sum_{j=1}^{d} \gamma_j^{-2} x_j^2)$.
Then
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{F}[\phi_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}](\boldsymbol{\omega}) &= \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\phi_{X,\boldsymbol{\gamma}}(\mathbf x)\exp(-i\langle \mathbf x, \boldsymbol{\omega}\rangle) \mathrm{d}\mathbf x \\
    &= \left(\prod_{i=1}^{d}\gamma_i\right) \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\phi_{X,1}(\mathbf x)\exp\left(-i\left\langle \mathbf x, \boldsymbol{\omega} \odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}\right\rangle\right)\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\\
    &= \pi^{d/2} \left(\prod_{i=1}^{d}\gamma_i\right)\exp\left(-\frac{\|\boldsymbol{\omega}\odot \boldsymbol{\gamma}\|_{2}^{2}}{4}\right)
\end{align*}
where the last step follows from \cite{wendland2004scattered}[Theorem 5.20].

By definition of the operator norm, we have
\begin{align*}
    &\quad \|C_{FO}\|^2 \\
    &= \sup_{\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} = 1}\left\langle f, \mathbb{E}[(F_{\ast}(Z, O) \otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(O))\otimes (F_{\ast}(Z, O) \otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(O))]f\right\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}\\ 
    =& \sup_{\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} = 1} \mathbb{E} \left[ \left(\mathbb{E}[f(X,O)|Z,O] \right)^2 \right]\\
    \geq & \sup_{\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} = 1} \left( \mathbb{E}_{ZO \sim P_{ZO}} \left[\mathbb{E}[f(X,O)|Z,O]\right] \right)^2\\
    =&  \sup_{\|f\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}} = 1} \mathbb{E}[f(X,O)]^2 \\
    =& \|\mu_{XO}\|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}^2 , 
\end{align*}
where $\mu_{XO} := \mathbb{E}_{P_{XO}}[\phi_{\gamma_x}(X) \otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(O)]$.

nodes.statement:
Notice that 
\begin{align*}
    &\|\mu_{XO} \|_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}^2\\ &= \left\langle \iint_{\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{X}} \phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x) \otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o) p_{XO}(\mathbf x,\mathbf o)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o, \right. \\
    &\qquad\qquad \left. \iint_{\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{X}} \phi_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x') \otimes \phi_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o') p_{XO}(\mathbf x',\mathbf o')\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x'\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o'\right\rangle_{\mathcal{H}_{\gamma_x,\gamma_o}}\\
    &= \iint_{\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{X}} \iint_{\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{X}} K_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o,\mathbf o') K_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x,\mathbf x')p_{XO}(\mathbf x,\mathbf o) p_{XO}(\mathbf x', \mathbf o')\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x'\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o'\\
    &\stackrel{(a)}{\geq} a^2\int_{[1/4,3/4]^{d_o}}\int_{[1/4,3/4]^{d_o}} K_{\gamma_o}(\mathbf o,\mathbf o')\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o'\int_{[1/4,3/4]^{d_x}}\int_{[1/4,3/4]^{d_x}} K_{\gamma_x}(\mathbf x,\mathbf x') \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x'\\
    &\stackrel{(b)} = a^2 \left(\gamma_x \sqrt{\pi} \left[\frac{\mathrm{erf}\left(\frac{1}{2\gamma_x}\right)}{2} + \gamma_x\frac{\exp\left(-\frac{1}{4\gamma_x^2}\right)-1}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right]\right)^{d_x} \\
    &\qquad\qquad \cdot \left(\gamma_o \sqrt{\pi} \left[\frac{\mathrm{erf}\left(\frac{1}{2\gamma_o}\right)}{2} + \gamma_o\frac{\exp\left(-\frac{1}{4\gamma_o^2}\right)-1}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right]\right)^{d_o},
\end{align*}
where $\mathrm{erf}(x) := \frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi}}\int^{x}_{-x}\exp\left(-t^2\right)\;\mathrm{d}t$
is the standard error function of normal distribution. Step $(a)$ holds by \Cref{assn: technical} and step $(b)$ holds by using \Cref{lem:gaussian_kernel_embedding}.

nodes.statement:
Notice that 
    \begin{align*}
        &\int_{1/4}^{3/4} \exp \left(-\frac{(x_i - x_i')^2}{\gamma^2} \right) \;\mathrm{d} x_i\\ &= \gamma \int_{(1/4-x_i^\prime) / \gamma}^{(3/4-x_i^\prime) / \gamma}  \exp(-x^2) \;\mathrm{d}x \\
        &=\gamma \int^{(3/4-x_i')/\gamma}_{-\infty}\exp(-x^2) \;\mathrm{d}x - \gamma \int^{(1/4-x_i')/\gamma}_{-\infty}\exp(-x^2)\;\mathrm{d}x\\
        &=\gamma\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}\left(1+\mathrm{erf}\left(\frac{3/4-x_i'}{\gamma}\right)\right) - \gamma\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}\left(1-\mathrm{erf}\left(\frac{x_i'-1/4}{\gamma}\right)\right)\\
        &=\gamma\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}\left(\mathrm{erf}\left(\frac{3/4-x_i'}{\gamma}\right) + \mathrm{erf}\left(\frac{x_i'-1/4}{\gamma}\right)\right).
    \end{align*}

nodes.statement:
Since $\Delta^{r}_{\mathbf{h}} = (\tau_{\mathbf{h}} - \mathrm{id})^r$, we have $\Delta^{r}_{\mathbf{h}}(K\ast f) = K\ast \left(\Delta^{r}_{\mathbf{h}}f\right)$. Thus for any $r > \max\{s_1, \ldots, s_d\}$, 
\begin{align}
    \omega_{r,2}\left(K\ast f, t^{\frac{1}{s_1}},\dots, t^{\frac{1}{s_d}}, \mathbb{R}^d\right) &= \sup_{0<|h_i|<t^{\frac{1}{s_i}}}\left\|\Delta^{r}_{\mathbf{h}}(K\ast f)\right\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)}\nonumber\\
    &= \sup_{0<|h_i|<t^{\frac{1}{s_i}}}\left\|K\ast \Delta^{r}_{\mathbf{h}}( f)\right\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)}\nonumber\\
    &\stackrel{(i)}{\leq} \sup_{0<|h_i|< t^{\frac{1}{s_i}}}\|K\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)} \left\|\Delta^{r}_{\mathbf{h}}f\right\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)} \\
    &= \|K\|_{L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)}\omega_{r,2}\left(f,t^{\frac{1}{s_1}},\dots, t^{\frac{1}{s_d}},\mathbb{R}^d\right), \nonumber
\end{align}
where we use Young's convolution inequality in $(i)$.

nodes.statement_short: Bound the $x$-direction modulus.

nodes.statement:
We first bound $(I)$.  We have
\begin{align*}
    \tau_{\mathbf{h}}(K\ast g)(\mathbf x) = (K\ast g)(\mathbf x + \mathbf{h}) = (K \ast (\tau_{\mathbf{h}}g))(\mathbf x) .
\end{align*}
We thus have $\Delta^{r}_{\mathbf{h}}(K\ast g) = K\ast \left(\Delta^{r}_{\mathbf{h}}g\right)$. Thus we have
\begin{align*}
    &\omega^{\mathbf x}_{r,2}(f, t^{1/s_x},\dots, t^{1/s_x})\\
    =&\sup_{|h_i|\leq t^{1/s_x}}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_o}}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x}} \left|\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o} ( (\Delta_{\boldsymbol{h}}^r M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}) \ast \mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}])(\mathbf x) M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}(\mathbf o)\right|^2 \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    =&\sup_{|h_i|\leq t^{1/s_x}}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o'}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x}} ( (\Delta_{\boldsymbol{h}}^r M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}) \ast \mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}])(\mathbf x) \overline{( (\Delta_{\boldsymbol{h}}^r M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}) \ast \mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o')}])(\mathbf x)} \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x  \right. \\
    &\qquad \left. \cdot \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_o}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}(\mathbf o) M_{k,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o'}(\mathbf o) \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    \stackrel{(a)}{=}&\sup_{|h_i|\leq t^{1/s_x}}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|\mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}]\ast (\Delta^r_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}})\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}^2 \|M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    \stackrel{(b)}{\leq}& \sup_{|h_i|\leq t^{1/s_x}}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|\Delta^r_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}^2 \|M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    =& \left(\sup_{|h_i|\leq t^{1/s_x}}\|\Delta^r_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\right)\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    \stackrel{(c)}{\leq} & \sup_{|h_i|\leq t^{1/s_x}}\|\Delta^r_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\\
    =& \omega_{r,2}(M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}},t^{1/s_x},\dots,t^{1/s_x}).
\end{align*}
In the above derivations,
\begin{itemize}
nodes.name: Derivation for (I)
nodes.statement_short: Convolution commutes with differences; disjoint $o$-supports.

nodes.statement: we use $\mathrm{supp}(M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o})\cap \mathrm{supp}(M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}) = \emptyset$ if ${\boldsymbol\ell}_o\neq {\boldsymbol\ell}_o'$ in $(a)$,
nodes.name: Disjoint supports
nodes.statement_short: Justification (a).

nodes.name: Plancherel indicator inequality
nodes.statement_short: Justification (b).

nodes.name: Sum over o-splines and conclude (I)
nodes.statement_short: Justification and resulting bound on (I).

nodes.statement:
Now we bound $(II)$. Notice that
\begin{align*}
    &\omega^{\mathbf o}_{r,2}(f,t^{1/s_o},\dots, t^{1/s_o})\\
    \stackrel{(a)}{\lesssim} &\omega_{s_o,2}^{\mathbf o}(f,t^{1/s_o},\dots, t^{1/s_o})\\
    \stackrel{(b)}{\lesssim} &2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\omega^{\mathbf o}_{s_o,2}\left(f,2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{1/s_o},\dots, 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{1/s_o}\right)\\
    =&2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}} \sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{1/s_o}}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}} \left|\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}(\mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}] \ast M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}})(\mathbf x) \cdot (\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}} M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o})(\mathbf o) \right|^2 \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    =&2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}} t^{1/s_o}}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o'}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x}} (\mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}]\ast M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}})(\mathbf x) \cdot \overline{\mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o^\prime)}]\ast M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}}(\mathbf x)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \right. \\
    &\qquad \left. \cdot \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_o}}(\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o})(\mathbf o)\cdot (\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o'})(\mathbf o) \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    \stackrel{(c)}{=}& 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{1/s_o}}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|\mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}] \ast M_{k,{\boldsymbol\ell}_x}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})} \cdot \|\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    \stackrel{(d)}{\leq} & 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{1/s_o}}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})} \cdot \|\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    = & 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\left( \sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}} t^{1/s_o}}\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    \stackrel{(e)}{=} & 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\left( \sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}} t^{1/s_o}}\left\|\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\left(\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\right)\right\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    \stackrel{(f)}{=} & 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\left( \sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}} t^{1/s_o}}\left\|\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\right)\right\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    = &2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\left(\omega_{s_o,2}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o},2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{\frac{1}{s_o}},\dots,2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{\frac{1}{s_o}}\right)^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}.
\end{align*}
In the above derivations,
\begin{itemize}
    \item we use $r=s_x\vee s_o \geq s_o$ and Minkowski's inequality in $(a)$ (this is also sometimes referred to as the reverse Marchaud inequality, see \cite{KOLOMOITSEV2020105423}[Property 8]),
    \item we use \cite{leisner_nonlinear_wavelet_approximation_2003}[Theorem 2.1.1] in $(b)$, which we can apply since $2^{\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}\geq 1$,
    \item we deduce from Eq. \eqref{eq:Bspline_main} that
    \begin{align*}
        \mathrm{supp}(M_{k{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}) = \bigtimes_{j=1}^{d_o}\left[2^{-\left\lfloor\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}\right\rfloor}\ell_{o,j} , 2^{-\left\lfloor\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}\right\rfloor}(\mathfrak{m}+\ell_{o,j})\right].
    \end{align*}
    We also see that 
    \begin{align*}
        \mathrm{supp}(\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}) = \bigtimes_{j=1}^{d_o}\left[2^{-\left\lfloor\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}\right\rfloor}\ell_{o,j} - s_oh_j , 2^{-\left\lfloor\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}\right\rfloor}(\mathfrak{m}+\ell_{o,j})\right]
    \end{align*}
    We deduce that a sufficient condition to guarantee that \begin{align*}
        \mathrm{supp}\left(\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\right)\cap\mathrm{supp}\left(\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o'}\right) = \emptyset
    \end{align*}
    if ${\boldsymbol\ell}_o\neq {\boldsymbol\ell}_o'$ is given by 
    \begin{align*}
        (\forall j=1,\dots,d_o),\; |h_j|\leq 2^{-\left\lfloor\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}\right\rfloor}\frac{\mathfrak{m}-1}{s_o}.
    \end{align*}
    Since $\mathfrak{m}-1\geq s_o$ by choice, and we have for all $i = 1,\dots, d_o$, $|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{1/s_o}\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}$, this sufficient condition is satisfied. Hence 
    \begin{align} \left\langle \Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o},\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o'}\right\rangle_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})} = \left\|\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\right\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}^2\delta_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o'}. 
    \end{align}
    \item we use Plancherel's Theorem in $(d)$, in a similar way as in Eq. \eqref{eq:plancherel_indicator_inequality},
    \item we use Eq. \eqref{eq:lemedotfiveortho} again for step $(e)$,
    \item we use linearity of $\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}$ for step $(f)$. 
\end{itemize}
Thus we have shown that, for $q=\infty$, 
\begin{align*}
    (II) &\lesssim 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\sup_{t>0}\left[t^{-1}\omega_{s_o,2}\left(\sum_
    {{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}, 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{\frac{1}{s_o}},\dots, 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{\frac{1}{s_o}}\right)\right]\\
    &\lesssim \|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\sup_{t>0}\left[\left(t2^{-\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\right)^{-1}\omega_{s_o,2}\left(\sum_
    {{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}, 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{\frac{1}{s_o}},\dots, 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{\frac{1}{s_o}}\right)\right]\\
    &\stackrel{(a)}{\lesssim} \|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\sup_{t>0}\left[\int_{t}^{\infty} w^{-s_o}\omega_{s_o+1}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}, w,\dots,w\right)\;\frac{\mathrm{d}w}{w}\right]\\
    &\leq \|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\int_{0}^{\infty} w^{-s_o}\omega_{s_o+1}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}, w,\dots,w\right)\;\frac{\mathrm{d}w}{w}\\
    &\asymp \|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\left\|\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\right\|_{B^{s_o}_{2,1}(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\\
    &\stackrel{(b)}{\lesssim} 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}d_x}{2s_x}}2^{\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}(s_o - d_o/2)}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}1\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    &\lesssim 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}\left(1 - \frac{d_x}{2s_x}\right)},
\end{align*}
where we use the Marchaud-type estimate \citet[Chapter 2, Eq. (10.3)]{devore1993constructive} in $(a)$, we use the sequential Besov norm equivalence \cite{devore1988interpolation}[Theorem 5.1] (see also \citep[Theorem 3.3.3]{leisner_nonlinear_wavelet_approximation_2003}) in $(b)$.
nodes.name: Bound term (II)
nodes.statement_short: Bound the $o$-direction modulus.

nodes.statement:
Now we bound $(II)$. Notice that
\begin{align*}
    &\omega^{\mathbf o}_{r,2}(f,t^{1/s_o},\dots, t^{1/s_o})\\
    \stackrel{(a)}{\lesssim} &\omega_{s_o,2}^{\mathbf o}(f,t^{1/s_o},\dots, t^{1/s_o})\\
    \stackrel{(b)}{\lesssim} &2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\omega^{\mathbf o}_{s_o,2}\left(f,2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{1/s_o},\dots, 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{1/s_o}\right)\\
    =&2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}} \sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{1/s_o}}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_o}} \left|\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}(\mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}] \ast M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}})(\mathbf x) \cdot (\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}} M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o})(\mathbf o) \right|^2 \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    =&2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}} t^{1/s_o}}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o'}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_x}} (\mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}]\ast M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}})(\mathbf x) \cdot \overline{\mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o^\prime)}]\ast M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}}(\mathbf x)\;\mathrm{d}\mathbf x \right. \\
    &\qquad \left. \cdot \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_o}}(\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o})(\mathbf o)\cdot (\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{k,{\boldsymbol\ell}_o'})(\mathbf o) \;\mathrm{d}\mathbf o\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    \stackrel{(c)}{=}& 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{1/s_o}}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|\mathcal{F}^{-1}[\mathbbm{1}_{S({\boldsymbol\ell}_o)}] \ast M_{k,{\boldsymbol\ell}_x}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})} \cdot \|\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    \stackrel{(d)}{\leq} & 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{1/s_o}}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})} \cdot \|\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    = & 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\left( \sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}} t^{1/s_o}}\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    \stackrel{(e)}{=} & 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\left( \sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}} t^{1/s_o}}\left\|\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\left(\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\right)\right\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    \stackrel{(f)}{=} & 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\left( \sup_{|h_i|\leq 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}} t^{1/s_o}}\left\|\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\right)\right\|^2_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    = &2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\left(\omega_{s_o,2}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o},2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{\frac{1}{s_o}},\dots,2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{\frac{1}{s_o}}\right)^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}.
\end{align*}
In the above derivations,
\begin{itemize}
nodes.name: Derivation for (II)
nodes.statement_short: Chain of inequalities for (II).

nodes.statement: we use $r=s_x\vee s_o \geq s_o$ and Minkowski's inequality in $(a)$ (this is also sometimes referred to as the reverse Marchaud inequality, see \cite{KOLOMOITSEV2020105423}[Property 8]),
nodes.name: Minkowski / reverse Marchaud
nodes.statement_short: Justification (a).

nodes.statement: we use \cite{leisner_nonlinear_wavelet_approximation_2003}[Theorem 2.1.1] in $(b)$, which we can apply since $2^{\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}\geq 1$,
nodes.name: Leisner Theorem 2.1.1
nodes.statement_short: Justification (b).

nodes.name: Support analysis
nodes.statement_short: Justification (c): disjointness of shifted supports.

nodes.statement: we use Plancherel's Theorem in $(d)$, in a similar way as in Eq. \eqref{eq:plancherel_indicator_inequality},
nodes.name: Plancherel
nodes.statement_short: Justification (d).

nodes.statement: we use Eq. \eqref{eq:lemedotfiveortho} again for step $(e)$,
nodes.name: Orthogonality again
nodes.statement_short: Justification (e).

nodes.statement:
we use linearity of $\Delta^{s_o}_{\boldsymbol{h}}$ for step $(f)$. 
\end{itemize}
Thus we have shown that, for $q=\infty$, 
\begin{align*}
    (II) &\lesssim 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\sup_{t>0}\left[t^{-1}\omega_{s_o,2}\left(\sum_
    {{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}, 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{\frac{1}{s_o}},\dots, 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{\frac{1}{s_o}}\right)\right]\\
    &\lesssim \|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\sup_{t>0}\left[\left(t2^{-\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}\right)^{-1}\omega_{s_o,2}\left(\sum_
    {{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}, 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{\frac{1}{s_o}},\dots, 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}}t^{\frac{1}{s_o}}\right)\right]\\
    &\stackrel{(a)}{\lesssim} \|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\sup_{t>0}\left[\int_{t}^{\infty} w^{-s_o}\omega_{s_o+1}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}, w,\dots,w\right)\;\frac{\mathrm{d}w}{w}\right]\\
    &\leq \|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\int_{0}^{\infty} w^{-s_o}\omega_{s_o+1}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}, w,\dots,w\right)\;\frac{\mathrm{d}w}{w}\\
    &\asymp \|M_{k,-\frac{\mathfrak{m}}{2}}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^{d_x})}\left\|\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}M_{\mathfrak{K},{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}\right\|_{B^{s_o}_{2,1}(\mathbb{R}^{d_o})}\\
    &\stackrel{(b)}{\lesssim} 2^{-\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}d_x}{2s_x}}2^{\frac{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}}{s_o}(s_o - d_o/2)}\left(\sum_{{\boldsymbol\ell}_o}1\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\\
    &\lesssim 2^{\mathfrak{K}\underline{s}\left(1 - \frac{d_x}{2s_x}\right)},
\end{align*}
where we use the Marchaud-type estimate \citet[Chapter 2, Eq. (10.3)]{devore1993constructive} in $(a)$, we use the sequential Besov norm equivalence \cite{devore1988interpolation}[Theorem 5.1] (see also \citep[Theorem 3.3.3]{leisner_nonlinear_wavelet_approximation_2003}) in $(b)$.
nodes.name: Linearity and conclude (II)
nodes.statement_short: Justification (f) and the bound on (II).
